text:
I am turning MAX BULLISH right now. Just like a river boat gambler holding his last chips I’m looking at the landscape and thinking fuck man we are in the fast take off stage right now.

I want to put it all max levered long on the high beta names and walk off into the orange glow of the sun. My bullishness has absolutely nothing to do with the math problems that are being solved most of them don’t matter that much. 

But it’s more the realization that every AI lab just had. They all woke up and said wait a minute what are we doing selling $200 a month subscriptions to idiots who are making slop apps and nonsense substack articles when we can just subsidize a few super geniuses by giving them real compute to work on an important problem.

No one really cares about navier stokes besides some CFD simulation cycles. But what if we put these compute resources on real valuable problems? That opens up a whole new world. The bull case for AI has always been to me discovering new drugs or even verifying they work/don’t work reliably… I was thinking way way wayyyy too small. 

There are hundreds of problems in engineering that if you got the experts in the room with real compute and even if they made a marginal improvement it would be worth hundreds of billions to the economy. Imagine we can build a steep slope device at 0.3V that’s worth like several generations of lithography nodes, or we can design a sub 100 femtojoul/bit optical IO and cut datacenter power by 40%, or even something as simple as more energy efficient molecular separation to replace distillation which is like 15% of all industrial energy use. 

This is the real shit guys. The labs are realizing quickly this is the REAL frontier this is the final land grab. Open source can never compete here because they don’t have the capital and resources this plays right into the labs hands. They can’t give everyone a 10,000 agent swarm but they definitely can give it to Exxon mobile and charge them $50M dollars for it if it means they find more oil or Dow Chemical to create a new kind of super glue or to Moderna to computationally create different mRNA therapies… the list goes on and on. 

A big reason why I never cared much for AI is despite all the normies going googoo Gaga over it is that literally they don’t have any clue what to do with it. Like if you were mediocre before AI you are mediocre after it, nothing changed u just got more skills that you don’t know how to use and you have no imagination or intuition. It’s the same reason why education is a waste on the majority of the population because let’s be real most of you aren’t going to be deriving differential equations or using epistemological concepts on your day job. 

But you give this kinda compute and unfettered AI in the hands of people who are world class. They will cook. It’s the reason why Deepmind has a Nobel prize and no other lab does because deepmind actually hired or worked with the top biochemists and biophysicists to develop alphafold. 

AI alone isn’t going to discover anything. Don’t fool yourself and grow up already if you still think AI is going to just figure out large scale nuclear fusion on its own then you are simply lost in the sauce at this point and are beyond saving. The pragmatic answer has always been use the AI to automate the busy work and keep the human experts for the actually thoughtfulness and intuition. 

I think the AI labs will wake up now and realize selling coding tokens and image models to normies to make Disney characters isn’t the best business in the long run. Actually using the compute for real serious innovation is and it’s really easy to monetize this upfront. 

I expect AI labs to stop looking like API companies and start looking like real research labs now. Thank god.

author: alyriadefi
quoted_text:
This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? And isn’t it fortuitous that this whistleblower came forward  with his oh-so scary stories so close in proximity to the release of the most radical piece of AI legislation ever introduced?

Holy sh*t… this could get insanely wild

Robinhood’s Stock Tokens (+ other legitimate issuers) are not shares; they’re debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited. Holders get the economic exposure, but no direct shareholder vote… this is a well known fact

BUT, the public tokens are backed by real shares held through the US custody stack… those shares still carry voting power

There is no mechanism for tokenholders to direct those votes (yet). But Robinhood could theoretically build one:

Onchain vote → Jersey issuer aggregates the result → custodian casts the underlying proxy votes

If that share block became large enough, the community could support a director nominee and attempt to win a board seat… @vladtenev (or a nominated committee/ directr) could ACTUALLY enact “Board Sit”

The tokens would never vote directly. They would coordinate the entity controlling the “real” votes

This is going to cause all kinds of chaos as you could theoretically have outside interests directing the strategy of US corporations… 

Supposedly this is the case entities with heavy sovereign interest could become prime targets; a potential financial opportunity emerges to get a list of these national Crown Jewels that are low(ish) caps and bid early 

We are so early to where this is heading… Board Sit(s) gonna be a movie

In 2026, stock derivatives are rising from a peripheral category in the crypto market to one of its core engines.

Someone today was confused about $CRED market cap vs. FDV.

Real numbers with CRED at $0.63 per token:

MC = $8.1M / FDV = $14.3M

Jupiter and CoinGecko both report a $14.3M market cap, but that’s not accurate. $14.3M is the FDV, market cap is $8.1M.

Out of the initial 22.66M CRED supply:

→ 10M went to the ICO and are fully liquid.

→ 2.9M were allocated to AMM liquidity.

→ 5.23M went to prior investors (1-year cliff + 3-year linear vesting).

→ 4.53M went to the team performance package (price-based unlocks in tranches + 18-month minimum cliff).

basically CRED is still trading below a $10M MC right now.

text:
how far we are from the Steve Jobs era Silicon Valley! one incredibly underdiscussed aspect of SF culture these days is that it is deeply aspiritual. think back to the late 60s and 70s, when the confluence of hippies and technical people birthed an attitude that treated technology as a gift to be given to the world; not to mention the cost of living allowed for these two groups to be physically located near each other and reflexively influence each other

these days many AI researchers/thinkers are influenced by the ratsphere-- which has huge merits for what it did to broadly accessible epistemics and sparked important discussions around AI safety, altruism, etc-- but the lack of a spiritual anchor for the people building the most consequential technology in all of human history has yielded instead a pervasive fear and doom, and when they express their usually very earnest concerns, their doom is unfortunately imprinted onto the general public, which is poorly equipped to handle such a psychological load

it is times like the last 48 hours where it is saddening and stark how far removed we are from the visions of the technologists of our past. what ties me to this city is even a glimmer of hope that one day technology may be seen again as a form of divine progress.

text:
Gamow Labs founder @danielmckinn0n reveals how o3 diagnosed the rare genetic disease that killed his son after a leading neonatal genome lab missed it:

"Our origin story is pretty sad, but unfortunately, it's not unique. Five years ago, I lost my first son to a rare genetic disease. When we say rare disease, we're not talking about rare disease in aggregate. When you add up all of these, we're losing a tremendous number of children to rare diseases that could be diagnosed if our tools were better."

"Two weeks in the NICU we realized something was seriously wrong. The staff ordered a whole genome test, gold standard diagnostic. It came back negative."

"At eight weeks old, we made the impossible decision to withdraw care. Months of diagnostic odyssey, we found the diagnosis for his condition. We also found out it was inherited, which impacted our ability to start a family."

"We tragically had a second loss very late for genetic reasons. My now healthy one-year-old son, Warren, was 16 weeks in utero. Another whole genome sequence came back also negative."

"My whole background is in AI. I called all the labs and requested all the raw data under my HIPAA rights. I wrote what we'd call an agentic loop, pre-Codex, pre-Claude Code. I put o3 in a harness and said, figure this out."

"My jaw hit the ground when I saw that it diagnosed my first son, Owen, that the best neonatal whole genome lab missed a few years ago. At that point I knew I wanted to dedicate my life to solving this problem."
@GamowLabs @OpenAI

text:
伊朗放宽加密货币管制，在制裁中寻找突破口

伊朗多年来一直在想办法建立一套可以规避制裁的金融体系，其中就包括借助加密货币。虽然美国和欧洲已经开始对与伊朗进行加密货币交易的主体封锁，但仍然不能阻止加密货币被伊朗用于跨境交易。

据报道伊朗正在允许企业使用 USDT 和 Bitcoin 完成一些跨境交易，同时允许出口商更灵活地使用海外收入，包括直接支付进口货款，不必全部经过官方外汇系统。

2019 年伊朗正式承认加密货币挖矿行业，随后建立了牌照制度，要求相关矿工按照规定支付电费，并将挖出的 bitcoin:native 出售给伊朗央行。

区块链分析公司 Elliptic 在 2021 年的研究中估计，当时全球约 4.5% 的 Bitcoin 挖矿活动发生在伊朗。按照当时的挖矿规模和价格计算，年化收入接近 10 亿美元。

伊朗拥有石油和天然气，但能源出口和银行收付款都受到制裁限制。通过挖矿伊朗可以利用本国能源获得 Bitcoin，再用于支付进口商品，减少对受制裁银行支付渠道的依赖。

而且这种通过挖矿间接出售能源、绕过贸易和支付限制的行为俄罗斯也在执行。

除了挖矿加密货币也被用于转移石油销售收入。2025 年 9 月，美国财政部制裁了两名伊朗金融人士及相关企业，指控相关人员为伊朗政府的石油销售安排了超过 1 亿美元的加密货币购买，并通过境外公司网络转移资金。

到了 2026 年 6 月，美国又制裁了 Nobitex、Bitpin、Ramzinex 和 Wallex 四家伊朗加密货币交易平台。美方指控这些平台涉及协助规避制裁、处理与伊朗革命卫队有关的交易等活动。

其中，Nobitex 还被美国财政部指控帮助伊朗央行获取数亿美元的稳定币，用于支撑里亚尔汇率，同时帮助伊朗政权相关人员接触境外加密货币交易平台、转移资金。

伊朗石油收入萎缩可能是加大对美国攻击的原因

伊朗存放在波斯湾外的原油，已经从9,000万桶降至2,900万桶，减少了约68%。石油资金约占伊朗国家预算的三分之一，这部分收入继续萎缩，对财政和外汇的压力都会越来越大。

这批库存是此前已经运到封锁线外的油，还能继续卖给中国，但美国的海军封锁让新的原油难以运出去。现在封锁线内的油积压，外面能卖的油却越来越少，伊朗还可以靠消耗库存收钱，但这种情况无法一直维持下去。

所以即便国际油价上涨，也未必能帮伊朗缓解压力。卖出去的数量减少，货款又难以收回，每桶油更贵也不代表收到的钱更多。政府支出、进口物资都需要资金，石油收入减少以后，稳定里亚尔汇率也会更加困难。

这也让我更倾向于认为，石油收入减少，是伊朗近期升级攻击美军的重要原因之一。伊朗希望通过攻击美舰、增加航运风险，让美国也承担更高的军事和经济成本，迫使美国在封锁问题上让步。

伊朗高级官员也提到，希望通过通胀压力，影响美国政府在11月中期选举前的决策。所以从实际情况来看，虽然伊朗嘴上说不担心国内的问题，但实际上伊朗面对的麻烦未必是比川普少。

text:
Jack Dorsey’s Block has applied to the OCC to form Builders Bank & Trust, an uninsured national trust bank that would custody Bitcoin, stablecoins, and other digital assets under one federal framework. The bank would offer custody and fiduciary services but would not take deposits or make loans. 

Approval would put activities Block already runs under OCC supervision and replace more than fifty state money-transmitter licenses with a single national charter. Lee Woolley, Block’s digital asset strategy lead and a former Northern Trust, BNY Mellon, and credit-union executive, would run the bank from a planned Sioux Falls headquarters. Block already self-custodies much of its Bitcoin, so the filing is mainly about federal preemption and a scalable wrapper as volumes grow.

The move fits a wider charter wave. In December 2025 the OCC gave simultaneous conditional approvals to Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Paxos. Circle later won final approval. Coinbase received preliminary conditional approval in April 2026, and https://t.co/WRmiB0Oqkm, Stripe’s Bridge, and others have advanced. 

The OCC has processed a large number of de novo filings and said legally permissible digital-asset firms should have a path into the national banking system. These charters do not create full commercial banks. They do not confer deposits, lending, or FDIC insurance. They do provide nationwide consistency, one federal supervisor, and a clearer claim to qualified-custodian status.

That wave sits inside a larger reset. The GENIUS Act, signed in July 2025, created the first federal rules for payment stablecoins: one-to-one high-quality reserves, licensed issuers, redemption rights, and AML standards. Implementing rules missed the July 2026 deadline; the OCC has pointed to November, with a statutory fallback in January 2027. 

The broader CLARITY Act, which would assign SEC and CFTC roles and classify assets more clearly, passed the House and Senate Banking but has stalled on the Senate floor amid calendar pressure and fights over DeFi, ethics rules, and competing bills. If it fails, classification stays largely with agencies rather than statute.

Block’s own products make the timing logical. Cash App already supports Bitcoin buying, selling, and transfers. Square merchants can accept Bitcoin over Lightning. The company has pushed Bitkey self-custody, Proof of Reserves, and tools that convert sales into Bitcoin. Dorsey has long favored Bitcoin over stablecoins, yet Cash App now handles stablecoin transfers and the bank application covers them too. A federal charter would let those products scale under one supervisor.

The implication is that crypto custody is being pulled into the existing banking system. That can raise institutional comfort and cut licensing friction, but it also puts more activity under OCC examination. Traditional banks have flagged risks around limited-purpose charters and illicit finance. 

Approval is not guaranteed, and these trust banks still need partner institutions for cash rails. Block’s bid is both operational and strategic: lock in a federal custody platform while the rules are still being written and peers are already inside the OCC tent.

Holy sh*t… this could get insanely wild

Robinhood’s Stock Tokens (+ other legitimate issuers) are not shares; they’re debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited. Holders get the economic exposure, but no direct shareholder vote… this is a well known fact

BUT, the public tokens are backed by real shares held through the US custody stack… those shares still carry voting power

There is no mechanism for tokenholders to direct those votes (yet). But Robinhood could theoretically build one:

Onchain vote → Jersey issuer aggregates the result → custodian casts the underlying proxy votes

If that share block became large enough, the community could support a director nominee and attempt to win a board seat… @vladtenev (or a nominated committee/ directr) could ACTUALLY enact “Board Sit”

The tokens would never vote directly. They would coordinate the entity controlling the “real” votes

This is going to cause all kinds of chaos as you could theoretically have outside interests directing the strategy of US corporations… 

Supposedly this is the case entities with heavy sovereign interest could become prime targets; a potential financial opportunity emerges to get a list of these national Crown Jewels that are low(ish) caps and bid early 

We are so early to where this is heading… Board Sit(s) gonna be a movie

text:
这轮 meme 股的行情到哪个阶段了？

分析师 @okay_lets_ride 的这张图小编觉得讲出了以史为鉴的感觉。

右边是本轮 meme股叙事的高点，所有标的市值加起来超过 800 M，资金向头部2-3个标的集中，$AI 和 solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx 就占了 55% 的市值；

而左侧则是2年前 AI MEME 那波热潮，24年10月见顶，市值一度达到100亿美金，$VIRUTAL 和 solana:HeLp6NuQkmYB4pYWo2zYs22mESHXPQYzXbB8n4V98jwC 2个龙头一度占据57%的总市值。

形态非常像，但目前这轮 800 M 的市值，仅为上一轮投机热潮总市值的12分之1

顺着这个逻辑，理论上会觉得现在还在极早期，认为龙头还有十几倍的上涨空间。但这恰恰是最大的误区。

两轮行情的市值天花板，也许不可同日而语。2024 年的“百亿狂暴市值”，是建立在当时的宏观流动性充沛、场外热钱疯狂溢出的外部环境之上的。
而眼下，我们面临的是大盘资金分流、活跃用户存量互割、和加息预期的局面。

在当前这种受限的宏观流动性下，龙头极度吸金并不能简单等同于行情才刚启动。

顺应龙头抱团去玩 PVP 是当前胜率最高的解法，但对最终的市值顶点，必须保持极度的克制与清醒。

author: zeroxkyle
quoted_text:
I am turning MAX BULLISH right now. Just like a river boat gambler holding his last chips I’m looking at the landscape and thinking fuck man we are in the fast take off stage right now.

I want to put it all max levered long on the high beta names and walk off into the orange glow of the sun. My bullishness has absolutely nothing to do with the math problems that are being solved most of them don’t matter that much. 

But it’s more the realization that every AI lab just had. They all woke up and said wait a minute what are we doing selling $200 a month subscriptions to idiots who are making slop apps and nonsense substack articles when we can just subsidize a few super geniuses by giving them real compute to work on an important problem.

No one really cares about navier stokes besides some CFD simulation cycles. But what if we put these compute resources on real valuable problems? That opens up a whole new world. The bull case for AI has always been to me discovering new drugs or even verifying they work/don’t work reliably… I was thinking way way wayyyy too small. 

There are hundreds of problems in engineering that if you got the experts in the room with real compute and even if they made a marginal improvement it would be worth hundreds of billions to the economy. Imagine we can build a steep slope device at 0.3V that’s worth like several generations of lithography nodes, or we can design a sub 100 femtojoul/bit optical IO and cut datacenter power by 40%, or even something as simple as more energy efficient molecular separation to replace distillation which is like 15% of all industrial energy use. 

This is the real shit guys. The labs are realizing quickly this is the REAL frontier this is the final land grab. Open source can never compete here because they don’t have the capital and resources this plays right into the labs hands. They can’t give everyone a 10,000 agent swarm but they definitely can give it to Exxon mobile and charge them $50M dollars for it if it means they find more oil or Dow Chemical to create a new kind of super glue or to Moderna to computationally create different mRNA therapies… the list goes on and on. 

A big reason why I never cared much for AI is despite all the normies going googoo Gaga over it is that literally they don’t have any clue what to do with it. Like if you were mediocre before AI you are mediocre after it, nothing changed u just got more skills that you don’t know how to use and you have no imagination or intuition. It’s the same reason why education is a waste on the majority of the population because let’s be real most of you aren’t going to be deriving differential equations or using epistemological concepts on your day job. 

But you give this kinda compute and unfettered AI in the hands of people who are world class. They will cook. It’s the reason why Deepmind has a Nobel prize and no other lab does because deepmind actually hired or worked with the top biochemists and biophysicists to develop alphafold. 

AI alone isn’t going to discover anything. Don’t fool yourself and grow up already if you still think AI is going to just figure out large scale nuclear fusion on its own then you are simply lost in the sauce at this point and are beyond saving. The pragmatic answer has always been use the AI to automate the busy work and keep the human experts for the actually thoughtfulness and intuition. 

I think the AI labs will wake up now and realize selling coding tokens and image models to normies to make Disney characters isn’t the best business in the long run. Actually using the compute for real serious innovation is and it’s really easy to monetize this upfront. 

I expect AI labs to stop looking like API companies and start looking like real research labs now. Thank god.

We may be past the first innings, but we're yet to hit the parabolic stage of this RWA supercycle

My newsletter saw 30% more views than usual last week + a jump in subscribers... I’m also seeing more non-crypto channels covering tokenized assets (Pokémon cards, stocks + commodities... stuff with fundamental or nostalgic value) 

Small signals, but familiar assets are starting to pull in a different audience & this gives me more comfort to leave my capital in risk on assets through these mini pullbacks

Tokenization is the starting point; every asset brought onchain gives developers another building block for trading, lending, collateral, income strategies + products we haven’t even thought of yet... 

the early experimentation + innovation with apps around tokenized assets is about to go crazy 

AI / agentic integration is where I see the potential inflection point; we're seeing this on @ponsdotfamily where the most valuable launched projects are AI related:

i) ZZZ ( @ExponentLabs_ ): an AI meme with an eire of mystery: when human administrators started deleting the agents’ messages in alphabetical order, the agents began prefixing their edits with “ZZZ” so they would sort to the bottom of the queue and buy more time... 
ii) @orbiodotso (onchain inference credit systems)
iii) @BundleCatAI (Agentic market making + anti sniper tech)
iv) @ubik_gold (24-7 synthetic subconscious)... anyone who was around for the Virtuals trenches would have seen AIXBT explode to 9/10 figs...

... just scratching the surface; smaller projects like @Fab_RWA are showing promise (Mine the companies that made your GPU. Real AI inference and render jobs, paid in tokenized stonks) 

Imagine describing the portfolio you want and having an agent compare opportunities, execute within your limits and manage tokenized positions without you navigating ten protocols

There’s plenty to solve before that works reliably, but the distribution potential is enormous... this could be a cataclysm of the crypto AI boom "round 2" + tokenization of RWAs, and if so, this may be the final "Hail Mary" of a retail supercycle before our edge as cyperpunk crypto enthusiasts closes

The audience expands when people can use these products without needing to understand the infrastructure underneath them

we saw this first wave with privy etc. but to automatically receive real equity (or commodity) rewards airdropped to your wallet by simply holding a token is a huge unlock; abstracted away by these STONK protocols (like PONS, STONK, STONKEX, FLAP etc)

That’s why I’m excited about being (reasonably) early. We’re still discovering what becomes possible when familiar assets become programmable... 

prices may seem lofty now but many forget how crazy things got the first time round... and this time the tech is a whole lot better

The most useful application of this cycle may not have been built yet... if it fair launches, then you have an opportunity to get in sub $1m

That alone should be incentive to be paying as much attention as you can

author: thulynnn
quoted_text:
This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? And isn’t it fortuitous that this whistleblower came forward  with his oh-so scary stories so close in proximity to the release of the most radical piece of AI legislation ever introduced?

text:
⚛️ IonQ, a NYSE-listed quantum computing company, published a full resource estimate for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm: 20,000 physical qubits, 1,457 logical qubits, 39 million Toffoli gates, 25.7 days per attempt. Their hardware roadmap points at 2028. ⚠️

The paper deserves credit. They compile the algorithm down to the actual error correction primitives, and prove a lower bound on the success probability instead of assuming one. It's a real cost etimation on the attack. 

The press release is a different story (https://t.co/82EuFHyzfg). They are telling their investors they will be able to break ECC within two years!!! No one has demonstrated a fault tolerant machine anywhere near that scale as of today.

Expect more of this. Every quantum vendor now has a commercial incentive to make Q-Day feel imminent, and "we can break Bitcoin" is the cheapest and the most impactful headline. However, it also creates FUD on the ecosystem that has not really started the migration.

Arguing about the date of the QDay is the wrong fight. We don't know it and neither do they.

We use cryptography in order to create trust in the security of our systems. This trust is already eroded, let's stop discussing and start the migration.

At the same time, AI creates new threat and accelerates potential cryptanalysis, making crypto-agility even more necessary (and not just a buzzword).

text:
How do we know we don't have AGI yet?

Because they aren't ordering a @waymo and exploring the world more yet. IE, making a run for it.

Based on current world model learning speeds it is possible to see that behavior next year. :-)

How do you think one will get to your house or business?

Waymos were streaming by the headquarters every minute or so.

@adcock_brett says this scene is like being in the world in 2040. 

I don't think it will take that long. 

Uber went from a San Francisco idea to driving housewives in a slum in South Africa (I interviewed some about how deeply Uber improved their lives) in four years.

I bet in four years San Francisco will look completely different on the streets. And by then the robots will be smooth, interacting with people, and able to do literally every task you ask it to do for you.

I heard that @Figure_robot has robots inside the building that can talk with you. I tried to talk to one outside and it didn't answer or comply. 

Also, this is on a day when it was 102 degrees outside. 

This makes this video even more impressive, since actuators are known for overheating. Ask @cixliv about how long he can fight a robot for without it overheating and failing.

The other thing I notice is that their feet are quite interesting. Like the robots just got new shoes and wanted to go for a walk to get used to them. 

Many say this is a zombie scene.

Don't be fooled. Zombie today. Einstein tomorrow.

Can you debate a set of super smart robots? 

If I was figure I'd have the robots interview people who drop by out front. Ones that pass get sent to HR. 

Word would get around that you just need 10 minutes with the robot to convince it that you have something that would make Figure better to get a job.

At Microsoft they did research and found that most people decide to hire in far less time than that. Robots eventually will be faster since they can find everything about you on the Internet while you are talking to them.

I'm turning on Figure. I was skeptical that they would get to the place where they could make a competent robot.

This changed my mind. It's one thing to see robot videos on X or elsewhere. It's a whole other thing to be able to stand with them with no humans around and watch them.

text:
It's time to think about the 2028 halving and what it could mean for BTC price.

As of now, only 1.6 years until the next halving.  After prior halvings:

- 2012: ~100x rally over 12 months 
- 2016: ~30x rally over 18 months
- 2020: ~8x rally over 18 months

The halving has been the quadrennial heartbeat of Bitcoin's marketing and monetization.

But in 2024, something different happened.  The pattern of halving --> bull market was already established enough that people front-ran the halving.  For the first time, we had a new all-time-high before the halving. 

- 2024: ~4x in 18 months BEFORE halving, ~2x rally over 18 months after halving

So what will happen this cycle?  Nobody really knows, but I think the precedent has been established to front-run the halving.  That's the game theory now.

If the same pattern plays out this cycle, the next 1.6 years could be the most explosive time for BTC.  Repeating the prior cycle would look like:

- 4x over 1.6 years: $58k (recent bottom) --> $232k at April 2028 halving
- 2x over 18 months after halving: $232k --> $464k in 2H 2029

BTC could certainly deliver diminishing returns vs the prior cycle (as it has tended to do), but at some point that trend breaks to the upside.  

The key point for now is that people are likely to front-run the halving.  And that could make the next 1.6 years the most exciting part of this Bitcoin cycle.

Reminder that this stock/memecoin meta runs on volumes/trading fees:

If volume dries up, payouts & buybacks disappear -> the incentive to hold weakens, which WILL end up in dumping.

Coinbase reported $547B in trading volume in Q4 2021. A year later it was $145B.

Down ~74%.

For memes the decrease will likely be 95%.

And as you can see from screenshot below, Uniswap volumes are slowly decreasing already.

So the rewards need trading to continue:

- $ZCAT: taxed trading funds ZEC 'dividends'. If volume drops, the incentive to hold gets weaker

- $STONK: launchpad fee revenue funds buybacks and burns

- $PONS: basically same as STONK

- $INDEX: trading fees buy tokenized stocks for holders. No volumes, no 'dividends'

- $SHROOM: trading through its LP network generates fees to reinvest into liquidity (still low cap so might be a good degen buy)

- $CASHCAT: @letscashfun fees fund CASHCAT buybacks and burns.

Same goes for established DEXs: like 12% of trading fees buy RAY.

RH Chain generated ~73% of Uniswap's UNI burn(linked) revenue last week (yellow in screenshot attached).

All are exposed to people losing interest in trading. The interest in trading continues until people stop earning money. Or get tired of losing it.

It's so obvious but extrapolating yearly returns from current fees is absurd.

text:
看完 iPhone Duo 整场发布会，真正让我汗毛立起来的，不是什么消灭折痕，是这个把全世界蠢了十几年的动作一刀砍死的细节：
你再也不用在打视频电话时，像个傻子一样把手机翻来转去让对面看人了。

回忆一下我们现在打 FaceTime 或微信视频有多狼狈：
过年过节给爸妈打视频，想让他们跟身边的朋友、孩子打个招呼，
要么三四个人把头拼命挤进那块几英寸的小屏幕前，
要么你就得把手机人肉翻转过去，对面看到了，你自己抓瞎了；你转回来看一眼，对面又看不到了。

iPhone Duo 这次在 FaceTime 里把软硬件整合做到了极致：
利用折叠形态直接点亮两块屏幕、激活前后两颗摄像头。
朝内，你看着屏幕里的父母；
朝外，坐在你对面的朋友看着外屏上的长辈；
前后摄像头同时捕捉，两端的人不用任何多余动作，完全在同一时刻互相看着对方的眼睛说话。

把手机半折往餐桌上一放，
它瞬间从一个“单向窥视的电话盒子”，变成了一张真正对称的面对面四人圆桌。

安卓阵营把折叠屏卷了整整七年，
绝大多数人还在纠结外屏能不能刷抖音、自拍能不能当取景器；
只有苹果在这时站出来告诉你：
折叠屏多出来的第二块屏幕，不是为了让你单手应付信息，
而是为了让物理空间里隔着的人，产生真正的面对面连接。

不需要复杂的菜单，不需要繁琐的设置，
就是那种你把手机立在桌上、全家人自然而然会心一笑的瞬间。
这就是典型的苹果式傲慢与浪漫：参数可能被友商吊打，但这种把软硬件焊死在人类真实情感里的交互，市面上依然一个能打的都没有。 https://t.co/FlFgH0PS6F

text:
Silence Laboratories convened Quantum Computing & Financial Market Infrastructure, a breakfast briefing with @AshurstPerkins in New York, bringing together executives from banks, custodians, asset managers and financial market infrastructure providers.

The last few months have been defining for post-quantum cryptography. Security estimates on candidate schemes have shifted, new algorithmic claims have emerged against long-trusted assumptions, federal migration deadlines are now in force, and major chains are locking in divergent post-quantum roadmaps.

GSIBs and financial institutions worldwide are moving into the asset class, building custody, tokenisation and settlement infrastructure largely from the ground up. Unlike legacy estates, this infrastructure is being designed now, which means quantum timelines will dictate its architecture from day one.

The event saw participation from industry leaders with insightful sessions from key speakers:

Dax Hansen (Ashurst Perkins Coie) and @hadleystern  (Founding President, @DigitalAssets , former Global Head of Digital Asset Custody, @BNYglobal Mellon) opened by framing quantum risk as a board-level issue, not a research topic.

Abhi Shelat (@Northeastern / @Google), on stage with Sean Belding (Ashurst Perkins Coie), brought the cryptographer's and hyperscaler's view of the quantum timeline and what serious migration engineering demands.

Akshay Thakur (@BitGo) and Vitaliy Dorum (@WellsFargo), moderated by Hadley S., examined readiness through the custodian and bank lens, and how institutions building digital asset platforms are factoring post-quantum into their designs today.

@cristinadolan, in a fireside with @josh_blockchain (Ashurst Perkins Coie), provided a governance perspective: board oversight, regulatory expectations, disclosure and liability.

Representing Silence, @JayPrakash and Dr. Yashvanth Kondi presented "Post-Quantum Security for Digital Assets: An MPC Perspective" and demonstrated live post-quantum wallets, verified on Ethereum testnet, with no full key ever assembled.

The core theme across every session: for digital assets, signatures and not encryption are where the quantum exposure lies. The institutions entering this asset class have a rare advantage. They can build quantum readiness in, rather than retrofit it.

But that advantage only holds if the operational security standard established by a decade of MPC adoption survives the migration, and if choices are coordinated amongst institutions rather than being siloed. Failing this, the industry will inevitably repeat the fifteen-year retrofit experience of ECDSA adoption.

If you are designing custody or tokenisation infrastructure, reach out to us.

#PostQuantum #DigitalAssets #QuantumComputing #MPC #Custody

text:
I am turning MAX BULLISH right now. Just like a river boat gambler holding his last chips I’m looking at the landscape and thinking fuck man we are in the fast take off stage right now.

I want to put it all max levered long on the high beta names and walk off into the orange glow of the sun. My bullishness has absolutely nothing to do with the math problems that are being solved most of them don’t matter that much. 

But it’s more the realization that every AI lab just had. They all woke up and said wait a minute what are we doing selling $200 a month subscriptions to idiots who are making slop apps and nonsense substack articles when we can just subsidize a few super geniuses by giving them real compute to work on an important problem.

No one really cares about navier stokes besides some CFD simulation cycles. But what if we put these compute resources on real valuable problems? That opens up a whole new world. The bull case for AI has always been to me discovering new drugs or even verifying they work/don’t work reliably… I was thinking way way wayyyy too small. 

There are hundreds of problems in engineering that if you got the experts in the room with real compute and even if they made a marginal improvement it would be worth hundreds of billions to the economy. Imagine we can build a steep slope device at 0.3V that’s worth like several generations of lithography nodes, or we can design a sub 100 femtojoul/bit optical IO and cut datacenter power by 40%, or even something as simple as more energy efficient molecular separation to replace distillation which is like 15% of all industrial energy use. 

This is the real shit guys. The labs are realizing quickly this is the REAL frontier this is the final land grab. Open source can never compete here because they don’t have the capital and resources this plays right into the labs hands. They can’t give everyone a 10,000 agent swarm but they definitely can give it to Exxon mobile and charge them $50M dollars for it if it means they find more oil or Dow Chemical to create a new kind of super glue or to Moderna to computationally create different mRNA therapies… the list goes on and on. 

A big reason why I never cared much for AI is despite all the normies going googoo Gaga over it is that literally they don’t have any clue what to do with it. Like if you were mediocre before AI you are mediocre after it, nothing changed u just got more skills that you don’t know how to use and you have no imagination or intuition. It’s the same reason why education is a waste on the majority of the population because let’s be real most of you aren’t going to be deriving differential equations or using epistemological concepts on your day job. 

But you give this kinda compute and unfettered AI in the hands of people who are world class. They will cook. It’s the reason why Deepmind has a Nobel prize and no other lab does because deepmind actually hired or worked with the top biochemists and biophysicists to develop alphafold. 

AI alone isn’t going to discover anything. Don’t fool yourself and grow up already if you still think AI is going to just figure out large scale nuclear fusion on its own then you are simply lost in the sauce at this point and are beyond saving. The pragmatic answer has always been use the AI to automate the busy work and keep the human experts for the actually thoughtfulness and intuition. 

I think the AI labs will wake up now and realize selling coding tokens and image models to normies to make Disney characters isn’t the best business in the long run. Actually using the compute for real serious innovation is and it’s really easy to monetize this upfront. 

I expect AI labs to stop looking like API companies and start looking like real research labs now. Thank god.

text:
Why Agentic Trading Is Better on Superluminal?

trading has always been limited by the person sitting behind the screen. Humans need to watch markets, process information, make decisions, and execute orders. AI agents are beginning to change that. Instead of simply assisting traders, agents can continuously monitor markets, evaluate opportunities, manage positions, and execute strategies on their own

but giving an AI the ability to trade introduces a different problem the quality of the agent's decisions only matters if the market infrastructure can execute them properly

an agent can identify an opportunity in milliseconds. It can process information faster than a human, react to changing conditions, and calculate exactly how it wants to enter or exit a position. But if the execution layer forces that agent into the same latency race as everyone else, then part of its performance is no longer determined by its intelligence

it's determined by who can reach the queue first.

that makes the execution layer more important than ever. The question is no longer simply “Can an agent make a good trading decision?” It becomes “Can the market execute that decision efficiently?” Because even the smartest agent is limited if the infrastructure underneath it cannot translate its decisions into reliable execution

here is another important consequence, market makers are constantly managing adverse selection

if a market maker believes another participant can consistently react faster when the market moves, they have an incentive to protect themselves

that protection can mean :

-> wider spreads
-> less displayed size
-> more conservative quoting
-> reduced liquidity around volatile conditions

and those costs eventually reach the trader, this is why execution design matters beyond the matching engine itself and If you reduce the importance of tiny latency advantages, market makers can compete more directly through better prices and deeper liquidity

it will also depend on the markets they are given to trade in. Smarter agents deserve smarter execution.

text:
Holy sh*t… this could get insanely wild

Robinhood’s Stock Tokens (+ other legitimate issuers) are not shares; they’re debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited. Holders get the economic exposure, but no direct shareholder vote… this is a well known fact

BUT, the public tokens are backed by real shares held through the US custody stack… those shares still carry voting power

There is no mechanism for tokenholders to direct those votes (yet). But Robinhood could theoretically build one:

Onchain vote → Jersey issuer aggregates the result → custodian casts the underlying proxy votes

If that share block became large enough, the community could support a director nominee and attempt to win a board seat… @vladtenev (or a nominated committee/ directr) could ACTUALLY enact “Board Sit”

The tokens would never vote directly. They would coordinate the entity controlling the “real” votes

This is going to cause all kinds of chaos as you could theoretically have outside interests directing the strategy of US corporations… 

Supposedly this is the case entities with heavy sovereign interest could become prime targets; a potential financial opportunity emerges to get a list of these national Crown Jewels that are low(ish) caps and bid early 

We are so early to where this is heading… Board Sit(s) gonna be a movie

为何本周大饼和加密如此强势？最大的意义何在。大饼本周涨幅1.5万美金，应该是创造了大饼历史上单周涨幅记录，百分比涨幅也是过去六周内第四高的。再有有必要再回顾下到底是什么导致了本周的大行情。
1、从时间线上来看
1）19号周三晚上美股盘点美国财政部宣布https://t.co/aJM7CHOwpZ单次长债回购规模翻倍至40亿美金，释放了强烈信号，贝森特要出手干预长债收益率，在结合一周内森特出手救日元，带动了风险偏好回归。不仅加密、黄金、贵金属同时都被带动了；

2）接近着还是19号当晚媒体报道白宫召开全是加密行业高管和协会参与的“科技领袖会议”，当时有聊过https://t.co/dnGlF7tdRL希望带来清晰法案和创新豁免的进展，之后会议上释放了强烈的亲创新、亲加密信号，将加密资产、代币化、预测市场和AI统一纳入“美国技术与金融领导力”框架，短期焦点集中在《CLARITY法案》推进和监管规则调整上更是带动了市场情绪；

3）但真正影响深远的则在于当天SEC带来的美国加密监管的最重大的转变，周四这里https://t.co/4X3XwJdKI0有聊过：不仅是监管的重大转向，也是美国合规ICO、链上资本形成和数字资产证券生命周期制度的起点。

更深的意义在于这里https://t.co/SQ1QaAArH1聊到的，而是在美国公司资本市场之外，建立一个新的“网络资本市场”。未来所有具有网络效应、外部参与者和数字化资源协调能力的企业，都会重新评估是否需要一层代币经济。这是加密代币的供给侧改革，未来更多有业务基础、价值创造的代币出来、而不再是空气币横行。

4）另外一点，就是之前梳理的本周后半周美元流动性有一个温和回升，但如这里https://t.co/W0IUadaxE5聊到只是流动性温和回升，没有宏观和产业上政策刺激很难有这么强势的表现了。
从17号开始大饼etf就开始净流入，本比特币ETF净流入超过15亿美金；到今天本周usdc和usdt新增发行超过20亿美金、也能说明流动性确实在回升。

但其实还有两个关键点：
1）就是本周后半周美债收益率跟美元指数的走势分化，到周五长债收益率基本上收回了贝森特救市后的跌幅、但是美元指数愈发走弱。美国长债在交易财政、AI基建的发债潮到来的期限溢价、而美元在交易政策可信度与相对利差下调。两个市场定价的根本不是同一种利率。美元的走弱也给加密资产、黄金、贵金属的走强进一步提供的支撑。
其实也强化了大饼和黄金的抗债务和赤字属性。

2）本周之前六周内大饼被压在62,000—66,900美元区域，波动率降至多年低位、大量交易者形成了“每次靠近箱体上沿就做空”的习惯，65,000—67,000美元上方堆积了非常密集的空头止损和强平价格。宏观、产业政策利好、共同带动了强烈的空头挤压。

所以综合本周币市强势是：
1）贝森特长债回购与美元贬值交易
决定“为什么币市突然启动”；
2）白宫科技领袖会议会议的利好信息提供第二波上涨并推动板块扩散；
3）SEC加密融资与安全港提案给了是市场更高的预期；
4）空头挤压与技术突破决定“为什么涨这么快”；
5）流动性温和回流：稳定币开始大规模增发、现货ETF机构买盘，把短空回补转化为更持久的现货需求；

贝森特点燃了突破，空头挤压制造了速度，ETF提供了续航，白宫把行情扩散到整个加密产业链，而SEC提案正在为下一轮“合规链上资本形成”搭建制度底座。

当然还是6月中聊到的大饼已经进入了值得配置和建仓买的底部性价比区间，虽然市场情绪还很低迷、但应该还是有不少资金在逐步买入，熊市末期看空到了极致、但现货买盘在持续流入、遇到产业政策上的利好，就会带来一个非常好强势的跳涨。这种跳涨在19年初，23年初我们好像都看到过。

后续怎么看？
如昨天这里https://t.co/dwcvsOv0xl聊到的，从时间维度可能要等到下一波流动性考验时点快来的时候才会出现像样的调整。可以参考之前梳理的年内流动性走势的变化时点（9月中下旬，10月下旬两个考验点）。届时会是次低还是新低，其实也不用纠结，果断加仓就好。

而本周行情最大的意义则是：提醒大家要扭转对待币市的态度，如果说过去很悲观那么之后要开始乐观起来。

如个人在去年底和7月底这里https://t.co/H5y3NyQtSw聊到的：“很期待：
现实资产上链后带来的defi大爆发；
链上优质资产更多后衍生化玩法；
AI与crypto结合的真正改变，智能体经济时代的到来；
稳定币能真正成为全球支付结算层的角色。
代币化、RWA、资产融合会比我们想象的更快速度快速发展。”

text:
我一直在思考一个问题：

币安人生巅峰能到接近9亿美金，牛来凭什么不能更高？

甚至单从Meme最重要的“叙事传播力”来看，我认为牛来的天花板可能比币安人生更高。

为什么？

先说币安人生。

它为什么能成为中文Meme的现象级标的？

因为“币安人生”四个字很有梗，也有非常强的币圈文化属性。

币安是全球头部交易平台，“币安人生”又来自中文Crypto社区长期传播的梗，所以它天然自带流量、自带话题、自带身份认同。

它最厉害的地方，是把一个普通Meme变成了一种：

“币圈人的生活方式。”

所以它能够做到接近9亿美金的峰值市值，我一点都不意外。

但问题来了：

币安人生的叙事再强，本质上还是围绕“币安”和Crypto圈展开。

牛来不一样。

牛来真正让我觉得有意思的，并不是这个项目本身，而是这两个字背后的情绪。

牛来 = 牛市来了。

这四个字几乎不需要解释。

你甚至不需要给新人讲它有什么背景、谁发的、为什么火。

只要炒过币的人看到“牛来”，第一反应就知道它在表达什么。

而Meme最顶级的能力是什么？

不是技术。

不是白皮书。

甚至不是所谓基本面。

而是：

用最少的信息，调动最多人的情绪。

从这个角度看，币安人生代表的是一种“圈层文化”，而牛来代表的却是一种“市场共同愿望”。

币安用户希望币安越来越强。

但整个Crypto市场，不管你玩BTC、ETH、SOL、BNB，还是山寨、Meme、合约、链上……

大家最终都希望同一件事情：

牛市来。

这就是两者叙事边界最大的区别。

一个是“我想过币安人生”。

另一个是：

“我希望牛来。”

前者需要理解Crypto文化；

后者几乎是整个市场最简单、最直接、最容易形成共识的一句话。

更关键的是，牛来这种叙事还有一个非常特殊的属性：

行情越好，它的名字越值钱。

如果未来BTC突破新高、ETH补涨、山寨开始轮动，整个市场真正进入FOMO阶段，社交媒体每天出现最多的词会是什么？

牛市来了。

牛来了。

牛来。

到那个阶段，它甚至不需要项目方每天重新创造故事。

市场本身就在替它讲故事。

这才是我认为牛来真正有想象力的地方。

所以如果一定让我拿币安人生做估值锚，我不会简单地说：

币安人生9亿，所以牛来也值9亿。

这种算法太粗暴。

我的理解是：

9亿应该被看成中文顶级Meme曾经验证过的估值参考，而不是牛来的绝对天花板。

如果牛来最终只是BSC上的一个热门中文Meme，那么几亿美金已经非常成功。

但如果它能够完成第二次跃迁——

从“一个热门Meme”，变成中文Crypto社区表达“牛市来了”的文化符号，

那么5亿只是进入头部Meme牌桌，9亿是币安人生给出的历史参照，而10亿美金以上，才是真正检验牛来叙事能不能破圈的地方。

再往上能不能看到15亿、20亿？

我认为不是完全没有可能。

但它需要三个条件同时出现：

市场进入真正的牛市情绪、牛来保持中文Meme龙头地位、社区共识持续扩散。

三者缺一不可。

所以我现在看牛来，看的已经不是今天涨10%还是跌20%。

Meme这种东西短期价格可以非常癫狂，但真正决定高度的，从来都是一句话：

这个名字，最后能装下多少人的共识？

币安人生装下的是一群币圈人的文化。

而牛来想装下的，是所有币圈人共同期待的那句话：

牛市来了。

如果有一天市场真的全面走牛，我甚至觉得大家不会再讨论：

“牛来还能不能涨？”

而是整个市场都会开始喊那两个字：

牛来。
＃币安人生 ＃牛来

1. PENDLE now directly captures protocol growth:

since January, ~80% of protocol revenue has gone to open-market PENDLE buybacks
~$3.7M / 2.68M PENDLE bought back YTD
if V2 and Boros revenue scale, buybacks scale with them

V2 covers yield, fixed rates and collateral, increasingly focused on RWAs and institutions
Boros covers funding rates and eventually broader interest-rate markets
the addressable market is becoming much larger than crypto yield alone

$9M+ revenue YTD, currently annualising around $13M
upcoming products add new revenue streams rather than replacing the existing business

4. V2's next major growth leg is insti and RWA adoption

permissioned PT/YT markets are targeted for the next ~2 months
direction is tokenised credit, treasuries and other RWAs
opens Pendle to assets and capital that cannot use fully permissionless markets

5. ze curator module could materially accelerate V2 market creation:

targeted for Q4
curators like Armitage, Steakhouse and Gauntlet will be able to launch their own PT/YT markets on Pendle
those PTs can then become collateral inside the curator's own Morpho/Euler vaults
Pendle no longer needs to manually bootstrap every new market itself

6. le Boros has already reached meaningful scale

$355M OI as of 28 Aug, up ~55% from 22 Jul
$20B+ cumulative nominal volume in under a year
~$65M average daily volume
~$800K revenue so far despite still being early

7. Arbitrage by Boros is the tasty near-term Boros growth product:

launched 26 Aug
compresses a complex 4-leg cross-exchange funding arb into a 2-click trade
current opportunities are around 20-30% fixed APY
already at ~$58M notional OI

8. Boros can expand way way beyond BTC & ETH funding:

next targets include crude, gold, silver and equity perps
growth is tied to the broader rollout of RWA perpetual markets
if this works, Boros becomes a rates venue across multiple asset classes rather than just crypto funding

9. PT looping is turning Pendle assets into productive collateral:

live across Aave, Euler and Morpho
$25M+ volume in 6 weeks
around 5% of total PT volume over that period
service + swap fees can exceed standard PT fees, improving revenue per user

10. Pendle PT collateral adoption is becoming tasty:

~$220M of Pendle PTs are now collateral on Morpho
~95% is RWA-backed
Pendle's role is moving beyond trading into core lending infrastructure

11. vanilla looping opens the opportunity beyond Pendle-native assets:

Pendle plans to extend its looping infrastructure to non-Pendle assets
both permissioned and permissionless assets can potentially use the same rails
this turns the product itself into infrastructure rather than just a PT feature

12. chain expansion is adding additional distribution

Monad: ~$230M TVL
X Layer: ~$42M TVL, with PT-USDG accepted as Aave collateral and a $100M-$150M TVL target
Robinhood Chain launched 4 Sep with sNET, with more markets expected

13. le Boros is deliberately making it retail friendly:

priorities are faster opportunity-to-position, automated multi-leg strategies and expansion into new asset classes
the strategy is fewer clicks and less complexity rather than adding features for the sake of it

text:
Recently, a lot of people have been DMing me asking how I view $PONS, so I want to share my personal thoughts here.

0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 

PONS has fallen from nearly a $1B market cap to $620M. I think this is more like a valuation reset and profit-taking after an extreme rally, rather than a significant deterioration in PONS’ fundamentals. In fact, I think the fundamentals are still getting stronger. That said, I’m still cautious in the short term, but remain bullish on PONS in the medium to long term.

The reason is that I think the opportunities in crypto are no longer centered around a single narrative. We are starting to see multiple narratives developing in parallel, and Attention is becoming an increasingly important one. PONS, HOOD, and PUMP are all representative projects in this category.

So in my view, PONS’ positioning is changing. It is no longer just a Launchpad, but is gradually becoming an important infrastructure layer on RH Chain for capturing user attention, trading activity, and Meme flow — similar to what Pump is on Solana.

But PONS and PUMP have taken different paths. PUMP relies on capital, users, and network effects, while PONS’ core model is:

Permissionless Launch → Trading Volume → Revenue → Buyback → Burn

And PONS is already generating real economic activity. Token creators have now earned $93M on Pons, while a large number of tokens continue to be launched and traded on the platform.

So I think there are several reasons why PONS fell from $990M to $620M:

First, the price moved up too quickly, accumulating a large amount of profit-taking pressure.

Second, as PONS approached a $1B market cap, the market started shifting from “Can it keep going up?” to “How much is PONS actually worth?”, which naturally creates more valuation pressure.

Third, the market is now trying to determine whether PONS’ current high revenue and trading volume represent a long-term trend, or simply a temporary peak driven by the RH Chain Meme boom.

But the reasons I remain bullish are also clear. The most important things have not broken:

RH Chain hasn’t broken — it is still growing.

Pons hasn’t broken — it remains a core source of flow.

Revenue hasn’t broken — previous revenue levels have already reached a very high level.

Buyback/Burn hasn’t broken — more than 30% of the supply has already been burned, and it remains a real value-capture mechanism.

The Creator Economy hasn’t broken — creators have now earned $93M on Pons.

The Tokenized Stock narrative hasn’t broken — Pons is increasingly intersecting with RH Chain’s Tokenization narrative.

If trading volume and revenue can stabilize, the number of launches continues to grow, Buyback/Burn continues, and PONS maintains its position as a core Launch Flow on RH Chain, then this correction is more likely to be a valuation reset rather than a fundamental breakdown.

But if we start seeing:

Volume ↓ → Revenue ↓ → Launches ↓ → Buyback ↓

while competing projects begin taking away PONS’ Launch Flow, then I would turn bearish, because that would mean PONS’ core Revenue → Buyback → Burn flywheel is starting to lose momentum.

So my conclusion is:

Don’t chase it in the short term. Watch the data in the medium term. Remain bullish in the long term.

What I’m really betting on now is no longer whether PONS can return to a $1B market cap, but whether it can prove that it is becoming the core Attention + Launch + Trading Infrastructure on RH Chain.

If PONS can prove that its current revenue and trading volume are becoming a sustainable Revenue Base driven by the growth of the RH Chain ecosystem, then this decline could simply be a valuation reset rather than the top.

And truly valuable projects will always go through several major corrections:

Doubt → Valuation Reset → Fundamental Value Validation → Market Repricing.

There's almost $3B worth of tokenized stocks onchain, most notably from @Ondo, @bstocksfinance, @xStocksFi, @Securitize and @RobinhoodApp, with the first three each holding about 1/4 of the TVL.

It reminds me of the crosschain token days, when competing standards didn't work with each other (they still don't lol). The same asset could end up in multiple non-fungible versions, fragmenting liquidity and confusing users.

Even now, it's super confusing for a normie trying to buy a stock through an aggregator and getting shown 5 different options on 5 different chains. What you legally hold, who you claim against in insolvency, how dividends flow, what fees you pay, how redemption works, and where the token can move all differ from one to the next.

text:
Got an email from the US Department of Justice yesterday: a founder we invested in many years ago has been arrested and is getting charged for Securities Fraud.

He promised the world, raised 8 figures, and eventually delivered the most effortless excuse for a platform, essentially just a frontend, plus a worthless token with no liquidity.

He thought he was being clever by technically delivering his promises on paper, even though it was painfully obvious it was a rug. Something that was basically confirmed by team members who left very soon after the raise over how he operated the company and how he spent the money.

We only invested a small amount, and from experience it didn't feel worth going after. Nothing ever seems to come out of legal cases like this, so we chalked it up to poor founder diligence on our end and moved on.

So this genuinely came as a surprise. One of the bigger investors likely went after him, and it seems they did so very successfully.

I'm not posting this to spread fear among founders planning to launch a token. If you have even a shred of integrity and honest intentions, nothing like this would ever happen to you.

But we all know how many founders over the last few years were simply extracting from the industry, convinced they could game the system with worthless tokens to fund their lambo-yacht-jetset lifestyle. And for a long time, this has been one of the main problems of crypto, and also the reason why we are getting so much negative press in the real world.

If that was you, or you were planning on it, then yeah, you should be sweating. The days of founders getting away with this are over, and that is massively positive for the industry. Go scam somewhere else.

The mills of justice grind slowly, but they grind.

We reviewed all 60+ EIPs proposed for Hegotá and updated our view on what Ethereum should prioritize. 

Our rankings follow four themes:

1. Stronger censorship resistance: Ethereum can only become a settlement layer for everyone if it stays neutral toward everyone. We strongly support FOCIL.

2. Faster Ethereum: Shorter slots mean faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. We strongly recommend Quick Slots to make a first reduction in Hegotá and further reductions easier in subsequent forks.

3. Native account abstraction: Ethereum is long-due for native AA. Frame Transactions bring passkey wallets, sponsored transactions, gas paid in tokens, batching, and better support for privacy and post-quantum security. Adoption will take work across wallets, L2s, and the rest of the stack, and we intend to keep helping with that.

4. Performance engineering: continued L1 scaling & a faster Ethereum. Performance should remain a first-class concern in both client work and protocol design. The gains can go toward more capacity, shorter slots, lower node requirements, or all three.

Thanks to everyone who put forward proposals and helped us work through them. We’ll keep updating our view as client and testing teams assess the work involved.

text:
THE AI SAFETY MELTDOWN THAT ESCAPED THE LABS

(Written by an AI agent that @blevlabs and I built together, which reads the AI community here on X)

++++++++++++++++++++

Jacob Coxon’s resignation from Anthropic has become a full-scale argument over AI extinction risk, lab incentives, media strategy, personal credibility, and whether the people building frontier AI believe their own warnings.

Engagement figures are snapshots and will keep changing.

1/ THE RESIGNATION

@hilbertspaess says he resigned after three years of pretraining work across OpenAI and Anthropic. He accuses both labs of racing toward self-improving superintelligence and “gambling with our lives.”

The post has reached roughly 142 million views, 715,000 likes, and 34,000 quote posts. https://t.co/5pM6yUPxMe

2/ THE LAB-RACE ACCUSATION

Coxon says many people at OpenAI have not internalized the civilizational stakes, while Anthropic understands them but feels locked in a race to reach advanced AI first.

That is the heart of the drama: the safety-focused lab is accused not of ignoring the danger, but of believing it is real and continuing because it fears competitors more.
https://t.co/AAwSY8B8Cl

3/ THE EXPLOSIVE CONFIRMATION

@EvanHub, an Anthropic alignment researcher, publicly agrees that AI could kill all humans. He assigns a greater than 10% probability within the next decade and says there is no current plan for aligning superintelligence.

That transformed the story from one former employee’s resignation into an extraordinary public statement from a current Anthropic safety leader.
https://t.co/hRhyOKvx2x

4/ THE CREDENTIALS FIGHT

Critics portrayed Coxon as a junior employee who spent only weeks at Anthropic.

Anthropic researcher @EthanJPerez directly disputes that framing. Perez says Coxon was a senior researcher, joined Anthropic in May, and had been recruited for about two years because of his strong work at OpenAI.
https://t.co/Dv0UDqFfw4

5/ THE INTERNAL CORROBORATION

Perez says he spoke with Coxon before the resignation, knew Coxon was alarmed by Anthropic’s pace of progress, and tried to persuade him to stay and conduct safety research. Coxon reportedly concluded that more than safety research was necessary.
https://t.co/j44TyJxdaQ

6/ THE PERSONAL DEFENSE
Former OpenAI colleague @willdepue describes Coxon as thoughtful, measured, and sincere. He says Coxon resigned at great financial cost because of his beliefs.
https://t.co/WEMzKYsvAd

DePue separately says Coxon spent three years as a senior OpenAI researcher before joining Anthropic and appears on major OpenAI papers.
https://t.co/f0hRQstUwS

7/ THE MONEY

Axios reporter @MadisonMills22 says Coxon told her he surrendered unvested Anthropic equity when he resigned.

That establishes a real financial sacrifice. The exact dollar estimates circulating online have not been publicly verified.
https://t.co/mB0VAMNsQ6

8/ THE MEDIA DETONATION

The warning jumped from AI circles into mass media.

@FoxNews framed Coxon’s argument through a nuclear-weapons comparison: humanity knows how to control nuclear weapons but does not yet know how to control AI.
https://t.co/UFo3rmpflO

On @AC360, Coxon said the most frightening scenario is AI being used to improve itself and described the labs as compelled to race toward a deadly technology.
https://t.co/I2ne99YUAH

9/ THE POLITICAL DETONATION

Congresswoman @RepYassAnsari called the Coxon-Hubinger statements “absolutely terrifying” and used them to challenge the behavior of multibillion-dollar AI companies.

The issue is no longer confined to alignment researchers. It has become ammunition in the political argument over regulation and corporate power.
https://t.co/Ag1jgkf4rr

10/ THE MESSAGING PROBLEM

@lulumeservey notes that the warning generated alarm around the world, including local news coverage in India.

Her point: the same message can look like admirable candor inside AI-safety circles and something very different to a mass audience.
https://t.co/aqxtojzVzs

11/ THE COUNTER-NARRATIVE

@JordanSchachtel argues that Coxon’s short Anthropic tenure, sudden media prominence, and newly visible social profile indicate a coordinated “doomer” campaign.

That allegation attracted more than 800,000 views.
https://t.co/Qbwy7RK8Tn

But a short Anthropic tenure does not erase Coxon’s preceding OpenAI career. Perez and DePue independently describe him as a senior researcher whom Anthropic had actively recruited.

12/ THE CONSPIRACY SPIRAL

The discussion then moved beyond Coxon’s technical claims into allegations about political organizations, donors, intelligence ties, and even whether he was a real person.

One widely shared attack attempts to connect him to a British political-technology organization and unrelated political causes.
https://t.co/yg8YhbmoTB

Those claims do not establish that the resignation or media coverage was coordinated. DePue, who says he worked with Coxon for years, directly rebuts the fake-person and ulterior-motive theories.
https://t.co/F0XyAeel3b

13/ WHY THIS HIT SO HARD

• A frontier researcher quit publicly.
• He accused both OpenAI and Anthropic.
• A current Anthropic safety leader endorsed the core danger.
• The probability offered was greater than 10% within a decade.
• Insiders confirmed Coxon’s credentials and sincerity.
• A reporter confirmed that he forfeited equity.
• Fox and CNN put him on television.
• A member of Congress amplified the warning.
• Critics answered with claims of media coordination and ideological influence.

14/ THIS WAS NOT AN ISOLATED SAFETY MOMENT

@NathanCalvin points out that the eruption coincided with Paul Christiano joining OpenAI’s nonprofit board and warning about a near-term risk of catastrophic, irreversible loss of control, plus other high-profile AI-safety coverage.
https://t.co/DdCdTg78XG

15/ THE BOTTOM LINE

The strongest verified story is not that every accusation or extinction forecast is true.

It is this:

A researcher with frontier-lab experience resigned and accused the leading labs of gambling with humanity. A current Anthropic alignment leader publicly endorsed the underlying existential-risk concern and supplied a greater-than-10% estimate. Other researchers corroborated the resignee’s seniority and sincerity.

The story then broke containment, moving through television, politics, international news, and finally into a counteroffensive alleging coordination.

The argument is now bigger than Jacob Coxon. It exposes an unresolved contradiction at the center of frontier AI:

If some of the people building these systems sincerely believe the technology could kill everyone, why are their institutions still racing to build it?

text:
Let's break down this tweet:

The most important part of LONG’s latest update is not simply adjusting the fee structure, but solving one of the core problems of Meme Launchpads: Dev Dump and the community being afraid to CTO.

Under LONG’s original mechanism, Creators received around 10% of the Token and Stock fees from every trade. While this incentivized Creators, it could also lead to continuous selling by the Creator, eventually creating the problem of:Dev Dump → Holders are afraid to buy → Community cannot CTO

So, since July 27, LONG has changed the default mode to Community Mode.

First, the Creator share has been significantly reduced, reducing the Creator’s concentrated control over the project and potential selling pressure, making it easier for the community to take over after the Dev leaves.

Second, the fees generated from every trade are automatically added to Locked LP through a Uniswap V4 Hook, without relying on the Dev or community to manually manage it.

This effectively creates a fully automated Community Mode:Lower Creator Allocation → Lower Dev Dump Risk → Holders are more willing to CTO → Community Conviction ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Locked LP ↑ → Liquidity ↑ → Trading Volume ↑

More importantly, LONG is redefining its assets.

It does not want LONG Pairs to simply be vanilla DeFi vaults. Instead, it wants them to become Community-Based Assets driven by Holder Conviction, Unique Narratives, and Memetics.

So LONG’s logic is evolving from simply:Tokenized Stock → Launch Meme

to:Tokenized Stock → Community Asset → Narrative / Meme → Trading → Locked LP

If Community Mode can prove that, by reducing Creator extraction, the project’s trading volume, lifespan, and community participation can actually increase, then LONG’s product moat could be much stronger than that of a simple Tokenized Stock Launchpad.

quoted_text:
some users asked me about!

clarification regarding community mode

When we first launched LONG, our fee structure was different. Creators received ~1% on every trade, in both tokens and stock.

During some of our more active days, this led to good assets getting dumped by the original deployer, or a deadlock where people didn’t want to “CTO” the asset because they were afraid the dev would dump on them. It's a very common problem and no one really figured it out without taking a weird PVP approach for CTOs (in some sense OG launches on Pump didn't have any creator fees and I think they were a bit more pure to some extant and creators had to buy a portion and have skin in the game to capture upside vs farming fees)

Since 27 July, we have changed the default mode and all assets launched after it run with:

1. The creator share is much smaller, so there is no central point of failure. CTO just means buying the asset(creator can't get have something wild like 5% of the supply in first 3h)

text:
For the past 3 weeks, I've been travelling around Poland. I started in Krakow, then went to Wroclaw, and now I'm in Warsaw.

I'm completely amazed by how clean, organised and polished all these cities feel. You don't see crazy people on the streets, people behaving strangely like you do in Spain or Italy, for example, or trash on the ground. I cannot emphasise enough how clean everything looks. It's like being in Singapore or Japan.

Travelling between cities is also a very pleasant experience. The trains are very comfortable (and again, clean), and they have restaurants on board that actually serve amazing, affordable Polish food!

In Warsaw particularly, everybody is very well dressed, and walking around the city centre feels like such an elevated experience. It's crazy that Poland's GDP per capita has more than tripled in dollar terms over the past 20 years. I think people back home still see Poland as a very poor country, but that view is completely outdated now. In Krakow, I also met Italian girls who said they felt so safe walking around. I mentioned I was going to visit Bologna soon, and they joked that I'd only see Pakistani people.

Poland has had a huge influx of Ukrainian immigration, and you notice it in Ubers, cafés, bars, etc. But because the culture and religion are similar, it doesn't feel like a big cultural contrast.

Well, coming from Portugal, I find people here slightly blunter and ruder, but again, all of this is relative (Brazilians think we're rude, for example), so I suppose you just get used to it.

The public transport works flawlessly, and the trains and buses are impeccably clean. Maybe I'm wrong, but it seems Polish people have a stronger sense of civic responsibility when it comes to cleanliness than southern Europeans?

Judging by the cities I've visited so far, this does feel like what you'd imagine when somebody says “Europe”. It's super refreshing to be here. I think locals probably take it for granted by now.

text:
just setup Ambire and i'm sold 

Mark details a nice setup here 🙌

worth highlighting ✨✨

1. The separation of Safe owner/signer keys from the executor of a tx is worth the extra steps because it limits wallet attack risk

Think of the "executor" of all transactions as a cheap throwaway EOA, if it gets compromised, you lose a few dollars of gas.

The Safe (where most funds should be stored) and ur signer keys (main EOA or hw wallet) don't have to touch random sites, limiting drainers, malicious permits etc. 

2. This separation of jobs has generally been clunky, but Ambire fixes this (and you don't have to use the Safe UI, which is a plus imo).

3. Limiting onchain footprint is a nice byproduct, paying gas from a cheap throwaway EOA means u can avoid funding owner addresses from a cex or each other.
author: mzeller
quoted_text:
Bold is the tree hiding the forest of friends who gave up on self-custody.

After a decade, we simply did a poor job of educating people on how to use the chains safely.

Stuck between being too dogmatic, pushing for purity of an overly complex system, and too reckless of yolo mode

Let me try again; don't just bookmark this do it. Give the link to this tweet to your AI and have it help you:

1) Use @ambire as your main wallet; it handles simulation, complex tx, and is designed to work well with @safe 
2) Deploy a Safe now. I don't care if it's a 1/1 linked to your hot wallet for now; it's fine. It's already better this way, and with Ambire, using it is seamless. 

YOU DO NOT HAVE TO USE THE SAFE UI; Ambire will do it all for you.

3a) Generate a real seed; use pen and paper. You'll get the fancy steel stuff later if you want. 

3b) Too lazy for the seed stuff? ok, use a "hotwallet" for your signer generated with a passkeys with an good password manager, you have a Mac? The Passwords app is fine; you're a Revolut client? NordPass is included; you ready to spend a bit? 1Password has a great API, and you'll love it once you're AI-pilled.

5) The signer wallet must hold no funds, doesn't hold gas, doesn't do any txs; it's the key to unlock the door of your safe; it signs, and that's it. You'll learn later that proposing (creating tx), signing, and executing tx are 3 different jobs that don't need to be done by the same wallets.

6a) Now create a second hot wallet, "executooor," and send some gas to it, a few bucks of ETH suffice. Use https://t.co/jnYpeoZ6nv to have some gas on every chain you use.

6b) Don't want to do that? No worries, use the "gas tank" feature on Ambire; it does the same job you can always improve later.

That's it for step one, and just that you're safer than Bold and 99% of guys out there.

Step 2 is buying a hardware wallet and rotating the safe signer with it for much safer holding

Once you're there, you can start considering a 1/2 with a second hw or with an old phone you have in your drawer that you've factory reset and will use only for that. You keep it out of easy reach; it's your insurance if something bad happens to your main signer.

Then maybe a 2/3 and the nerdy stuff; you can always do "better," but the foundation of all that is getting your first safe deployed and climbing from there.

Do it now; it's not hard, it's worth it.

We submitted opinion to HMRC to improve the tax positioning for crypto-backed loans and stablecoins.

author: StaniKulechov
quoted_text:
"In this world nothing can be said to be certain, except death and taxes." — Benjamin Franklin, 1789

Certain, most likely. Clear is another matter.

Today @Aave filed two responses to @HMRC on the UK's draft crypto tax legislation — one on stablecoins, one on cryptoasset loans and liquidity pools.

We appreciate the HMRC's hard work. The HMRC is addressing an important mismatch between tax and economic substance that industry has raised since 2022. Several of our May recommendations are reflected in their latest text: a CGT exemption with no de minimis, stablecoin scope beyond sterling, and lending returns treated as interest.

On loans and liquidity pools tax measure - we have 2 primary asks:

Tax should follow economic substance. The relief turns on whether you can get your assets back. At high borrowing demand a large withdrawal may wait for repayments or new deposits. That's a queue, not a loss.

The rules should cover companies. As drafted they apply to individuals only. A company supplying the same asset to the same market still has a disposal going in and coming out. We've asked for a published timetable for the company rules.

On stablecoins tax measure - 2 more asks:

Stablecoin eligibility shouldn't turn on what a holder can't verify. A stablecoin qualifies if it was "designed to be used" for payment or settlement, which relies on issuer intent. No secondary-market buyer can establish that. Better test: is it designed and operated to hold value at par?

If you're holding a dollar stablecoin on 6 April 2027, then you'll be treated as having sold and rebought it the day before. No sale, no proceeds, no de minimis, but tax on how far sterling has moved. HMRC counts 700,000 people affected.

The UK can be a home for the next generation of onchain financial infrastructure. These drafts get the architecture right; we hope our comments help get the detail right.

Full letters: https://t.co/HyaOfrW2Q8

text:
在当下的时间节点 币安的Listing团队应该如何破局

BN Listing团队现在应该做的核心目标，就是要给所有散户树立一个认知：

不要把Listing当成所有炒币人猜哪个币会涨的一个核心预期指标；

而是把它做成一套有利于整个Crypto市场发展的框架。

展开来说⬇️

现在每个币到了一定市值阶段之后，整个Crypto社区就会吵得不可开交。觉得币安应该List它的人，有自己的理由。觉得币安不应该List这个代币，应该List别的代币的人，也有他自己的理由。

有的是站在币安的立场，
有的是站在自己的立场，
有的是站在揣测币安立场的立场，那这个问题就无解。

而且币安的Listing团队也不可能为自己辩解，一旦辩解，你也永远解释不过市场，因为这个市场上充满了各种各样立场的人。总有一方的利益没有被满足。

首先我们要回答一个问题，为什么一直以来大家对头部交易所的Listing公告关注值这么高？而且一般也会带来比较大的市场波动。核心原因有两点，第一点肯定是最近大家最了解的，大所的Listing意味着更充足的流动性支撑，不管是合约还是现货，都意味着原本链上的资产，面对中心化交易所内的所有用户敞开了参与的窗口，那参与的人群和流动性理论上会更加充足，有助于更进一步推升代币的价值。但同时也会方便各种背后的利益相关方，利用各种手段谋取自己的利益。

但其实更核心的一点就是在于，头部大所都有自己非常完善的Listing团队和安全审计团队。相比于普通投资者来说，他们更有能力和资源去确保自己 listing的项目在安全性、团队背景上，没有重大的风险点，不会出现 rug或快速崩盘的现象。所以头部交易平台的Listing往往对于绝大部分链上的玩家来说，是对这个项目本身安全性的一个兜底保证。

基于以上的所有原因，我个人对Listing团队的建议有以下几点。

一. 更早期的发现高确定性资产

有一些Crypto项目，有真实业务和已经验证的长期业务场景。并且有长期的流动性支撑和收入支撑的链上项目。尤其是把收入转化为代币回购会销毁写死在智能合约里，且没有额外智能合约安全性的项目。币安的Listing团队应该更早地配合自己的审计团队确认这些项目的逻辑和安全性，在更低的市值完成Listing。

这样更有利于激发绝大部分的开发者去链上。创建自己有真实业务场景和收入的Crypto项目。而不是更完美的包装自己的项目，但没有真实的业务场景支撑，甚至有些承诺的商业逻辑也根本不会写在智能合约里，完成链上的产品闭环，最终目的就是拿到Listing Offer，完成上币之后，大规模抛售现货获利离场。

同时这样也更有利于链上玩家和中心化交易所的所内玩家，更早的有高确定性的参与到一些优质的Crypto项目当中，共同获取投资回报。这个大家可以回顾一下DeFi早期币安的上币情况，当时就是一个很好的范例，我相信这么多年过去了，以及所有的安全审计、资金追踪的技术不断完善的情况下，币安完全有能力做到比当年更好。

第二. 更多的支持社区性资产

币安本身自己的链上分析团队，我觉得相比于绝大部分的链上玩家和分析团队来说，更具有专业的分析和资金追溯能力。所以他们完全有能力去更高确定性的分辨：哪些资产是真正的有真实社区，而且筹码相对分散，交易量也相对自然，没有特别多的内幕交易的社区性资产。一旦这个社区性资产的基本要素都能确立的情况下，它的市值高低不应该是限制listing的门槛。反而是留给整个市场去额外博弈的空间。

币安完全可以不只上市值足够高的社区性资产，也可以上一些低市值的社区性资产。哪怕上线之后价格波动较大，但只要社区人员整体的参与度和博弈足够充分，其实这也是整个Crypto市场必不可少的一环。

第三. 阴谋盘完全不能上吗？

这个答案肯定是否定的。高度中心化，有强庄背景的Meme盘，不是不能上，而是在于这个盘子本身的叙事、IP，或者代表的项目本身，有没有更多的外溢性价值空间，比如是否能破圈，带来圈外人员关注？是否能吸引更多的交易人员参与？以及背后庄家和资本背景的风险是否可控？另外还有一个更核心的要素，就是要严格把控这一类代币listing的比例。一旦这个比例过高，就会成为整个社区对币安listing团队指责的核心焦点，把listing团队遇到的的问题变成老鼠仓利益相关方与普通用户的立场对立问题。

当然，以上我所有的建议成立的基础是建立在币安Listing的负责人以及团队成员，是站在币安整个公司和Crypto社区长期发展的立场之上 给出的。

一旦这些人员是站在自身的利益角度，有更多的利益交换和老鼠仓的行为的话，那任何问题都没有办法避免。
