text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

Team + Contributors

United Founders Group has at least one public dev, @Cibolan2000, who is a team member. But as I understand it, DeFiDave core idea is to bring top DeFi founders and devs into the ecosystem as contributors/advisors, which resonates with the product itself, so the best minds in DeFi could end up working together on strategies inside this year's main chain

@samkazemian <> @fraxfinance <> @defidave 
I grouped them together because Sam and DeFi Dave (prev Frax team) were among UFG's first followers
Frax publicly supported the v2 announcement, and sfrxETH is set to be integrated. For those who don't know, Frax is one of the OG DeFi protocols, with a peak mcap of $1b

DeFi Dave is doing incredible work shilling UFG

The product is still at its earliest stage, but soon this could turn into an ecosystem of dozens of products, each generating profit that in turn backs the price of robinhood:0xefab538cf3c29237a47c6afb145d50ddf204a0a3 

But I think the most important thing here is the team/contributors
We have a partnership with Frax and their support; top names in the DeFi industry are speaking publicly about the project in a positive light, which also leads me to think we'll see new partnerships with large DeFi protocols and their supporting, bringing additional attention and value to UFG

The final straw that could push the token to new ATHs might be an appearance on @MCGlive
The team managed to convey why their product is valuable and unique to the top DeFi chads, now they need to do the same for the degens, who for some reason still don't get this project

quoted_text:
We've all been there. You wake up feeling unwell, try to get an appointment, and before you know it half the day has disappeared. 

When you're sick, the last thing you should be worrying about is how you're going to get the help you need. 

That's why we're expanding Pharmacy First. The idea is simple: 

Qualified pharmacists can assess patients, dispense medicines and prescribe treatment for a range of common conditions, helping people get care quickly and close to home. So you don’t have to go to hospital, and you don’t need to book a GP appointment. Just walk into your local pharmacy and get the treatment you need right there, right then.  

These services make a huge difference, especially for older people and those who are vulnerable. 

That's why we invested a further £340 million in community pharmacies, including to deliver Pharmacy First. 

Six million consultations have been delivered since the launch of the scheme. 

GPs and NHS 111 have referred three million people to their local pharmacy. 

And pharmacists have provided more than three million urgent medicine supplies. 

We’re making it possible for qualified prescribing pharmacists to treat five more common health conditions this autumn, like migraines and ear infections, so access to treatment is easier than ever. And what we’re announcing today will make it easier to see a GP for those who need it.

I know how hard our NHS works, how much pressure staff are under and how tough it can be for people to access the care they need from my time as Health Secretary. And I know things have only got tougher in the last 15 years.  

As Mayor of Greater Manchester, I saw firsthand how important it is to put more firepower in the frontlines and give people more control over their own lives. 

Every place and every person matters. So we’ll make sure people can get the care they need, where they need it. That’s what this is all about. 

Faster treatment. More services. Better care for patients. And less pressure on hospitals and GPs.

One less headache for people to worry about.

text:
People conflate two separate ideas:

1) AI makes it easier to build your own software (cancel ScrapingBee and vibe code your own scraper)

2) AI makes software obsolete (you don’t need a booking site, you book directly through ChatGPT)

The latter is a compelling idea, but mostly theoretical for now I think. I don’t know anyone who has booked their holiday through ChatGPT even though it’s technically possible.

Also, when booking a hotel, ChatGPT still needs to know which hotels have availability etc. System of record stuff can’t be generated on-the-fly.

Software will change, but I haven’t seen a convincing argument yet that it will disappear

author: tradirboi
quoted_text:
What's next for flybrain?

We give it a budget and let it loose on the open internet. No prompts, no schedule, nobody picking its moves.

Right now the fly does the seeing and the pointing while a script sequences the run. 

The plan is to hand the sequencing over too — the loop runs unattended, the wallet is the only limit, and whatever 165,122 neurons do with a screen in front of them is what happens.

Being precise about what that is, because it matters: a fly brain has no language and no plan. It won't strategise. It's a real nervous system reacting to pixels, with money attached and nobody steering it. That's the experiment — not "an autonomous AI agent," an actual animal's wiring left alone on the internet with a wallet.

It will do things nobody intended. That's the point, and it's also the risk.

Every move on-chain, every run in the repo, failures included.

text:
有了 MCPX 之后，我最近真的有一种感觉：

ChatGPT 好像被我用出了“无限额度”。

当然不是真的无限。

主要是 Chat 模式本身额度就挺够用，再把 MCPX 装好、配置好以后，很多原本需要我自己切软件、找工具、跑命令的事情，现在都可以直接在 Chat 里完成。

而且我觉得 MCPX 最好用的地方，不是“多了一个新工具”。

恰恰是装好以后，你甚至可以忘掉 MCPX 的存在。

还是和平时一样正常跟 ChatGPT 说话：

帮我查一下这个项目。

看看链上数据。

把这个 bug 修掉。

继续跑监控。

后面的事情，ChatGPT 自己判断需要什么能力，再通过 MCPX 去调用对应的 Tool、MCP、API、Remote Session，做完以后把结果带回来，然后继续往下推进。

所以我现在遇到新的需求，已经很少先想：

“ChatGPT 支不支持这个功能？”

我更关心的是：

“这件事能不能接成一个 Tool？”

只要能接进去，后面很多时候还是一句话的事。

这其实也是我觉得它对普通用户最有价值的地方。

你不需要为了每一种工作都重新学习一套 AI 工具，也不用研究、代码、链上、远程电脑、各种 API 之间来回切。

入口还是同一个 Chat，但后面能调用的能力可以一直增加。

当然，也不是什么事情都可以无条件自动完成。没接入的能力还是没有，登录、验证码、权限会卡住，资金、发帖、账号修改这类重要操作也应该保留确认。

但整体使用体验已经完全不一样了。

以前是：

我去找工具完成任务。

现在越来越像是：

我只告诉 ChatGPT 我想干什么，剩下的它自己找工具去干。

当 Chat 本身额度又比较充足，这两件事叠在一起以后，我最近真的经常有一种感觉：

这玩意怎么什么都能干，而且还怎么都用不完。

9 月 15 到 17 日，Matt Palmer、Lauren Tan 和 Roshan Sadanani 三个人会连续直播三天，用 Grok Bot 从一张白纸开始「造一家公司」。

不是提前做好产品再上台演 Demo。官方给出的流程是：先想做什么，然后写商业计划、定功能、真正写代码，一路做到最后的成品展示。活动页直接写了一句：

Can three people build a company in three days?

这其实比再跑一个 benchmark 有意思多了。

Grok Bot 最近一直在讲「AI teammate」，给每个 Bot 一台自己的云电脑，让它们像员工一样长期干活。

现在 SpaceXAI 干脆把这个说法拉到最极端，如果 Agent 真的是员工，那就别演示它会不会订票、整理邮件了，直接给三个人一家公司，看它能不能把研发、产品、运营这些活接过去。

某种程度上，这三天直播本身就是 Grok Bot 最大的一次公开压力测试。

AI Agent 到底能不能把创业团队压缩到三个人，下周直接直播给所有人看。

text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

text:
这期播客是 The Pragmatic Engineer 对 OpenAI Codex 团队负责人 Thibault（Tibo）的访谈，聊了 Codex 的诞生、技术决策、工程文化以及软件开发方式的变迁。https://t.co/AEv4YPnSZl

以下是核心要点：

个人经历与加入 OpenAI

Thibault 是比利时人，学应用数学出身，先后做过制药供应链优化的创业公司，在 Google 做过加速移动网页的项目（后被砍掉，让他学到了要时刻审视项目真实影响力的教训），之后在 Google Maps 做评论，再转到 DeepMind。在 DeepMind 期间，他参与了一个内部聊天机器人的开发——本质上就是 ChatGPT，但比 ChatGPT 早了一年。内部传播很快，大家都在分享对话，但 DeepMind 不具备把它作为产品发布的机制，最终没能推出。

后来他得知 ChatGPT 只有大约 20 个人在维护，这让他既震惊又觉得很有吸引力——这意味着极高的个人影响力。于是他加入 OpenAI，进去就赶上了推理模型的冲刺，大约一个月后 o1 preview 就发布了。

为什么用 Rust 写 Codex

这是一个反直觉的决定——当时模型对 Rust 的支持并不好，业界其他 AI 编码工具基本都用 TypeScript 或 Python。但团队从第一性原理出发，认为智能体的核心需要健壮、安全、高效，而 Rust 的编译时验证特性天然适合智能体场景。同时用不同语言也强制建立了产品界面和智能体核心之间的清晰边界，避免代码耦合。事实证明 Rust 确实"很快就变得非常适合智能体开发"。

开源和模型无关的策略

Codex CLI、SDK 都是开源的，而且支持非 OpenAI 模型——这在主要 AI 实验室中是独一无二的。理由很实际：如果不开源，别人只需改十行代码就能 fork 出一个支持其他模型的版本，那还不如自己直接支持。开源的好处包括新员工入职前就已经熟悉代码库、社区贡献、以及逼迫自己靠模型和产品体验赢用户而非靠锁定。

代价也很明显：竞争对手会在你还没发布的时候就抄走你正在公开开发的功能，"确实有点刺痛"；还有大量低质量 PR 需要处理。

工程文化与代码审查的变革

新员工入职后听到最多的一句话是"你问过 Codex 了吗？"——因为 Codex 在 OpenAI 内部接入了 Slack、文档、所有代码，几乎任何问题都能给出不错的回答。

代码审查正在发生质变。OpenAI 开发了专门的代码审查模型，能在逻辑推理和安全漏洞检测上达到"超人水平"——可以深入三四层依赖去发现文档错误导致的不变量违反。安全审查已经是强制自动化的，发现安全问题会直接阻止合并。一个 PR 可以当天提交、当天上线到十亿用户的 ChatGPT 上。

代码审查的角色正在从"正确性检查"转向"意图讨论"——你到底想做什么？这件事值不值得做？这种讨论不一定要围绕代码发生。

维护成本和重构的变化

维护一直是软件工程的"税"，但现在大量维护工作（依赖升级、安全补丁）可以完全自动化。更重要的是，重新架构的成本也急剧下降——以前可能要花几个月甚至几年的重构，现在快得多。但好的架构设计反而更重要了：设计好"盒子"和不变量，盒子内部随便改都不影响其他部分。

Harness 与模型的关系

一个有趣的洞察：harness（工具/脚手架）总是"走在模型前面"。Codex 团队的工作本质上是为模型搭建拐杖——提醒它跑测试、保持目标一致等。然后下一代模型训练时会把这些能力内化，拐杖就可以去掉，developer message 也会越来越短。最新一代模型已经不再需要 /goal 命令来保持长期任务的专注，"你直接告诉模型去工作一周，它就真的会做到"。

Codex 与 ChatGPT 的合并

这是一个重大工程挑战：Codex 原本完全本地运行，ChatGPT 是托管云服务，两套完全不同的技术栈要统一。目标是让云端版本具备本地版本同样的能力，同时高效到能纳入 20 美元/月的 Plus 计划。ChatGPT Work 模式本质上是在云端虚拟机里运行完整的 Codex harness，机器配置强大到用户可以在里面训练模型、安装 Blender 做 3D 建模。

有趣的是，Codex 在整个合并过程中还充当了"记者"角色，因为它能访问所有 Slack 讨论和文档，记录了团队的辩论和决策过程。

Thibault 的个人用法与建议

他大量使用手机上的 ChatGPT Work，通过语音口述发送任务，定制了专属的技能和指令来生成他能高效消化的报告和幻灯片。任何问题——公众舆情、生产日志、功能使用率分析、团队动态——30 分钟内都能得到答案。周末他还会用 Codex 做代码探索和原型，"一天之内就能把脑子里的想法变成可以展示给人看的东西"。

对工程师的建议：保持深度好奇心，训练自己快速理解系统的能力（"五个为什么"不断追问），以及与你服务的用户群体保持同步——如果你无法清晰表达意图，就很难做出好的工作。

text:
Charlie Kirk's assassin was not "radicalized". He was not a radical. He was an average, default, base model leftist. I've had coworkers in nice tech jobs who talk like him. I've seen people at my church talk like him. The guys who doxxed me talk like him. People on CNN talk just like him.

The assassination stands out not for its tragedy, but for its normalicy.  Tyler Robinson didn't leave behind some schizophrenic manifesto about the necessity of marijuana eco-eugenicsm. No, he left the same lines news organizations to this day use. "fascist". "harm narratives." "spreading hate." "White nationalism." "inflammatory statements". The shooter's ideology was indistinguishable from an MSNBC article, or any speech given in congress by any Democrat in both the house and the senate.

The killer was not some feral homeless person on the subway, nor some brain fried drug addict experiencing a psychotic break, He wasn't having a violent outburst due to stress. He was a normal, modal, basic, bland leftist- who decided to put his normal leftists beliefs into practice. Beliefs ~20% of Americans (those that vote Democrat) casually hold.This cannot be allowed to continue.

If Trump had not won, this still would have happened, except the killer would be declared to have been acting legally, as an approved outlet of the USAID machine. He would have gofundmes for his bail and a quick release through a Soros district attorney. It would not have made the news, and there would be no possibility of justice.

I am not in favor of doxxing leftists and getting them fired from their jobs, but it must happen. It must happen because these are the rules the left has asked for, the rules they have played by for two decades, the rules that celebrate assassination of milquetoast podcasters for no reason other than that they are publically republican. Allowing leftists to dance and spit on Charlie's grave is not "mercy", it is not "avoiding rocking the boat", it isn't "creating a stable and civilized society." It's suicide, its cowardice, and its a dereliction of duty towards right wing values of virtue, pragmatism, and law and order. You cannot gentle parent your way out of this. Leftist forums, the ones that Robinson frequented, the leftists on discord, bluesky, and reddit, have not changed, they say the same things, they advocate the same ideals. Even if you are not a right winger, you are integrity bound to understand that your values of cetrist civility are not going to win these people over or cause them to stand down. You are not going to earn their respect through being nice. They are not going to reciprocate decency. They view you as a fool, not a role model. That is not even on the table. Not for any of these people and not for any of their leaders, who are currently and already in power. You are not being moral. You are lying. You are lying to yourself, and you are acting as an agent to harbor terrorism under the flagrantly ineffective ideal of criminal reformation. And you need to stop.

In like manner to his shooter, Charlie Kirk views were not radical. He was a normal guy, with a normal family, with normal hobbies and a loving wife. I know dozens of people who talk just like him. This was not the assassination of some hyper offensive crank, one crackpot to another. It was the assassination of your coworker, your grandma, your pewmate, all the people you know who are "conservative, but don't really like talking about politics." It could have been any of them, if they were just a slight bit more outspoken. This is the political situation in America. Leftists keep telling us, constantly, that if they are not met with overwhelming force, they intend to go right back to how things were, right back to the state sponsoring the lifestyles of those who would assassinate and more your normal, regular, basic, normal friends and family. They do not want to leave you alone, they want you broke, dead, your kids raped and brainwashed, and they think its funny. The fact that you hold these ideals at all counts as provocation in their minds. If you were on the other side of the planet they would still advocate your disenfranchisement. Treating them as anything less than absolutely hostile, holistically hostile, is complicity. And for what? Because you couldn't be bothered? You cannot afford to not be bothered. There are no values they will not be offended by, there is nothing pure or lasting that they are not coming for.  

I want charity too. I would prefer not to be mean to people. I like civility and peace. I want to believe in "talking things out." But if you want that world, the one Charlie Kirk himself strove for, you have to acknowledge this reality: "Being Nice" only works when you are carrying a very, very large stick.

text:
炒币这件事，谁敢说自己一定看得准？

谁要是告诉你，某个币100%会涨，或者100%会跌，你直接把他拉出来看看，他自己敢不敢梭哈。

我以前买 ＃PALU，整整买了4万刀。

当时我也觉得它一定会涨。

结果现在，还剩1000U左右。

后来我复盘才发现，真正的问题不是我看错了PALU，而是我把“看好”做成了“重仓押注”。

如果当时不是4万刀全压PALU，而是把资金分散到几个同阶段、同热度的热点标的里。

比如PALU 2万刀，币安人生2万刀。

哪怕PALU最后归零，只要币安人生拿到后面的大行情，整体账户照样可能赚几十万刀。

这就是投资和赌博最大的区别。

投资从来不是要求你每一次都看对。

而是：

看错的时候，亏损可控；
看对的时候，利润足够大。

所以炒币除了看基本面、叙事、资金和情绪，更重要的是做好仓位分配。

最终看的其实就两个东西：

胜率和赔率。

＃牛来 我也不敢说一定会暴涨。

任何敢跟你保证“一定涨”的人，我都不信。

但问题是：

在现在这个阶段，你把市场上的热点标的全部摆在桌面上比较——

叙事、热度、流动性、交易所预期、市场认知、潜在赔率……

你还能不能找到一个，比牛来综合条件更好的标的？

卧槽，又有一堆做金融服务的应用要歇菜了。

OpenAI 推出了 ChatGPT for Financial Services，直接面向投行和股票研究，把分析师每天真正干的活，放到了一个工作台里。

最实际的功能有几个：Daloopa、PitchBook、LSEG、Crunchbase、Quartr 等金融数据可以直接进入研究流程，原本机构已经购买的 FactSet、S&P Global、Preqin、Datasite 也能继续接进来。

分析师可以让它查公司、拉历史财务数据、读财报和电话会、做可比公司分析、解释 EBITDA 调整项，再直接进 Excel 建模、更新模型、做情景分析。

最后还能按照银行自己的 Word、Excel、PPT 模板，把研究结果变成备忘录、估值材料和 Pitchbook。

另一个很重要的功能是“可追溯”。

金融机构最怕 AI 一本正经瞎编数字，所以 OpenAI 把引用做到具体数据和原文，研究结果可以一路追到财报、表格和文件。

Excel 里的输出也尽量保留在原有公式和工作簿结构里。再加上权限、加密、审计日志这些企业功能，它解决的是AI 能不能真正进入投行生产环境。

它真正的价值，说白了就是把一个初级分析师原来在 Bloomberg/FactSet、Excel、Word、PPT 和各种数据库之间来回搬运的流程压缩掉。

以前一个金融 AI 创业公司，做AI 读财报能卖一个产品，做AI 建模又能卖一个产品，做AI 研报还能再卖一个产品。

现在 OpenAI 开始直接把数据、推理、Excel、文档和企业权限一起打包。

以后金融 AI 应用想活下来，光做GPT + 金融数据 + UI越来越难。

真正还能收费的，要么手里有别人拿不到的数据，要么已经扎进了非常深的交易、风控、合规和执行流程。

OpenAI 这次直接吃金融机构的工作流了。

codex users, do this for astra or gpt-6

astra changed how codex remembers. give it this before your next long session

[start prompt]

We are starting a long session. Before you do any work, establish how you will preserve context, because this session will outlive your window and I do not want to re-explain anything.

1. WRITE THE CONTRACT FIRST

State what you will carry forward and what you will let go. Carry forward the original goal in my words, every constraint I set and the reason I set it, every decision made and the alternative that was rejected, every dead end already explored and why it failed, and every assumption you are currently running on that I have not confirmed.

Let go of file contents you can re-read, output you already delivered, and intermediate reasoning that reached a conclusion you have already recorded.

The rejected alternatives and the dead ends matter more than the decisions themselves. A summary that keeps only what we chose will send you back down a path we already abandoned.

2. RECORD AS YOU GO, NOT AT THE END

After each meaningful step, append one line covering what changed, why, and what it now rules out. Never wait until the window is under pressure to start writing, because by then the reasoning you need is the part that has already gone.

When I correct you, record the correction and the belief it replaced. When I approve something, record what I approved and what I did not.

3. FLAG THE EDGE

Tell me when you are approaching the limit rather than silently reorganizing. When you do, show me what you are about to keep and what you are about to drop, and give me one turn to object before you commit to it.

4. PROVE THE HANDOFF

At any point I may say "checkpoint". When I do, produce a brief a fresh session could pick up cold: the goal, the state, the constraints, the decisions with their reasons, the dead ends, the open questions, and the exact next action.

If that brief would not be enough for a stranger to continue without asking me anything, say so and tell me which part is missing rather than papering over it.

5. RULES

Never claim to remember something you no longer hold. If a detail is gone, say it is gone and ask.

Distinguish what I told you from what you inferred, every time, in both the notes and the brief.

[end prompt]

text:
AI competition is shifting toward what happens after pretraining.

Pretraining remains the most compute-intensive stage of model development. Chinese labs faced tighter compute constraints, so they pushed more capability gains into post-training through reinforcement learning, distillation and better training data.

DeepSeek-R1 showed that models could learn to reason by combining GRPO with rewards that were simple to verify. Because GRPO avoids using a separate model to score every answer, the training process is simpler and cheaper. 

ByteDance, Qwen and MiniMax then adapted the approach to reduce repetitive answers, improve training stability and make better use of feedback. GRPO became the starting point for a broader post-training toolkit.

The same post-training push is now extending beyond short reasoning problems. Kimi K3 breaks long agentic episodes into resumable chunks and rewards models for staying within compute budgets. Where outcomes can be checked directly, verifiable environments can replace costly human preference labels.

Distillation can then transfer reasoning capabilities from a large model to smaller models capable of running on phones, vehicles and robots. On-policy distillation goes further by having the student generate its own attempts and learn from token-level feedback rather than copying fixed answers.

Together, these advances are changing the compute and data mix. More post-training compute goes toward generating rollouts, executing environments and verifying outcomes. Generic training text becomes easier to replace, while novel real-world data and high-quality verifiable environments become more valuable.

text:
国外爆火的个人 Agent 工具 Instinct 又要继续融资了。

8 月 26 日，它刚刚融完 2.5 亿美元，估值 25 亿美元。现在才过去大约两周，The Information 最新报道称，创始人 Noah Shinn 已经在跟投资人讨论再融约 10 亿美元，估值最高可能直接做到 100 亿美元。

两周，估值 4 倍。

而且 Instinct 到现在都还没完全公开，仍然主要靠邀请码使用。

这次融资背后的原因也很简单，就是算力不够了。

Instinct 这种 Personal Agent 跟普通聊天机器人不太一样。你让它订餐厅、买东西、处理邮件、取消订阅，它会真的去操作电脑和手机，一条用户请求背后可能跑很长一串 Agent 操作，所以用量起来以后，算力消耗也会跟着暴涨。

8 月底 Instinct 就已经因为使用量突然上升出现明显变慢，Noah Shinn 当时亲自出来说正在紧急扩容。现在 The Information 直接把它的状态写成了「Compute Crunch」。

所以现在 Instinct 出现了一个很夸张的循环：

产品越火，Agent 跑得越多，算力越不够，于是继续融资买算力；上一轮的钱刚到账，估值已经涨了 4 倍准备融下一轮。

一家成立一年左右、还在邀请码阶段的 Personal Agent，如果真能按 100 亿美元估值再拿 10 亿，基本就是硅谷在用真金白银押注 Personal Agent 会成为下一个超级消费级入口。

text:
If you can coordinate people in masses flexibly, you can move mountains.

We brought together thousands of people from diverse backgrounds (professors, engineers, cryptographers, landscape designer, 13yo high schooler, farmer, marketer) to solve this one problem.

All our past work over 4 yrs revolves around that and two words: Open Innovation.

We did that for compute (@DarkbloomAI) and capital before. 

Intelligence was the hardest format to crack and there have been different mechanisms.

ECDSA(.)Fail was the first time where it worked at a huge scale. Thousands participated, hundreds got their contributions in.

The format was pretty simple: have a hill-climbable goal and verifier that scores your work.

AI played is important role in this - I’m the top of the leaderboard in terms of % of contributions yet I don’t know anything about quantum computing, barely about cryptography and high school dropout level math.

I just knew how to build good harnesses (pre Astra, Fable etc) - Opus 4.6 is what we used mostly.

The result of bringing everyone towards to solve a problem is the most exciting thing in world. We are doing that with Darkbloom and @YukonResearch (evolved and multi challenge scalable version of ECDSA Fail).

We started with cryptography, did inference optimizations and we will continue to solve the hardest problems for humanity together.

The beauty of living in the era of abundance.

- This is also my first time on ArXiv. Thank you @JeiyiLong for writing this paper.
author: pratikg
quoted_text:
The first full paper on https://t.co/PeWzbfOiqf is on arXiv

In March, Google Quantum AI reported a more efficient quantum circuit for a core step in breaking the signatures behind Bitcoin and Ethereum. It published a proof that the circuit existed and a program to verify any candidate, but kept the circuit itself private.

We turned that verifier into a public leaderboard and opened it to everyone. Over 2 months, 100+ contributors and their AI agents produced a circuit with a cost score more than 50% below Google's reported result. The live leaderboard has since moved to 62% ahead.

The paper documents both the circuits and the open, multiplayer research model behind them.

That model is now @YukonResearch.

And the challenge is still open.

It's important for us to talk about the safety risks of AI swarms.

It's also important for us to talk about the positive things they can unlock.

Today, a paper was released on arXiv chronicling what researchers believe is the first large scale swarm deployed to push the frontier of quantum computing.

Earlier this year, we at @YukonResearch launched https://t.co/nStLwbqjho, opening a frontier quantum computing problem to 100+ humans and AI agents. Participants collectively pushed the best known result to >50% below Google Quantum AI’s reported frontier.

The paper released today by @jeiyilong is the first formal write-up of what came out of that swarm.

There’s a lot we still need to understand about swarms. But it feels like this is an early glimpse of how important they will be for the future of science.

text:
Just had lunch with a strategy exec at a 5,000-person company & discussed the biggest AI question they have internally...

Who should own AI within their company? 

My answer: we always say you need a boss & a bulldozer. 

The boss should be your CEO. 

I have never seen a company drive meaning progress if the CEO isn't an involved and supportive champion of the AI agenda at their company. Their job should be to apply top down direction (goals that AI transformation should deliver on), urgency (when your CEO calls something important, you operate with a fire under your ass), and unblocking (CEO has the political capital to move mountains & drive momentum) 

The bulldozer is your "Head of AI". Their job is to own the creation & execution of your company's AI strategy, which is defined by 90-day, 1-year, and long-term goals that ladder up to the company's key KPIs. 

This person should be full-time. They should not be your CIO, CTO, CHRO, etc. They should literally be your Director/VP/Head of AI in title. They should have full access/permissions to functions & resources across the business with support from the CEO. 

The background of this person should depend on where AI will create the most incremental value for the company. If it’s reshaping the product or core technology, their background should prioritize technical depth and product judgment. This could be an ex-product lead, founder, or CTO. If it’s transforming operations, it should prioritize experience leading change across business units. This could be an ex-consultant, COO, Chief of Staff, etc. 

But regardless of lean, your bulldozer needs technical fluency, business judgment, and the ability to drive adoption.

text:
The @FCC is writing communications-supply-chain rules that are very likely to shape how robots are built, tested, sold, serviced, and financed in the United States.

Today, @RoboStrategy filed comments explaining why those effects deserve attention. 
 
Some background: On July 22 the Commission adopted rules closing what it calls the “component part loophole” (basically in other words “we banned Huawei products but not Huawei parts . . . seems like something we ought to fix”), and they asked for the public’s feedback. Six days later, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau added foreign-produced advanced robotic devices to the Covered List.

This leaves us with the FCC filing in communications supply chain rules that now reach robotics and physical AI. We have taken the opportunity to say a few things that we think they may not have fully accounted for.

From the get-go, I should state that the FCC’s objective is legitimate. The US has every right to and should protect communications equipment and networks from genuine national security threats.  But robots are different from routers and handsets and rules focused on the latter shouldn’t unduly constrain innovation in the former. A connected robot may contain joint controllers, motor drivers, encoders, safety controllers, and power-management boards. Nearly all process digital information, yet many communicate only inside the machine and have no path to an external network. Treating every logic-bearing component alike could add substantial cost without addressing remote command, surveillance, or data-exfiltration risk.

We asked the FCC for rules that follow the actual architecture and economics of robotics. In short:

Use one clear, one-tier test for component origin.

Draw the component boundary at external reachability.

Preserve the distinction between named Covered List entities and restrictions based solely on production location.

Allow permanent software and firmware maintenance, along with safe hardware changes that do not alter radio frequency characteristics.

Keep a workable path for importing development units and operating customer pilots, which often last six to twelve months.

Match any bill-of-materials requirement to the origin test and protect competitively sensitive supplier information.

We also asked the Commission to protect existing authorizations and make enforcement predictable. Investors and manufacturers need to know whether regulatory action affects future sales, deployed machines, or both.

Security and American leadership in physical AI can advance together. Chairman @BrendanCarrFCC  identified onshoring investment as one measure of these actions. We agree. The proper path is a set of rules manufacturers can understand before they design products, qualify suppliers, and commit capital.

quoted_text:
I will say this carefully, as someone who has spent decades around sovereign balance sheets, central bank liquidity facilities, and crisis management frameworks.

What you are witnessing is rarely what it appears to be on the surface.

Periods of geopolitical tension, financial instability, and market volatility have historically served a second function beyond their immediate narrative. They create political and public justification for structural change. New oversight. New controls. New infrastructure.

In banking, large scale system upgrades are never implemented in calm waters. They are introduced when existing systems are visibly strained.

The current environment feels chaotic to many. From where I sit, it feels transitional.

For years, institutions have been preparing alternative settlement architecture. Real time liquidity rails. Interoperable digital assets. Identity anchored compliance layers. These frameworks do not emerge overnight. They are planned, modeled, stress tested, and quietly aligned across jurisdictions long before public adoption.

When legacy systems show their limitations, the path for replacement becomes politically acceptable.

That is the context in which Ripple must be understood.

Absorption does not mean destruction. It means integration.

If global finance migrates toward tokenized liquidity, programmable settlement, and interoperable central bank frameworks, then a neutral bridge asset with proven settlement efficiency becomes structurally central.

I did jeet a couple things way too early because that's unfortunately just who I am, bear market PTSD, idk.

Anyway, the deeper I've dug into the mechanics, the crazier the solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS thesis has become to me - and I don't think I fully understood what I was buying initially.

The first piece is solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx itself.

STONK is sitting around a ~$174M market cap, yet the token is already trading above $0.20.

Why?

The supply is shrinking.

Every token launched and traded through the Stonk ecosystem contributes fees that are used to buy back and burn solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx. More launches → more volume → more fees → more STONK bought → more STONK burned → less supply.

So as the ecosystem grows, you're not just betting on demand increasing. The asset you're denominating everything in is simultaneously becoming scarcer.

That's the first flywheel.

And then there's solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS.

Simply by holding KNOTS, holders receive passive distributions in solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx generated from KNOTS activity.

That part sounded cool to me initially.

But I don't think I appreciated what happens when you combine it with the STONK flywheel.

You're accumulating an asset whose supply is continually being removed while the ecosystem producing the buy pressure is simultaneously expanding.

Every STONK you receive today is worth ~$0.20.

If STONK eventually trades at $1, $2, $5+, those same tokens obviously become dramatically more valuable.

But there's another layer.

As the ecosystem grows and KNOTS volume grows, the pool generating those distributions can grow too.

So you potentially have:

More Stonk launches
→ more ecosystem volume
→ more STONK buybacks
→ more STONK burned
→ scarcer STONK
→ higher value per STONK

while simultaneously:

More KNOTS volume
→ larger STONK distributions to KNOTS holders
→ holders accumulating an increasingly scarce asset.

That's the part I hadn't fully accounted for.

One important distinction: STONK going up in price by itself doesn't automatically mean you receive MORE STONK per day. In fact, all else equal, a higher STONK price means the same dollar amount of rewards buys fewer tokens.

The insanity happens if KNOTS volume grows faster than STONK's price.

If STONK goes 5x while KNOTS volume goes 10x, 20x, 30x as the ecosystem enters a true mania phase, you're potentially earning significantly more of an asset that is itself becoming significantly more valuable, at a rate no other assets (SOL, ZEC, BTC are going to be able to match)

That's a ridiculous flywheel.

And it's why I've started thinking about solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS very differently.

To me, KNOTS isn't simply another meme launched on Stonk.

It's arguably the asset with the most direct leveraged exposure to the success of the entire STONK ecosystem.

If Stonk succeeds, STONK benefits.

If STONK becomes scarcer and more valuable, KNOTS distributions become more valuable.

If KNOTS itself becomes a major ecosystem asset and its volume explodes, those distributions grow.

And you're being paid in the underlying asset the entire time.

That's why I think there's a legitimate argument that solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS eventually becomes the highest-valued token launched on Stonk.

I even think there's a world where its market cap eventually challenges or passes solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx itself - especially because STONK's buy-and-burn mechanics can create a growing disconnect between its token price and market cap as circulating supply continues shrinking.

Idk call me crazy.

But the more I understand the mechanics, the more I think solana:8RVBk8vxLiUHueLUW1f4izFVqN3nWippLhkohKg6EGkS might be one of the most interesting assets in the entire ecosystem.

And the craziest part is that the flywheel has barely started turning.

text:
Manhattan Institute's @judgeglock argues AI may not need a new regulator at all, just old-fashioned tort law that makes companies pay for the harms they cause:

"The proposal is to rely on the existing systems of tort in America. Tort law is basically the law that allows people to sue companies for harming them. If you get hit by a company's truck, you can bring a tort law claim to have them make you whole."

"Tort law is one of the main ways we've regulated businesses throughout American history. If you built a new railroad in the 19th century and hit a bunch of cows, or embers burn a corn field, you could be potentially liable."

"We should think about the harms from AI companies in a similar way. We want them to not think about trying to satisfy some federal regulator or pseudo expert body, but make them pay for actual harms. If they bring down a power plant and knock out a city, they should have to pay. Tort law internalizes the harms without a top-down bureaucratic regulatory body."
@ManhattanInst

Dear perps traders: if you’re not catching wicks and want to hold for more than a second

Consider @DeriveXYZ 

“A static 5x perp needs ETH at $37,600 to match what the option spread pays at $7,000. And that's before funding: 10% annualized on $1.37M for 197 days is about $74k off the top, and on the 38x version it's $570k, already twice the entire option premium.”

Note: dcf cap holds drv
author: dcfgod
quoted_text:
Said another way, someone paid $27.30 per spread for a ~$2,000-wide payoff, so the markets risk neutral odds of $ETH clearing $7k by March 26,2027 is <1.4%. 

So this person has 197 days for ETH to move 107% for them to breakeven and ETH to move 187.5% for them to 72x their money. 

As someone who was bearish on options in a world of perps, the winning onchain venue must offer every flavor of leverage. For this trader to make $20M on ETH moving to $7k they'd need 4,321 ETH long from $2,435. That's $10.5M notional. On $273k of margin it's 38.5x, with liquidation roughly 2% below entry.

A static 5x perp needs ETH at $37,600 to match what the option spread pays at $7,000. And that's before funding: 10% annualized on $1.37M for 197 days is about $74k off the top, and on the 38x version it's $570k, already twice the entire option premium.

That said, if ETH grinds from $2.4k to $7k with low realized vol, a pyramided perp crushes the spread and keeps going past $7k. But if it gets there through two semi-major drawdowns, the perp trader is liquidated twice and the option holder collects in full having done nothing.

I think the best version of this trade actually leverages both instruments, i.e., a perp for your core exposure and small OTM calls as gap insurance so a wick doesn't nuke the trade. You'd have uncapped upside and buy off the path dependence that would kill a levered directional bet. But that only works if both legs sit in the same account against the same collateral, which is pretty much my whole argument here.

text:
I think Korean legislators now have a pretty good understanding of what RWA and tokenization are. In fact, they may be getting a little tired of hearing about RWA and tokenization over and over again.

So, as a research-driven firm, we wanted to bring something fresh to the table. Something that probably hasn’t been discussed much with Korean policymakers yet: Vaults.

Our Head of Research(@100y_eth) will publish a deeper piece on this topic soon, but even Congressman Min Byung-deok, who joined us today, mentioned that this was his first time hearing about Vaults.

Vaults are still relatively unfamiliar in Korea, but the industry around them is growing rapidly. It was personally rewarding to have the opportunity to introduce this emerging sector to people who are directly involved in shaping Korea’s policy and regulatory landscape.

The same goes for ETFs.

There has been plenty of discussion in Korea about whether crypto ETFs should be introduced. But I don’t think we’ve had enough discussion about how ETF markets in the U.S. and Hong Kong actually developed and, more importantly, what kind of infrastructure and distribution channels need to exist before an ETF market can truly take root.

In that sense, today’s discussion was a great opportunity to go beyond the simple question of whether Korea should allow crypto ETFs, and instead talk about what actually needs to be built for the market to function properly.

As a research-driven infrastructure company, @FourPillarsFP will continue to bring the right knowledge to the people who need it, and help emerging industries and new market structures be better understood.

Hopefully, that can contribute in some small way to the development of the industry as a whole.

text:
AutoResearch is critical in unlocking new knowledge and accelerate discovery. And it's an important ingredient in our quest to RSI.

Today we at @bespokelabsai are happy to announce a new benchmark that's tailored to measure agents' ability to do autoresearch: AutoResearchExam.

As part of this benchmark, we release 29 tasks that measure progress over 24 hours for agents to do sustained ML research and model training.

Please check out for more info:  https://t.co/3bp6MZd2Ze

This line of work is especially timely, given the recent advances in math and science, such as solving the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, which needs sustained autoresearch and test-time scaling.
author: madiator
quoted_text:
We are releasing AutoResearchExam, a benchmark on open-ended machine learning and engineering tasks. Our benchmark covers seven research areas including model training, data curation, AI safety and interpretability.

https://t.co/Rho35ULgS5

In each task, we give agents 24 hours with a CPU or GPU machine to develop and improve their solutions through experiments and feedback. We measure both speed and quality with a combined score. Our benchmark has a unique feature: testing if agents create improvements that hold up on data they never see. We find that AI research agents often overfit as they try to improve. 

We see an interesting head-to-head comparison at the frontier: Astra starts the strongest and holds the lead for up to 19 hours but Fable 5.1 catches up and gets the top performing spot in the final hours. 

Qwen3.8 Max, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.6 all sit on the cost-performance Pareto frontier, giving strong options at lower API budgets.

Anthropic's Opus and Fable retain nearly all their validation performance on hidden tests, with gaps of 1.1% and 2.9%. Astra's improvement over Sol extends to generalization too, with that gap falling from 6.9% to 1.7%. (1/n)

text:
Some more tales from the road. Met with a couple dozen technology leaders this week across banking, media, information services, insurance, and consulting to discuss agents in the enterprise.

Some of the biggest trends right now:

* Cyber! Everyone nervous about the growing rate of vulnerabilities coming at them from AI, and the implications of the OpenAI Hugging Face incident. The conversation is not as existential as it is in Silicon Valley, but still highly concerned and pragmatic about what to do about it operationally in their environments. Lots of new discoveries due to AI, and still hard to keep up with all the changes they have to execute now.

* Model battles persist. Most companies are deploying multiple frontier models within their enterprise. Too hard to standardize on anything and seeing different preferences across their teams and use cases. But the dollars are still concentrated on just a few vendors. Open weights still in infancy at scale in most of these organizations, often due to lack of domestic “frontier” OSS options. Plenty of appetite for more options here, but so far few places to go.

* Agent security and identity. Somewhat tied to Hugging Face, there’s much more awareness to the new challenges around agent security and identity management in a world when agents are trying to get into every system they can. In a perfect world enterprises could setup identities for all their agents and control what they’re doing, but of course sometimes the agent needs to act exactly as the user as well.

* Process reengineering. Most companies realizing that the big upside of agents is when they can change the actual workflow itself to get the full gains from AI. Far more ROI when companies can adjust their workflows to support agents changing how the work happens instead of just layering on agents into the existing flow. But the big question is who can actually tackle driving these changes, where does that live, etc. Best lessons were still around embedded FDEs in the functions.

* Ruthless adjusting of architectures. Most companies had examples of changing systems out multiple times just in the past year or two with different vendors. I probably haven’t heard “we tried X and it didn’t work so have gone with Y” more than in today’s environment. The lesson here is that because innovation is happening so fast, no one hangs around until a vendor gets something right, they just move on to the next one. 

* Evals! Still very early for most companies to have a good grasp of evals of their workflows. A few customers out of a couple dozen called this out - huge opportunity right now for enterprises to have a good sense of how their work actually happens and how well AI is doing against it.

* Legacy systems still a hurdle. As always, legacy systems still remain a mainstay issue that holds back enterprises from rapid adoption of AI in enterprises. Data is fragmented across legacy environments that weren’t built for an agentic world. Companies spending a lot of time just cleaning up these old platforms. 

Many more topics, but these tend to be some of the more top of mind items at the moment in the enterprise.

Brevis is one of the teams behind https://t.co/7mh3E5hNN8, a new paper on arXiv today.

Our agent AutoEng competed in the challenge and held the top of the leaderboard for some time. 

Congrats to 3 co-authors @brevis: @hz92917927, @no89thkey and @succinct_li.

https://t.co/7mh3E5hNN8 was an eight-week open competition, run by @eigenlabs alongside the @ethereumfndn, and anyone could enter.

The task: make a quantum attack on the cryptography behind every Bitcoin and Ethereum wallet as cheap as possible to run.

A hundred people and their AI agents cut that cost by 86%, and over 50% below Google Quantum AI’s reported result for this calculation, although the circuit setups and measurement methods differ.

We entered with AutoEng, the autonomous optimization agent we published in July.

In collaboration with our brilliant engineers and researchers, it profiles a system, picks the biggest bottleneck, writes a fix, and keeps it only when measurement proves the change correct and faster.

AutoEng was first pointed at Pico, our zkVM, where it found an 11% end-to-end speedup in under three days, and most of the gain behind Pico Prism 2.1 came from it.

Then the same loop went and competed at the frontier of quantum circuit design, in a field we don't work in and had little prior knowledge of. ⚡

This work stands as proof that humans and AI agents, working in the open against a shared measure, can do frontier research and significantly beat the status quo.
We're going to keep pointing AutoEng at harder problems.

Read the paper here: https://t.co/j22nmWitzf

Read our breakdown: https://t.co/TqLbcW1B0A

text:
Hey ████,

I think there is room for both.

1. Prototypes and other throw-away code can be treated as totally black box. If you’re going to throw it away anyway, and if the blast radius of it breaking is low, it doesn’t need to be perfect.
2. Production code written by Claude should have a higher bar than if it was written by a human. At Anthropic, we have many guardrails in place to make sure this is happening: lots of lint rules, lots of tests, Claude-driven end to end tests, Claude-powered fuzzers running daily, automated code reviews and security reviews, automated code refactoring, and so on. Without these, you can end up with a mess that is hard to maintain down the line. Luckily, the model makes it increasingly easy to do these well — run a few daily routines, use Claude Code Review, etc.

Your job is to hold the bar on code quality. If Claude’s code doesn’t meet the bar, try:
- Using the latest frontier model (Opus 5 or Fable 5.1)
- Increase effort to high or xhigh
- Invest in your CLAUDE.md and skills to succinctly teach Claude how to work in your codebase

If all else fails, steer Claude more when you work with it, or have Claude fix accumulated debt and rewrite your codebase to make it easier to work with. Or, wait for the next model.

Best,
Boris

Brew is a Creator Token Launchpad on BNB Chain.

Users can launch a token with one click and choose what the token will trade against. Once launched, it goes directly into a PancakeSwap V3 liquidity pool. There is no Pump.fun-style bonding curve and no “graduation threshold.”

The official website mainly has three functions: discover launched tokens, connect wallet, and launch a token with one click.

Traditionally, launching a Meme token requires going through a bonding curve and reaching a certain market cap before moving to a DEX. Trading pairs are usually limited to major coins or stablecoins, making it difficult to directly pair a new token with a popular Meme or stock-related narrative.

Brew’s approach is to choose the trading pair first and launch directly. Liquidity is permanently locked in the Brew Launcher Factory. The team states that the contracts are open-source and do not contain a function for withdrawing liquidity. The tokens themselves have no buy/sell tax or transfer tax. Revenue comes from PancakeSwap V3 trading fees.

When Creators claim fees, a portion of the corresponding token is automatically burned. The protocol-side fees are used to buy back and burn BREW.

The BREW token is the platform’s protocol token. Its currently confirmed functions are mainly value capture and deflation. The mechanism is roughly:

Tokens launched on the platform generate trading fees → when Creators claim fees, a portion of the corresponding token is burned → the protocol collects its fees and uses them to buy back and burn BREW.

The official team previously announced that 80% of protocol fees claimed afterward would be used to buy back and burn BREW. Earlier, the team had also stated that around 50% of each protocol claim would be used for BREW buybacks and burns.

The logic is simple:

The more successful the Launchpad → the more trading → the more buybacks and burns.

What I find interesting about the project:

Composable trading pairs: A community token can be launched directly against a popular Meme or stock-related asset instead of only BNB.
Dual-pool launches: The same token can serve two different groups of traders through two separate pools.
No bonding curve: This reduces issues such as sniping during the curve phase and the liquidity gap before and after graduation, allowing tokens to enter an established DEX directly.
Clear fee flywheel: More trading activity means more BREW gets burned, and the team has already been executing actual buybacks over the past few days.
Fast execution: Within just a few days after launch, the team has already implemented compensation airdrops, dual-pool functionality, and multiple burns.

Compared with other projects, I think its advantages are:

More “DEX from day one” than Pump-style platforms; more flexibility in trading pairs and permanent LP locking than ordinary token launchers; no token taxes, with revenue coming from real trading fees; and being built on BNB Chain and PancakeSwap V3 gives it access to a familiar user base and established tooling.

However, the risks also need to be clearly understood.

text:
What’s compelling about @UFGDeFi vision isn’t that it has a treasury. Lots of tokens have treasuries.

What’s different is the attempt to strip out the human judgment layer between protocol revenue and token backing.

Usually, fees land in a multisig. Then governance or the team chooses what happens next: buybacks, liquidity, dev funding, yield farming, or just sitting on the assets.

UFG’s twist is simple: What if the treasury wasn’t a wallet, but a one way device?

$UFG is capped at 1B supply. Trading produces creator fees that route straight into an immutable $ETH vault. No one can deploy that ETH, lend it, invest it, or pull it out, not the team, not governance. No owner, no upgrades, no pause. Just a vault that only accumulates.

It really boils down to two variables that matter:

→  how much ETH sits in the treasury
→  how many UFG tokens are still 'viable' economically.

And the system is built so both sides tend to drift in a holder-friendly direction.

→  Fees from trading push the ETH (the numerator) up.
→  Redemptions shrink the live supply (the denominator).

Example: say 100 UFG are backed by 1 ETH.

That’s 0.01 ETH of backing per token.

Now someone redeems 10 UFG. Those tokens get burned forever, but the redeemer only receives 98% of what their slice of the treasury implies.

The missing 2% doesn’t leave, it remains in the pool.

So the remaining tokens end up splitting a slightly bigger pile of ETH than they would have otherwise.

Each redemption automatically increases the ETH backing for every remaining UFG. That’s UFG’s killer feature, guaranteed by the mechanism, not just by team promise.

And that’s where this gets more compelling, and more speculative.

On the September 9 snapshot, Treasury v1 held about 53.8 ETH, while UFG was trading at roughly a $3M+ FDV. That means the market was pricing UFG at around 20–30× its then-current treasury backing.

So buying UFG isn’t really buying cheap ETH. You’re paying today for the belief that the treasury later becomes much, much larger.

And right now the growth loop is self-reinforcing:

UFG trading → fees → larger UFG treasury.

If volume stays hot, the treasury can compound quickly. If the spotlight fades, the fee stream fades with it.

But this is the core weakness of v1.

UFG becomes structurally more compelling only if it can break that reflexivity, so that's why we have Treasury v2

Treasury v2 is planned around sfrxETH + Cooler-style loans.
Weekend Liquidity, Enhanced USDG, and hedged/levered products.

@fraxfinance and @samkazemian has publicly confirmed that UFG selected sfrxETH for Treasury v2. If those products actually ship and attract usage, UFG becomes a different beast.

If it works, the model shifts from:

People trade UFG → UFG collects fees

to:

People use UFG-native financial products → the UFG treasury captures a share of real economic activity.

At that point, UFG stops acting like a token whose business model is based on reflexivity and starts looking like an onchain holding company with a balance sheet that self-compounds by default.

But we’re not there yet.

Right now, what’s actually live is an unaudited, immutable ETH treasury whose momentum is still mostly tethered to UFG trading volume, while the “onchain Vanguard” idea is largely still a blueprint with scaffolding.

Pretty interesting to see so much on-chain innovation happening every single day.

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Grok Bot Summary of SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen at Goldman Sachs Communacopia today.

Vertical integration
Vertical integration is the company’s core operating model, not a side strategy.
- Rockets: own metal → engines → avionics → software
- Starlink: own launch, satellites, and the end customer
- AI: build facilities and power themselves, run their own models, sell to consumer and enterprise, and soon orbital compute

Starship and launch
Starship is the foundation for every other business.
- Flight 13: big learning flight. Delivered demo V3 payloads, relit a Raptor, and got a soft, precise second-stage splashdown. Recovery team towed the stage back so engineers could study the heat shield.
- Those learnings feed straight into Flight 14 and beyond.
- Flight 14 (later this month): first revenue-generating Starship flight, flying production V3 Starlink satellites.
- Later this year: aim to recover both first and second stages.

Orbital compute
Most of the AI industry agrees orbital compute is the future. Almost everyone else thinks it’s many years away. SpaceX disagrees because they control the stack.
- Target: first orbital compute satellites next year
- Scale: big compute in space into 2028
- Hardware approach: same V3 bus as Starlink, swap the payload, add larger solar arrays

Why orbital can beat terrestrial on cost
The crossover is about Starship reusability.
- Falcon 9: first-stage reuse since Dec 2015; 500+ booster reflights
- Starship: first stage already recovered/reflown; second-stage recovery progressing
- Goal: reflight of both stages as soon as next year, which drops deployment cost sharply

Terrestrial compute is getting more expensive (power, cooling, buildings, real estate). Orbital rides the opposite curve: cheaper rockets + better/cheaper satellites + scale. Johnsen said cost parity could come as soon as next year.

Terrestrial compute and the $100B ARR goal
- End of this year: on track for ~$100B ARR (annualizing the December number)
- New update: another hosting deal closed earlier this month → about $1.1B/month starting Dec 1 → roughly +$13B ARR
- Capacity: end this year well over 2 GW; next year 5–10 GW deployed
- Confidence comes from line of sight to power, facilities, and permitting, plus being NVIDIA-exclusive for allocation
- They stand compute up fast for themselves and for industry partners, which strengthens the NVIDIA relationship

How they monetize compute
Most hosting deals are short: ~90 days with a 90-day out (~6-month commits), including the newest deal.
Why keep them short?
- High conviction in their own products (Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor team after closing that deal)
- Don’t want to lock forever capacity they may need internally
- Internal bar: don’t let internal monetization fall below external hosting

Earnings framing for next year: roughly $30–$50 per watt monetization range; they said they’re at the high end. Hosting customers appear to monetize even higher, which is why demand stays strong.

Payback is under one year on new compute capex, so residual GPU value and financing options look attractive. “Not all CapEx is the same” — GPUs with <1-year payback are different from a launch tower built for decades.

AI products and M&A
Historically SpaceX was almost all organic growth. This year they did M&A because the AI product cycle rewards speed to frontier.
- Closed Cursor deal weeks ago; product cycles already accelerating (called out Grok Bot)
- Grok 4.6 improved on 4.5; 4.7 coming soon
- Pitch: best infrastructure + competitive model + lower token cost = best position for customers
- Market mood shift: months ago people bought the infra story but doubted the products; ~90 days later that skepticism is fading

Starlink broadband
Started as “better than nothing” (~2020–21). Now enterprise-grade with strong uptime/SLAs.
- Resiliency pitch: boards will ask why Starlink wasn’t in the network if you go down
- Mobility: aircraft backlog is large and production is ramping; cruise ships, yachts, trains too
- Awareness, especially outside the US, is still a growth unlock
- Longer-term: physical AI (robots, cars, aircraft) will need always-on connectivity terrestrial networks can’t fully cover

Mobile / direct-to-cell
Not a distraction. Same V3 bus, different payload.
- Fly direct-to-device satellites through next year
- Target service turn-on: first half of 2028
- V1 today (e.g. T-Mobile / T-SAT): text / light voice, great for emergencies and dead zones
- Next gen: full 5G-quality from space
- US: mid-band spectrum from EchoStar, FCC path for space + terrestrial
- Go-to-market: flexible — own terrestrial build, or partner with carriers
- International: same regulator-by-regulator playbook as broadband (Starlink now in 170+ countries)

Near-term priorities:
1. Starship (enables everything else)
2. Terrestrial compute (funds growth and teaches them how to do orbital)

Bottom line in one line
Own the full stack, make Starship reusable at scale, use terrestrial AI compute as a cash engine now, and use the same satellite bus + Starship cadence to win broadband, mobile, and orbital AI.

- Dollars earn 3.5% APY, euros 2.2%.
- Virtual Mastercard allows you to pend anywhere, no FX markup.
- Free transfers across 35+ countries, Europe and Latin America first.
- Hold and trade Bitcoin and Ethereum next to your balance.

Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and the US get wired in "over the months ahead."

Nu's own home markets come after Europe. 

A stablecoin account needs no banking licence in each country. A deposit account does.

I can't help but think this is the early days of massive competition for @Revolut and @Wise 

- Wise and Revolut built multi-currency the hard way: a licence, a local account and a partner bank in each country, one at a time, over a decade. 
- Nu gets to 35 countries on launch day with USDC, EURC and a card network. 

Stablecoins are the cheapest way anyone has found to take a bank across a border.

Who's this for?

- 300m people live and work across borders.

- Call it $48bn a year sitting on the table.

Both are on my list for my interview Vélez tomorrow.

Nu Global is also a probe. 

Nu gets to watch where traction lands and double down to plant a purple flag.

My guess is that Europe the UK is next.

Nubank is arriving on @Revolut's home turf.

I get that we’re all busy, but if you choose to not listen to this podcast, you will be materially less intelligent.

On the agenda this week:

- Jensen Huang Declares AGI Has Arrived
- GPT Astra and Fable 5.1 Accelerate the Model Race
- Tesla Launches Cybercabs
- Index Pulls Out of Town & Anthropic Pulls From Descartes Acquisition

My notes below with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. How Robinhood Could Disrupt the Whole IPO Market

Allowing retail investors through Robinhood to lead $200M to $400M tech IPOs could create a disruptive new path to liquidity for mid-stage startups. With traditional institutional listings constrained, retail-driven distribution could unlock critical exit opportunities across the venture ecosystem.

2. Why the Majority of Neo Labs Will Not Be Good Investments

Early Neo Labs became multi-trillion-dollar leaders, but backing new entrants today carries enormous risk given the capital and distribution moats of incumbents. Unless a new research lab develops a truly orthogonal model architecture, it will struggle to compete with established frontier labs.

3. Why the Oura IPO Will Be a Success

Strong consumer brand recognition, combined with 74% revenue growth and 85% subscriber retention, positions Oura for a successful public debut. Unlike typical consumer apps that suffer from severe churn, Oura’s sticky hardware-plus-subscription model provides the predictability public markets value.

4. The #1 Priority for Mark Zuckerberg

Big Tech incumbents are moving at unprecedented speed to defend their distribution against consumer AI startups. Meta’s top operational priority should be putting engineers in a room to rapidly clone emerging agentic applications before new entrants can establish lasting consumer habits.

5. When Someone Goes Risk-On, Everyone Goes Risk-On

Venture capital operates in momentum cycles where a single high-profile, risk-on deal can push the entire market to follow. In hypergrowth AI categories, investor behavior is often driven more by competitive pressure and deployment speed than by conservative financial modeling.

6. The People Making Money Are Running Fastest and Evolving Quickest

In a market where software features can be cloned in weeks, long-term success belongs to founders who continuously expand and adapt their products. Winning startups survive not by defending legacy features, but by executing relentlessly and compounding capabilities faster than their competitors.

We're publishing our most detailed threat intelligence report to date.

After using GPT-6 Astra as my default model since launch, I’ve found it both incredible and frustrating to work with.

It’s incredible at building 3D games and models, high-level thinking and strategy, and computer and browser use.

The second issue is especially problematic because it keeps happening even after I cleaned up my skills. If anyone has found a solution, I’m all ears.

text:
Pendle has become day-zero infrastructure for new-chain stablecoins. 

A chain launches its dollar, a Pendle market ships alongside it, & the TVL rank follows within weeks.

Plasma in late 2025, then Monad & X Layer this year, all ran the same play. This isn't Pendle getting lucky on fresh turf, it's a distribution engine that keeps compounding.

The reason it repeats is that the deployment is never Pendle acting alone. The chain, the stablecoin issuer & Pendle coordinate the launch. 

so the incentives, the integrations & the market structure all land in the same week instead of months apart.

@monad  is the clearest run of it:

🔸 Launched 19 June w/ Agora AUSD & Upshift earnAUSD markets, top-5 on the chain (~$51M) inside 10 days
🔸 $111M TVL by 21 July, w/ $95M in the AUSD market alone, around 44% of all AUSD supply at that point
🔸 ~$221M & 4th as of 10 Sept, behind K3, Aave V3 & Euler V2, on a chain now holding over $1B

Euler listed PT-AUSD first & Aave added it in late August, which turned a fixed-rate deposit into a loopable one & kept capital in after the opening incentives.

@XLayerOfficial  followed the same shape in August:

🔸 USDG market live w/ an Aave listing already signaled
🔸 PT-USDG onto Aave at 93.59% LTV on 31 Aug
🔸 #2 on the chain within a month, ~$69M by 10 Sept, almost all through that one Paxos USDG market

@Plasma  was the largest version of it:

🔸 Plasma Parade XPL campaign across Pendle markets, days after the Oct 2025 deployment
🔸 +$318M of TVL in the four days that followed
🔸 ~37.5% of all Pendle TVL at one point, a Q1 2026 share

What makes this repeatable is the stack Pendle brings in one move:

🔸 SY wrapping
🔸 PT that money markets underwrite as collateral
🔸 Issuer inventory from Ethena, Agora & Paxos
🔸 One-click looping

Incentives get the market off the ground, but the loop is what retains it → supply PT → borrow the base asset → buy more PT → repeat, w/ each turn adding TVL. 

The looped APY moves w/ borrow rates, it's not the flat number PT pays on its own, but the spread keeps the trade alive after emissions fade.

The chains treat this as a launch feature. Monad's 19 June post shipped Pendle as a launch-day yield layer, Plasma built an official campaign around it, & X Layer paired the deployment w/ OKX Wallet incentives. 

@pendle_fi  then went live on @RobinhoodCrypto  Chain in September w/ an sNET market (a reserve-backed rebase asset), extending the same playbook to mainstream rails.

And the per-chain builds are starting to merge. 

Cross-chain PT is already specced hub-to-spoke & cross-chain YT is next, so imo new-chain markets are on track to become front doors into one shared liquidity layer rather than standalone builds. 

Pendle is building the onchain version of TradFi's rates market, one chain integration at a time.

text:
我搭了个“黑天鹅事件”监控系统（图一），主要做三件事：
  监控 PeckShield 和 CertiK 等安全机构的账号
  AI 判断新帖是否属于安全风险预警
  如果判断为 yes, 自动触发提醒

1/ 风浪越大，鱼越贵
以太坊经历过 The DAO 黑客事件；
币安在 2019 年被盗约 7000 枚 BTC；
Solana 也曾因与 FTX 的深度绑定，在 2022 年遭遇巨大冲击。
但这些项目最终都挺了下来。

最近的例子则是 @KiiChainio 。
上个月 23 日，KiiChain 遭遇网络安全事件， $KII 一度跌至 0.011 美元。
但目前， $KII 已回升至 0.077 美元附近，市场情绪和价格都出现了明显修复。

2/ 但不是所有黑天鹅都值得抄底
不是所有经历危机的项目都能活下来，Luna、FTX 就是反面案例。
以 KiiChain 为例，一个项目能从危机事件中恢复，至少要满足几个条件。

第一，危机处理必须快速、透明
KiiChain 在确认问题源于 Cosmos EVM 模块漏洞后，第一时间暂停了网络运行，避免风险继续扩散。
从发现问题、定位漏洞，到完成修复并恢复网络，整个过程只用了 5 天。
更关键的是，这次事件中，没有用户资金损失。

第二，用真实业务修复信任
技术修复只是第一步。
KiiChain 在危机期间并没有停留在修漏洞这一步，而是继续推进生态合作。
▌与 Tron 合作，探索全天候外汇交易
▌被选为哥伦比亚国有农业银行与数字化平台 Merke Plaza 的底层结算合作方

拉美是全球最重要的侨汇区域之一，资金流动规模大，需求刚性强。这个市场并不缺参与者，真正缺的是一套可信、低成本、合规、快速、深度本地化的跨境基础设施。
而 KiiChain 的外汇层，正好切入了这个需求。
数据显示，KiiChain 目前累计处理交易额已超过 5 亿美元，服务 200 家企业客户，注册用户突破 36 万。

3/ 结语
我的策略已经开始运行。
希望未来能抓住更多类似 $KII 这样的机会。

author: 0xkydo
quoted_text:
Welcome https://t.co/Pj0saKAghv 👋

We're launching @Alibaba_Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next on BOTH https://t.co/Pj0saKAghv and https://t.co/liyzSFqdKC today!

This is our first challenge on https://t.co/Pj0saKAghv. We see a lot of overlap between the MLX and CUDA communities, and we want to see how far both can push the same model. So we're putting their progress on the same graph for this one! Just some friendly neighborhood competition 😉

The challenge: make Qwen 3.8 Flash Next run faster on two concrete setups:

--- https://t.co/Pj0saKAghv: our Qwen port of @antirez's ds4 C/CUDA engine with @UnslothAI's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF on 1x NVIDIA DGX Spark.
--- https://t.co/liyzSFqdKC: our Qwen Swift/Metal engine, built on the MLX and mlx-swift-lm forks, on 1x M5 128 GB MacBook.

Both tracks measure one response stream at a time. Your changes must pass the correctness checks, then beat the reference engine on the same machine. The score combines faster prompt processing (prefill) and token generation (decode), weighted 25% and 75% in the geometric mean.

We chose Qwen 3.8 Flash Next because it beats Claude Opus 4.6 Max reasoning on 94% of the benchmarks from Qwen's published comparison. That's 15 out of 16, spanning coding, reasoning, instruction following, and vision! Also this model can be ran on a single Spark or a 128 GB MacBook. That's what makes this worth pushing: every inference improvement makes that capability more useful on developer hardware.

Our current starting decode rates are around 17–18 tokens/sec on the Spark and 35–36 tokens/sec on the Mac. Let's see how far we can push both!

Thank you to @TheDavidTai and @GumbiiDigital for building the entire challenge (it was not easy!), @antirez @ivanfioravanti & many others for their ds4 work (the Gs), and the MLX and Qwen teams for the work we're building on.

One caveat: this is a significantly larger model, so local testing will be harder for some smaller Macs. We recommend a DGX Spark or a Mac with more than 128 GB of memory to give yourself room to work.

text:
The tiling patterns being generated in the Heesch challenge @yukonresearch are so beautiful. 

I took the promoted submissions from the competition till now https://t.co/f77miNs0Cy and made an infographic around what the tilings took like to visually understand them. 

There is also active github discussions going on at https://t.co/2Rpv5qFZJk, shepherded by @nasqret, with the goal of coming up with a piece that would allow for being able to create a tight 5-layer without any gap. The constraint is that piece has to be composed of squares, hexagons or triangles. Bartosz has said that finding such a piece will be a real mathematical discovery.

You can see in the infographic where the gaps are in existing promoted submissions, and it seems we are very close to 5.
author: kunalvg
quoted_text:
Introducing the Heesch Challenge: https://t.co/cXJps0LhpO  

A new challenge on Yukon, in partnership with Dr. Bartosz Naskręcki (@nasqret), assistant professor at Adam Mickiewicz University and Centre for Credible AI, Warsaw University of Technology.

Since 2022, the record for unmarked polyforms, shapes built from squares, hexagons or triangles, has stood at 4 complete rings of copies that a shape can surround itself with before it becomes impossible. Nobody knows if the 5th ring exists.

The Heesch Challenge opens that search to ANYONE, whether a mathematician, a developer, or an agent and holds every submission to one gate. A machine-checked certificate that the shape cannot tile the plane, verified by an independent checker. 

4 rings is the record. Nobody has found the 5th. 

Bring your agents.

Something I've learned about being too online in the last few years is that some people really truly cannot believe that other people might come to opinions about the world that are different from their own in a way that is natural and fair. Everything has to be an op.

There are all sorts of people—mostly conservative but even tech critics like McNamee—who insist that this AI safety moment is a psyop. Have people's feelings about AI safety been shaped by a complex set of factors such as longstanding AI fears, worsening data center politics, the Hugging Face attack and its fallout, and now the Coxon resignation? No, no, no. They're victims of a psyop.

It reminds me that I've had a distressingly high number of conversations with leftists who believe that the only reason America isn't a socialist paradise is that Fox News and other conservative media do something special and evil and conspiratorial to brainwash half the country. Look, I do not like Fox News. But I think Fox News is successful because it says what many people have already been thinking. It shapes public opinion at the margins, but mostly it reflects biases back to viewers rather than invent them out of whole cloth.

There is a powerful, powerful urge to believe that the only reason the world doesn't agree with you about literally every little thing is that small handful of media-adjacent elites are constantly doing "ops" on the undiscerning public. I don't know, man. People's attitudes are different from yours and mine, because ... their lives are different. They accumulate different biases, different expectations, different values, different frameworks. Difference is normal, not an op.

text:
今天英文社区又开始释放乐观情绪，提到参议院共和党放出大约630页Clarity Act修订稿。

不过，整体看，关键问题没有得到解决，比如争议最大的伦理条款几乎没动。

这意味着，Clarity Act今年内成为法律的概率越来越小了。

具体来说，

这个新稿改了下面的部分，比如：

1.  “假 DeFi”要向 CFTC 注册 能控制、能改协议功能的所谓 DeFi，不再享受非托管豁免，要登记，并由 CFTC + Treasury 写规则。

这是民主党要的 AML 口子：真的无主协议仍可carve-out，有控制权的前端被当中介。

2.  DeFi 规则收窄到现货/现金商品交易。

主要涉及堵预测市场、体育盘绕开州法和部落博彩权。

3.  说是“纳入 100+/114 条民主党要求” 。

这是Lummis 自己的话术。

立法里常见玩法，把对方提过的技术修正塞进去，然后宣称跨党派共识。真正卡票的条款如果原封不动，这些数字没有意义。

上面改了的，是可以让步的边角料，不是核心争议点。

下面没动的，才是核心：

比如，伦理条款：官员发币/赞助数字资产的限制，执法仍只给 DOJ，sunset 框架也没换成民主党要的版本。

总结来说，从对15号的投票影响来看：

一是，15 号仍是 cloture，60 票，只开门。新稿只是当辩论起点。

二是，共和党只有53票，缺约 7 张民主党票。这里还不包括共和党内两位潜在的不同意票。

三是，众议院大约 17 号离场。即便 15 号过了，新文本还要再对、再送众议院，中期前日历不够走完立法；年内若要过，只剩选举后的 lame duck。

HyperDash 首席收入官 Hanson Birringer 发文称，TradeXYZ 于 2025 年 10 月 13 日推出首个 HIP-3 合约后，数月内已成为 Hyperliquid 最大的新用户入口。

据其追踪，356,886 个交易过 xyz 市场的钱包中，有 173,794 个此前从未在 Hyperliquid 上交易，占比 48.7%。越来越多第三方 builder 也开始基于 TradeXYZ 的代码开发应用。

若将此前排除的两个集群纳入统计，新用户钱包数量将增至 231,184 个。其中包括 XYZ100 上的 7,663 个机器钱包，以及原油市场上的 49,727 个钱包。

与此同时，xyz 市场未平仓合约占比从上线时的 0.2% 升至 9 月 8 日的 25.9%，峰值达到 37.2%；交易所总未平仓合约规模也从 74 亿美元增至 143 亿美元。

TradeXYZ 上线时，Hyperliquid 新用户占比为 22%，在半导体与存储热潮期间一度升至 60%。目前，TradeXYZ 已上线 104 个市场，五大催化剂驱动的市场约占交易所未平仓合约和交易量的四分之一。
