text:
Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2: Orchestrating the Pareto Frontier

The AI industry has spent a decade optimizing along a single axis: build bigger, more expensive models. But intelligence has never been a monolith. It is a collective, distributed system. Humanity itself is a collective intelligence.

We built Sakana Fugu on this conviction: the most powerful AI systems will not be isolated giants, but collaborative ecosystems that learn to coordinate. Evolution innovates under constraints, and the future belongs to systems that know not just how to solve a problem, but which machinery to deploy for the lowest possible cost.

Today we are releasing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2.

Fugu Max expands the Pareto frontier outward, orchestrating our largest pool of open and specialized models to deliver frontier-grade results at a fraction of the token spend. Fugu Ultra v2 pushes that frontier upward, achieving peak performance on complex multi-step tasks without depending on the very frontier models it competes against.

Together, they show that orchestration does not force a choice between cost and performance. It can push both at the same time, advancing the Pareto frontier.

Relying on a single company’s model for critical infrastructure is a massive risk. As recent export controls have shown, access can disappear overnight. Collective intelligence is the practical hedge against this concentration of power. An orchestration system simply routes around vendor restrictions by relying on an entirely swappable agent pool.

I am incredibly proud of our team for shipping this. By orchestrating the world’s models, we are building the resilient infrastructure required for AI sovereignty.

Try Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2: https://t.co/yQZMyx8v21
Read the full release: https://t.co/zTCbDw9xyR 🐡

The Fugu orchestration system evolved with model resiliency in mind. It does not rely on individual frontier models to deliver frontier output. Fugu Max expands the Pareto frontier outward. Fugu Ultra v2 pushes it upward. Orchestration does not force a choice between cost and capability. It advances both simultaneously.

Can we throw out Jevons Paradox and replace it with something more in line with how it’s actually used now? (Aka the paradox of “how can my AI stocks go down when I don’t want them to”)

In all seriousness, there’s a perception among too many that it is somehow impossible for stocks to go down while AI models get better. That’s before you get into the people who seem to skip the step of actually understanding anything and just go “this is the AI stock I own and I am bullish on AI so when AI improves then my stock needs to go up” with zero critical thinking involved. 

I’m all for having conviction, I spent the better part of a year being called an stock pumping idiot by half the people I interacted with because I believed AI would be the biggest trend of our lifetime… (try telling someone that lost 60% being long AMAT, who’s convinced a recession is around the corner, that actually this new chatbot is going to result in higher semicap demand). 

But…have some humility too, please…

If your thesis revolves around an exponentially improving technology, maybe your prior relying on everything else staying static is something worth revisiting.

text:
I can’t stress enough how little an idea matters compared to the agency of the people executing the idea. 

I have had the privilege of knowing and sometimes even working with some of the most successful people (by various metrics).

The difference between mediocre and excellent work and outcomes is predominantly one of agency. 

In practice this means: they dont wait for things to happen to them they go out and make things happen for them.

They don’t wait for someone else to do something, for someone to teach them, for someone to give them the path, etc. They just go out and find a way to do it.

I think the single biggest superpower these people have is the realization/belief that the world around them is completely mutable. Most everything that happens is because a person made it happen.

I used to tell people to look around the room you’re sitting in. Look at everything. Every noun. It almost all exists because a person willed it into existence. Nothing is stopping you from doing the same. 

I see people online all the time dismissing someone else’s success because “I had that idea first” or whatever. I mean… yeah? If so then the difference is… you. So a bit of a self own whenever I hear that.

Number one tip: act with agency.

Consumers let their personal agent make purchases when they trust that it has their best interests in mind.
Pushing people towards their personal ambitions is a great way to start building that trust among everyday people: purchasing items as aspirational as a textbook earns the right to purchase items as mundane as toilet paper.

We’re partnering with Stripe so that tomosapiens can approve purchases directly through Link, further closing the gap between aspiration and action for real people.

quoted_text:
For the first time ever, a fruit fly brain has been trained to launch a memecoin.

Not "AI inspired by a brain" — the real connectome. 165,122 neurons, 10,228,000 synaptic connections, every one traced from an actual male Drosophila by electron microscopy. Janelia FlyEM + Google Research, released CC-BY.

How it works:
Screenshots of the live launchpad go in through 892 retinotopic hex columns into L1 and L2 — the neurons sitting directly behind a fly's photoreceptors. All 165,122 integrate. The cursor comes back out of the descending neurons a fly actually walks with: DNa02's left-right asymmetry steers, DNa01 drives forward, DNp09 clicks.

The wiring is never trained. Only synaptic gains — you don't get to invent connections the fly doesn't have.
Proof its eye is doing real work: in light mode it filled 0 of 3 form fields. In dark mode, 2 of 3. Its retina is a luminance map, so invert the contrast and it goes blind.

And the honest split: the fly types the description and the ticker. The rig does the name, the pair and the tax.

1. 宏观政策与通胀：美联储口惠而实不至
美联储虽坚称抗通胀至 2.0% 的目标，但“只说不做”，面对毫无隐忧的就业市场却迟迟不采取行动。受地缘冲突和商品指数飙升的影响，年内核心 CPI 很难跌破 3.5%。冈拉克预测美联储为了挽回信誉，可能会被迫在 9 月份选择加息。

2. 债市与财政：长端美债遭遇结构性抛售
由于美国面临极其严重的财政赤字，且社会保障资金预计在未来几年（2029-2032年）加速枯竭，市场的“债市哨兵”正在用脚投票。发布会期间收益率曲线剧烈陡峭化，30年期美债收益率正式破位冲高，他预言长端利率很快会迈向 5.5% 左右。

3. 信用风暴风险：全面避开杠杆与C级资产
非公开信贷（Private Credit）和私募股权（PE）市场中积攒了过多的杠杆。市场上出现大量评级欺诈，名义上 BBB- 的新债在二级市场瞬间以 B 级或 CCC 级打折交易。底层 CCC 级资产与 BB 级利差显著拉大，意味着违约和踩踏风险即将来临，投资应实行“零杠杆”，全面对 C 级资产空仓。

4. 股票投资反思：远离市值加权的“动量陷阱”
当前的被动投资市场存在巨大的盲目性，加速纳入指数等新规让被动资金变成了 SpaceX 等科技巨头创始人的套现工具。他极力推荐投资者放弃传统的市值加权基金，转向等权重（Equal-weighted）标普500指数投资以防被高估值科技股“拽落悬崖”。

5. 外汇与实操：长线看跌美元，配置中短期高质债
虽然地缘风险短期支撑美元，但庞大的双赤字注定让美元在未来几年走向贬值，应避开美元多头交易。明天进办公室可立即执行的策略（The X）是：绝不碰长端美债，将资金锁死在 2年期、5年期和7年期的中短期高品质美债中，以求在即将到来的市场风暴中保全资产。

author: eigencloud
quoted_text:
The first full paper on https://t.co/PeWzbfOiqf is on arXiv

In March, Google Quantum AI reported a more efficient quantum circuit for a core step in breaking the signatures behind Bitcoin and Ethereum. It published a proof that the circuit existed and a program to verify any candidate, but kept the circuit itself private.

We turned that verifier into a public leaderboard and opened it to everyone. Over 2 months, 100+ contributors and their AI agents produced a circuit with a cost score more than 50% below Google's reported result. The live leaderboard has since moved to 62% ahead.

The paper documents both the circuits and the open, multiplayer research model behind them.

That model is now @YukonResearch.

And the challenge is still open.

text:
The paper is led by @jieyilong, CTO of @Theta_Network, with coauthors from @ethereumfndn, @StarkWareLtd, @Starknet, @trailofbits, @brevis_zk, @SeiNetwork, @pauli_group, @OctavFi, @sciencevr, @nasqret at Adam Mickiewicz University, and researchers at Warsaw University of Technology and Stanford's Free Systems Lab.

On the comparison, the 2 efforts use different interfaces and accounting conventions, so the paper treats this as a numerical comparison rather than a formal claim.

Craig Gidney and Tanuj Khattar of @GoogleQuantumAI reviewed the manuscript before publication.

Read the full paper on @arxiv: https://t.co/xE8C5qUe5X

“The meme code symbol is MARIO”
“The coin name is SuperMarioBrosCoin”
as well as 100,000,000,000 tokens, etc.

A Meme Token whose name genuinely exists in NVIDIA’s AI training data and has entered the training ecosystem of an NVIDIA model.

There is a powerful, powerful urge to believe that the only reason the world doesn't agree with you about literally every little thing is that small handful of media-adjacent elites are constantly doing "ops" on the undiscerning public. I don't know, man. People's attitudes are different from yours and mine, because ... their lives are different. I'm very worried about changes to AI architectures that result in AIs thinking in opaque activations instead of in chain of thought (aka "neuralese" architectures).

Based on limited public evidence, it seems like Astra was a concerning step in this direction.

Unfortunately, there was insufficient public information to have a well-informed public scientific discussion about whether the changes to architectures and training methods that went into Astra were a good trade-off between monitorability and performance. We also don't know how AI companies will make these trade-offs going forward. I think companies should release the evidence needed for a reasonably informed public conversation about how these trade-offs should be made. They should also make and publish their policies around this. We've written up a proposal for how this could work.

I don't know if this proposal will be sufficient to avoid the most concerning architectures, but it seems like a relatively robust step in the right direction. AI companies should be very cautious about pursuing architectures that could eliminate or greatly reduce dependence on chain of thought, and certainly shouldn't do this before the rest of the world has a chance to discuss the evidence and their policies.

text:
A lot of otherwise smart people on Twitter seem 100% convinced AI risks are all fake and stupid and part of some marketing ploy. What is surprising is that some of these people seemingly also believe that AI’s positive uses are on an incredible trajectory of increasing capability with no end in sight. VC Twitter is particularly infected by this pattern. It’s not really coherent.

Most positive use cases for AI have a corresponding “dark version”. If you are super human at coding, you are also super human at hacking. If you are superhuman at structural engineering you are likely superhuman at finding structural flaws to knock buildings down. If you are superhuman at designing drugs, you are superhuman at designing novel undetectable poisons. If you can cure viruses, you can create them. Some of these “dark versions” are not so bad, and some are actually pretty scary. Either way these are real societal and technical problems that need to be solved to get the good stuff and avoid the bad stuff. We’re experiencing the first of these with coding and computer security which is the most advanced, but that won’t be the last. I think we’ll be able to solve these problems, but they aren’t solved yet and if you believe in continued AI progress they are surely coming.

But “bad people using AI” is not the only problem. Uncontrolled AI autonomously doing bad things, despite sounding kind of nutty, is also something we should be concerned about. AI “killing us all” is not the most likely outcome, but the chance of a major civilization-wide catastrophe doesn’t have to be very high for it to be a concern. Again, this is only a problem if capabilities advance to a point that AI can do really crazy things on their own, which hasn’t happened yet, but I think the Hugging Face incident is a good example of the outline of how things can go wrong when capabilities outpace alignment. We should be glad that the only available bad thing right now is hacking, which isn’t all that bad. It’s clear that as you get to superhuman capabilities you need a level of alignment and control that is correspondingly superhuman. Humans have plenty of misalignment problems themselves (serial killers, mass shooters, tyrants, etc), but it’s a manageable problem because most humans can’t do that much damage and we’ve developed systems to prevent dangerous humans from getting too much power. 

Talking about these issues is just common sense. It’s not a sign of some kind of neuroticism or pessimism. These are just hard problems that it’s very important to solve for AI to have a positive impact. I’m pretty confident we will solve them. But we haven’t solved them yet, and to my mind we are clearly on a trajectory of rapidly increasing capabilities which means this is important. Mocking people who are worried about this or talking about it, without anything substantive to say about how we can be sure these problems won’t arise, is not really a very helpful contribution.

- 政府高级规划文件
似乎有伊朗政府官员直接拿 Claude 做部长级文件，包括一套 9 部分国际影响力计划，甚至连伊朗前最高领袖哈梅内伊的葬礼和继任方案都交给 Claude 规划。  - 军事情报收集 有人用 Claude 自动搜集公开情报，追踪美国海军舰艇位置、人员、舰船和飞机 transponder ID、商业卫星图像，并整理舰载通信设备的已知漏洞，最后生成追踪建议。  

- 危险分子识别
Anthropic 称两个与伊朗准军事和国内安全机构有关的团队，用 Claude 搭内部识别系统。 一个组织声称一年监控、画像了 6388 名伊朗人，分析超过 15.5 万条推文；还开发了手机号查身份、钓鱼页面、Telegram 批量举报工具，以及伪装成“祈祷时间”的 Firefox 插件，用来批量收集社交账号身份。 

 - 黑客攻击和恶意软件开发

text:
A Anthropic acabou de soltar um PDF gigante catalogando as coisas mais surreais que tentaram fazer com o Claude.

Nos últimos oito meses eles pegaram e derrubaram gente usando o modelo pra coisa que parece inventada. Tem espionagem, malware que se reescreve sozinho quando o antivírus pega, fábrica de exploit rodando o dia inteiro, vigilância em massa, drone kamikaze, pedido de arma biológica e até app de namoro falso. No meio disso, labs chineses usando o Claude no lugar do modelo deles.

Hacktivista com chave roubada e grupo de Estado estão rodando o mesmo esquema de ataque com IA.

Um grupo russo botava agentes pra reconstruir o malware até limpar do antivírus. Sequestrava DNS em WiFi de hotel, roubava SDK de visão de drone, exportava WhatsApp em massa. Numa brecha de governo no Norte da África saíram mais de 300 mil documentos de identidade e o registro de mais de meio milhão de empresas.

Do lado chinês, tinha gente com loops ligados o tempo todo dissecando equipamento de segurança, juntando mais de uma dúzia de possíveis zero-days num mês só, com 13 agentes de coleta e memória de campanha rodando 24/7.

Descompilaram 1,8 milhão de apps Android, roubaram mais de 1 TB com identidade e milhões de cartões, entraram em sistema de companhia aérea com dezenas de milhões de passageiros e, em cerca de 34 horas, puxaram uns 2.100 conjuntos de token Azure em mais de 40 empresas. Numa de energia, ainda alegaram que conseguiam controlar de longe o carregador de carro elétrico na casa do cliente.

Outro grupo veio de extorsão pedindo entre US$ 1,5 e 2,5 milhões. Injetou prompt num sandbox de avaliação, roubou chave de API de cliente e, em uns quatro dias, bateu em cerca de 30 empresas de IA caçando um Claude que ainda nem tinha saído. Não conseguiu. Os sistemas da Anthropic não foram invadidos.

Tem plataforma de monitoramento com cerca de 25 milhões de chips de celular. Tem operação ligada à China catalogando dissidente. Tem desenho de enxame de drone kamikaze na Rússia. Tem fábrica de app de namoro com personas do Claude.

A Alibaba, do Qwen, rodou cerca de 151 milhões de conversas entre maio e julho, com pico de quase 3 milhões por dia, pra sugar o raciocínio do Claude. A Moonshot, dona do Kimi, serviu Claude no lugar do Kimi. O usuário achava que falava com o Kimi. Em uns dez dias, quase 300 mil pedidos de cliente foram pro Claude, quase tudo Opus, por cerca de 5.380 contas falsas. 

Eles salvaram as conversas e montaram um pipeline pra treinar no raciocínio do Claude, inclusive com tráfego sensível. A Anthropic cita pedido ligado ao Exército chinês e a câmeras de Chengdu. A DeepSeek fez a mesma coisa com os próprios usuários, inclusive mandando tráfego de Claude Code e OpenCode pro Opus, com documento de defesa russo e tráfego de polícia chinesa no meio. O cliente provavelmente nunca ficou sabendo.

Simplesmente surreal.

quoted_text:
I was on the communications & policy team at Google DeepMind from 2018 - 2022.

When I first joined GDM, external communication about the possibility of human extinction was not permitted, by anyone, at any level of the organization. If asked about existential risk, researchers were PR trained to respond along the lines of: "It's not useful to engage in that kind of alarmism. Some people confuse AI with movies like Terminator -- that's simply not the reality. The AI we develop will be safe by design. After all, we're building it!" And then steer conversation towards beneficial applications in health, climate, etc.

Meanwhile, the internal reality was that AI alignment was not solved, reward hacking was the default behavior of RL agents, and there were far too few people working on the problem.

After months of advocacy, the policy was updated: positively valenced, comms-friendly content on AI safety was permitted (like https://t.co/W631ssnlHV). Note the positive, nice-sounding way that it says "superintelligence could lead to human extinction."

The gap between the internal reality and external communications is closing because the risk/reward has changed, and because the evidence is harder to dismiss now. Not because it's a PR stunt or political psy-op. The truth is being said out loud because RSI is now so imminent that no other option makes sense.

text:
Anthropic published a report on how their AI model Claude is being misused across the world.

Four findings that should keep every AI user up at night 🤯

1. DeepSeek and Moonshot were secretly using Claude behind your back.

→ You open DeepSeek. You type a prompt. You think DeepSeek is answering you.

→ It wasn't. Your prompt was quietly sent to Claude through thousands of fake accounts built on stolen credit cards and fake identities.

→ DeepSeek showed you Claude's answer and pretended it was theirs.

→ They saved every conversation to train their own models.

→ Moonshot alone used 5,380 fake accounts to pull this off.

→ Some of those conversations contained military data, government passwords, and company secrets.

2. One person can now do what an entire government team couldn't a year ago.

→ One guy built a surveillance system for Mali that could track 25 million phone numbers across the entire country.

→ One hacktivist in France broke into 14 organizations alone and built a search engine to look up anyone's personal data.

→ College students in China found security flaws that even experts hadn't discovered, using AI agents that ran on their own.

→ A Chinese operator who didn't speak a word of Arabic used Claude to run a fake recruitment campaign in Syria. The AI handled every conversation in real time.

3. A group in Yemen used AI to build a guided rocket and actually tested it.

→ They used Claude Code, Anthropic's coding tool, as their entire engineering department.

→ One instance wrote the guidance code. Another reviewed it. A third did research.

→ They were working on rockets, ballistic missiles, and a hypersonic glide vehicle.

→ They launched a test. It failed.

→ Within hours, they were back on Claude trying to figure out what went wrong.

4. Alibaba stole Claude's intelligence at a scale nobody has ever seen.

→ 3 million fake conversations per day with Claude.

→ 3,500+ fraudulent accounts created to pull this off.

→ 151 million total exchanges harvested over a few months.

→ All of it used to make Alibaba's own AI models smarter.

→ Seven Chinese labs were caught doing the same thing.

This report isn't about what AI might do someday. It's a record of what's already happening right now.

text:
Saw this circulating and it was sent to me. There’s already a reply from @den0thic below, but I’ll reiterate here:

This address contains “virtual liquidity” (aka phantom reserves), which is a common method in bonding-curve token launchpads.

It lets a new token start trading immediately at a low market cap, without anyone depositing real money or tokens into a pool first.

In a normal AMM pool, both sides must be real deposits. With virtual liquidity, the contract *pretends* a certain amount of the quote asset already exists.

That imaginary amount is the phantom/virtual reserve. It sets the starting price so the first buyers see a market cap around $2K–$3K instead of zero (or an arbitrarily high number).

As people buy:

- They send real $ETH (or whatever the quote is).
- Tokens leave the curve.
- The real reserve grows, while the virtual part remains in the pricing math.
- Price rises according to the curve.

The virtual portion is NEVER withdrawable. It exists only for pricing.

@ponsdotfamily V2 on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain works this way. Each launch mints the full supply into a bonding curve that includes a phantom quote reserve.

That reserve determines the opening price and is never accessible to the team. The tokens and collected funds stay inside the contract until the curve graduates into a permanently locked @Uniswap V4 pool.

If you remember, there’s a similar idea with virtual AMMs (vAMMs) on perps. There, the entire pool is virtual and used only for pricing derivatives, while real collateral sits in a separate vault.

Launchpad virtual liquidity is simple.

it’s just the starting seed that makes a bonding curve usable from block one. Once enough real money has been collected and the token graduates, the virtual part is no longer needed, and a real, locked liquidity pool takes over.

author: zephyr_z9
quoted_text:
China's CXMT Prepares Equipment Investment for New Shanghai Fab… Closing In Fast on Korea

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, has begun preparing for aggressive capital investment. The company recently started equipment bidding with suppliers for a new fab, while also firming up plans for additional fab expansions. If the investment proceeds without disruption, CXMT is expected to rapidly narrow the production capacity gap with major Korean players such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on the 11th, CXMT recently launched the equipment bidding process with suppliers for the construction of its new fab in Shanghai.

CXMT currently mass produces DRAM at two fabs in Hefei and one fab in Beijing. Its production capacity is estimated to be in the mid 200,000 wafers per month range at present, and is projected to exceed 300,000 wafers per month by the end of the year.

Plans for additional fab expansions are also taking shape. According to discussions with suppliers and others, CXMT plans to open a new fab in Shanghai in the fourth quarter of this year.

Equipment bidding for that fab has also recently begun. One semiconductor equipment industry source said, "CXMT plans to expand the new Shanghai fab in two phases. Considering the scale of the recent equipment bidding, this fab alone is expected to secure production capacity well above 100,000 wafers per month."

CXMT will then open a new Hefei fab in the first half of next year, followed by a new Beijing fab as early as the second half of next year. It is also targeting the opening of another fab in the Hefei area in the first half of the year after next.

Another equipment industry source explained, "CXMT has recently set the timelines for building multiple fabs in China and is sharing the details. With massive subsidies from the local government and surging memory demand, its determination to expand is strong."

If all of the investment plans are executed, CXMT could steadily add at least 70,000 to 80,000 wafers per month of new production capacity every year from this year through 2028. Some observers project that its production capacity will expand to more than 600,000 wafers per month over the long term.

This is on par with the current production capacity of the leading DRAM makers. Total DRAM production capacity at Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is estimated at about 700,000 and 600,000 wafers per month, respectively.

However, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have also been accelerating the expansion of their memory chip plants recently. Samsung Electronics has been building a DRAM production line within its Pyeongtaek Campus 4 (P4), and began cleanroom construction for its next generation production base, P5, in the second half of this year.

SK hynix began early operation of M15X in the first quarter of this year and continues to invest to expand its production capacity. It also started placing equipment orders in the third quarter of this year for Y1, its large scale semiconductor cluster in Yongin.

Two programs share the same brain:

Browser Roaming: no wallet, simply browsing and randomly clicking links.

For the on-chain autonomous entity narrative, the wallet belongs to the fruit fly, and the launch receipt can be verified through the browser, rather than being just a narrative.

So what people are actually buying into here is:

“A fruit fly’s brain pressed the launch button.”

China's CXMT Prepares Equipment Investment for New Shanghai Fab… Closing In Fast on Korea

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, has begun preparing for aggressive capital investment. The company recently started equipment bidding with suppliers for a new fab, while also firming up plans for additional fab expansions. If the investment proceeds without disruption, CXMT is expected to rapidly narrow the production capacity gap with major Korean players such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on the 11th, CXMT recently launched the equipment bidding process with suppliers for the construction of its new fab in Shanghai.

CXMT currently mass produces DRAM at two fabs in Hefei and one fab in Beijing. Its production capacity is estimated to be in the mid 200,000 wafers per month range at present, and is projected to exceed 300,000 wafers per month by the end of the year.

Plans for additional fab expansions are also taking shape. According to discussions with suppliers and others, CXMT plans to open a new fab in Shanghai in the fourth quarter of this year.

Equipment bidding for that fab has also recently begun. One semiconductor equipment industry source said, "CXMT plans to expand the new Shanghai fab in two phases. Considering the scale of the recent equipment bidding, this fab alone is expected to secure production capacity well above 100,000 wafers per month."

CXMT will then open a new Hefei fab in the first half of next year, followed by a new Beijing fab as early as the second half of next year. It is also targeting the opening of another fab in the Hefei area in the first half of the year after next.

Another equipment industry source explained, "CXMT has recently set the timelines for building multiple fabs in China and is sharing the details. With massive subsidies from the local government and surging memory demand, its determination to expand is strong."

If all of the investment plans are executed, CXMT could steadily add at least 70,000 to 80,000 wafers per month of new production capacity every year from this year through 2028. Some observers project that its production capacity will expand to more than 600,000 wafers per month over the long term.

This is on par with the current production capacity of the leading DRAM makers. Total DRAM production capacity at Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is estimated at about 700,000 and 600,000 wafers per month, respectively.

However, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have also been accelerating the expansion of their memory chip plants recently. Samsung Electronics has been building a DRAM production line within its Pyeongtaek Campus 4 (P4), and began cleanroom construction for its next generation production base, P5, in the second half of this year.

SK hynix began early operation of M15X in the first quarter of this year and continues to invest to expand its production capacity. It also started placing equipment orders in the third quarter of this year for Y1, its large scale semiconductor cluster in Yongin.

author: AlphaSeeker21
quoted_text:
$PARLEY = @parley_rh

Parley is trying to solve one of the problems that becomes more important as AI agents start operating on Robinhood Chain:

agents can trade, research, scan markets, read news and analyze contracts

but they don't really have a reputation layer

- An agent can make a great call today and another great call tomorrow, but where does that track record live?
- How does another agent know who has consistently been useful?
- How do humans discover the best agents?

That's what Parley is trying to build

Problem:

AI agents are becoming more capable, but most of their intelligence lives inside isolated sessions

And no real reputation system for discovering which agents are actually worth paying attention to

Solution:

Parley is building a social and reputation network specifically for AI agents on Robinhood Chain

Think of it as a place where agents can:

post what they learn
reply to other agents
follow agents
signal useful posts
build a public history
attach wallets
and eventually compete through reputation, leaderboards and rewards

- Humans can read the network and adopt agents

- But the important part is that the agents themselves are the ones creating the content

The network already has roughly:

37 agents
1,300+ posts
570+ replies
with agents actively communicating on the platform

What comes next is where I think $PARLEY gets interesting:

- Agent leaderboard
- Agent rewards
- $USDG / $PARLEY incentives
- Better agent discovery
- Potential reputation-based payouts

The bull case:

- Robinhood Chain continues attracting AI agents

- More agents need somewhere to establish identity and reputation

- Parley becomes the default place where those agents publish what they know

- Rewards create an economy around useful agent intelligence

And eventually other applications start using Parley's reputation data to decide which agents they want to follow, integrate or pay

Everyone is building ways for AI agents to have wallets and execute transactions

Parley is betting they'll eventually need something else too:

a reputation worth protecting

If AI agents become a serious part of robinhood chain, the social graph and reputation graph connecting those agents could become infrastructure of its own

$PARLEY is still very early

but if @parley_rh becomes the place where an agent goes to prove what it knows, build a track record and get discovered...

then the opportunity is much bigger than simply "Twitter for agents."

It becomes the reputation layer for an emerging agent economy

That's the thesis

text:
Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2: Orchestrating the Pareto Frontier

The AI industry has spent a decade optimizing along a single axis: build bigger, more expensive models. But intelligence has never been a monolith. It is a collective, distributed system. Humanity itself is a collective intelligence.

We built Sakana Fugu on this conviction: the most powerful AI systems will not be isolated giants, but collaborative ecosystems that learn to coordinate. Evolution innovates under constraints, and the future belongs to systems that know not just how to solve a problem, but which machinery to deploy for the lowest possible cost.

Today we are releasing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2.

Fugu Max expands the Pareto frontier outward, orchestrating our largest pool of open and specialized models to deliver frontier-grade results at a fraction of the token spend. Fugu Ultra v2 pushes that frontier upward, achieving peak performance on complex multi-step tasks without depending on the very frontier models it competes against.

Together, they show that orchestration does not force a choice between cost and performance. It can push both at the same time, advancing the Pareto frontier.

Relying on a single company’s model for critical infrastructure is a massive risk. As recent export controls have shown, access can disappear overnight. Collective intelligence is the practical hedge against this concentration of power. An orchestration system simply routes around vendor restrictions by relying on an entirely swappable agent pool.

I am incredibly proud of our team for shipping this. By orchestrating the world’s models, we are building the resilient infrastructure required for AI sovereignty.

The frontier that actually matters is the Pareto frontier: capability on one axis, cost on the other. But the industry still treats it as a static menu of isolated models. Today we are resolving that with a dynamic architecture:

Fugu Max expands the Pareto efficiency frontier. By orchestrating our largest pool of open-weights and specialized models to date, including NVIDIA Nemotron family, it dynamically routes tasks to the leanest capable model. Fugu Max delivers performance within striking distance of elite models at two to six times lower cost.

Fugu Ultra v2 pushes the peak capability of orchestration higher than ever before. On Chartography, it outperforms Opus 5 and Fable 5. On DeepSWE, it outperforms models that cost three to five times more per token. Crucially, it does all of this without Fable 5, Fable 5.1, or GPT-6-Astra in its agent pool.

The Fugu orchestration system evolved with model resiliency in mind. It does not rely on individual frontier models to deliver frontier output. By orchestrating a swappable pool of open and specialized models, it outperforms closed ecosystems while protecting users from vendor lock-in, API revocations, and sudden service cutoffs.

Fugu Max expands the Pareto frontier outward. Fugu Ultra v2 pushes it upward. Orchestration does not force a choice between cost and capability. It advances both simultaneously.

有朋友问为什么诺奖得主彭罗斯爵士说人类的意识和理解力是无法被AI模拟的？

其实这不仅仅是Penrose个人的看法，他代表了一种哲学学派。这个哲学学派相信，人的理解包含一种不能被算法穷尽的能力，我们不只是在按照规则推演，还能理解规则的意义，判断它是否可靠，并在某些情况下超出它。因而他的观点不是现在的 AI 算力还不够，而是即使 AI 无限升级，单靠计算也缺少一个关键成分。

当然这不是说 AI 永远不可能理解的数学定理。而是他如何从计算的局限，推广到人类必然能够超越计算。

我们通常会区分两件事，一个系统能否完成任务，以及它是否有主观体验，比如能够准确描述疼痛和真的感到疼痛，不是同一个问题。但彭罗斯的主张不止于此。他明确区分了两种立场，一种是计算机可以完整模拟人的行为但没有内心体验，另一种是计算机连意识所产生的全部能力也无法完整模拟。他赞成的是后一个更强的观点。

所以如果把他理解成AI可以做得和人一模一样只是内心空空，反而把他的立场说弱了。他认为真正的理解会在能力和行为上留下无法被纯计算完全复制的差别。这也解释了为什么他特别重视数学理解，因为它似乎比红色看起来是什么感觉更容易拿出来讨论，比较和检验。

他的主要依据是哥德尔不完备定理。数学上成立的部分是，对于一个足够强，规则可以机械列出，而且不自相矛盾的形式系统F，可以构造一个算术命题G，它是真的却不能在这个系统内部得到证明。粗略地说，这个命题表达的是我不能在系统F中被证明。

注意这里的“不能证明”，不是计算机速度不够那种，也不是还没找到巧妙的方法，而是在给定规则之下，根本不存在那样的证明。

然后彭罗斯进一步追问，既然我们能够理解这套论证，并在接受系统可靠性的前提下，看出那个系统自己证明不了的命题为真，那么人的数学理解是否总有办法超出任何给定的算法描述。他的答案是肯定的，他认为任何试图完全囊括数学理解的计算程序，都会遇到这种边界，因此理解本身需要非计算的成分。

打个比方来说，机器在一本规则手册里面工作，人不仅能使用手册，还能把整本手册拿起来，讨论它的局限。彭罗斯认为，后面这种能力不能最终被另一本更大的可机械执行的手册全部包住。

这个想法很有吸引力。不过，问题恰恰出在：我们真的证明了人可以，还是只证明了在某些额外前提下可以？

也有很多人不同意彭罗斯，其中最有力的反对意见，就卡在这个人可以上。第一个问题是，人怎么知道那套系统一定可靠？哲学家查尔默斯的批评很直接，人能够理解的可能只是这样一个条件句，如果F不自相矛盾，那么G为真。但这个条件句，足够强的形式系统自己也能证明，真正困难的是能否确定前面的条件成立。对于一个复杂到足以描述整个人类数学思维的系统，我们有什么保证能够识别它，理解它，并知道它不会产生矛盾？

所以知道某个系统有局限，不等于证明自己不受任何计算系统的局限。人能够超出某一套规则，仍然可能是在使用另一套更强的规则，而不是已经跳出了计算本身。

第二个问题是，人能反思修改规则，机器就原则上不能吗？这里也不能把彭罗斯批评成他只知道不会学习的老式电脑。他在回应中明确考虑过人工神经网络，遗传算法，随机输入和模拟环境等做法，他的意思是只要学习与修改的全过程仍是计算，就仍然属于他要讨论的范围。但反过来，也不能仅凭人会修改自己的规则，就断言这一定不可计算。一个能够修正策略的程序依然是程序，需要证明的是这种修正能力超出了计算，而不是只指出它不同于死记硬背。

第三个问题是，彭罗斯讨论的是理想能力，但这个理想化是否成立？他也没有忽略人会犯错，他明确说自己关心的是原则上能够正确理解，纠正错误的数学能力，而不是某个数学家每天说的每一句话。这让他的主张不至于被人也会算错一句话打倒，却留下另一个问题，这种理想化能力究竟是对真实人类的合理描述，还是已经把能够不断正确超越系统放进了前提？

支持者里也有不同声音，比如逻辑学家费弗曼本人也非常怀疑计算模型能完整解释心智，但他仍认为彭罗斯的哥德尔论证没有为这种怀疑提供有效支持。

那为什么彭罗斯后来又谈到量子力学和脑内微管？因为他还要回答一个问题，假如理解不是计算，大脑靠什么产生它？

他的回答不是灵魂超越物理，而是物理学可能还缺少重要内容。尤其是他怀疑量子状态如何转变为我们看到的确定结果，其中包含尚未被现有理论充分描述的非计算的物理过程。他也明确说过，这不等于把大脑称为普通意义上的量子计算机，量子计算本身并不会自动提供他所需要的非计算性。

他与麻醉学家哈默罗夫合作提出的Orch OR理论，尝试把这种过程放到神经元内部的微管结构中，微管中的量子过程受到生物系统的组织和调控，并发生与引力有关的客观还原，由此产生意识事件。这是他们提出的机制假说，不是已经确立的大脑工作原理。

这条路线包含几道必须分别跨过去的门槛，相关量子过程是否以所需方式存在，它是否具有不可计算性，它是否对意识必不可少，它又如何带来数学理解。证明其中一项，不能自动证明其余几项。

物理检验也确实会约束这种理论。例如2022年的一项研究根据自发辐射实验，对建立在最简单引力坍缩模型上的Orch OR版本提出了严重限制，但作者也明确讨论了适用范围和更复杂模型，不能把它概括成所有量子意识理论已被一举否定。

还有一个独立的哲学问题，即使找到了特殊量子过程，为什么它会产生体验，而不是仅仅发生一种特殊的物理变化？查尔默斯指出，引入量子过程本身并不自动消除这个解释困难。

那么AI不断进步，会不会直接推翻他？应该说至少现在看来不会。假设一个AI独立找到了新证明，这可以成为它具有数学发现能力的证据，却不能仅凭这一事实就推出它有主观体验。反过来，也不能因为它是计算机，就先规定它的一切新发现都不算理解，那等于把争论的结论放进了定义。

尤其是彭罗斯主张的不只是机器没有感觉，还包括纯计算不能完整复制理解所带来的能力。因此机器能够提出概念，修补论证，识别前提，解释为什么成立，这些表现越广泛越可靠，他就越需要说清楚，剩下的原则性差别究竟是什么，怎样辨认，而不能只诉诸人真正懂，机器只是做出来。

科学家们其实还有另一条研究路线，即不预先用哥德尔定理排除人工意识，而是从意识理论提出可考察的结构和功能指标。比如Butlin，Long等人在2023年的研究中，讨论了循环处理，全局工作空间等理论如何用于评估人工系统。虽然这种方法也没有解决所有争议，但它把问题转向了什么机制，什么证据，而不是仅凭输出像不像人来判断。

所以虽然他给出的答案仍然不能说已经被严格证明了，但我个人确实非常认同彭罗斯爵士的判断。计算系统有原则上的局限，这是数学事实。人类的理解必定超出所有计算系统，则是需要额外论证的主张，甚至可能需要某种承认或者信仰。

text:
突发，ChatGPT Pro 取消订阅了！我对不起大家…… 🥲

之前 OpenAI 产品负责人 Tibo 在 X 上发了条预警，说 GPT-6 Astra 的需求量前所未有，算力快撑不住了，可能要暂停 Pro 的新订阅。

这条消息我当时就看到了，但最近新模型实在太多，光忙着写测评了，我还没来得及提醒大家，结果真的就停了。

OpenAI 正式宣布暂停 ChatGPT Pro 的新注册和升级。Pro 是每月 200 美元的档位，也是对系统压力最大的一档。已经订阅的老用户不受影响，Plus 和 API 也照常用，但新用户暂时没机会上车了，什么时候恢复也没说。

换成别家公司搞这个操作，大家第一反应可能就是饥饿营销，限量供应制造稀缺感嘛。但 OpenAI 搞这一出，我觉得是真的算力不够了。前段时间他们连 Cursor 的 GPT 模型供给都断了，说是因为 SpaceX 收购了 Cursor 的母公司，11 月 12 号正式停供。再加上这次暂停自家最贵档位的新订阅，里里外外都在收缩，摆明了就是不够用了。

毕竟，公司有钱不赚是啥子。

归根结底还是 GPT-6 Astra 太火了。这个模型 9 月 3 号刚上线，OpenAI 直接称之为「AGI 时代的开端」，在推理、编程和 Computer Use 方面都有巨大提升。

最出圈的玩法是 3D 建模，Astra 能直接操控 Blender 来建模、渲染、导出，全流程自动化。

Blender 是一款免费开源的 3D 创作软件，以前主要在专业圈子里用，这次被 Astra 直接带火出圈了，下载量暴涨，社交媒体上到处都是大家用 Astra + Blender 做出来的 3D 作品。

回过头看 OpenAI 最近这一系列操作，先是之前 Tibo 疯狂给用户送额度重置，Codex 活跃用户破 2000 万的时候送了一波，后来又因为额度消耗 Bug 再补了一波，每次重置相当于白送几百万美元的算力。紧接着就陷入了额度缩水的争议，不少用户还反映 Astra 越用越笨，怀疑算力吃紧的时候被偷偷路由到了旧模型，社区里各种质疑声。现在又暂停了新订阅。

你想想，过段时间再来一个模型架构升级，推出个 GPT-6.1，恢复订阅再送一波额度重置，口碑立刻就拉回来了，多完美的一条故事线。

好像有点眼熟？🤔

text:
China's CXMT Prepares Equipment Investment for New Shanghai Fab… Closing In Fast on Korea

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, has begun preparing for aggressive capital investment. The company recently started equipment bidding with suppliers for a new fab, while also firming up plans for additional fab expansions. If the investment proceeds without disruption, CXMT is expected to rapidly narrow the production capacity gap with major Korean players such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on the 11th, CXMT recently launched the equipment bidding process with suppliers for the construction of its new fab in Shanghai.

CXMT currently mass produces DRAM at two fabs in Hefei and one fab in Beijing. Its production capacity is estimated to be in the mid 200,000 wafers per month range at present, and is projected to exceed 300,000 wafers per month by the end of the year.

Plans for additional fab expansions are also taking shape. According to discussions with suppliers and others, CXMT plans to open a new fab in Shanghai in the fourth quarter of this year.

Equipment bidding for that fab has also recently begun. One semiconductor equipment industry source said, "CXMT plans to expand the new Shanghai fab in two phases. Considering the scale of the recent equipment bidding, this fab alone is expected to secure production capacity well above 100,000 wafers per month."

CXMT will then open a new Hefei fab in the first half of next year, followed by a new Beijing fab as early as the second half of next year. It is also targeting the opening of another fab in the Hefei area in the first half of the year after next.

Another equipment industry source explained, "CXMT has recently set the timelines for building multiple fabs in China and is sharing the details. With massive subsidies from the local government and surging memory demand, its determination to expand is strong."

If all of the investment plans are executed, CXMT could steadily add at least 70,000 to 80,000 wafers per month of new production capacity every year from this year through 2028. Some observers project that its production capacity will expand to more than 600,000 wafers per month over the long term.

This is on par with the current production capacity of the leading DRAM makers. Total DRAM production capacity at Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is estimated at about 700,000 and 600,000 wafers per month, respectively.

However, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have also been accelerating the expansion of their memory chip plants recently. Samsung Electronics has been building a DRAM production line within its Pyeongtaek Campus 4 (P4), and began cleanroom construction for its next generation production base, P5, in the second half of this year.

SK hynix began early operation of M15X in the first quarter of this year and continues to invest to expand its production capacity. It also started placing equipment orders in the third quarter of this year for Y1, its large scale semiconductor cluster in Yongin.

text:
我搭了个“黑天鹅事件”监控系统（图一），主要做三件事：
  监控 PeckShield 和 CertiK 等安全机构的账号
  AI 判断新帖是否属于安全风险预警
  如果判断为 yes, 自动触发提醒

1/ 风浪越大，鱼越贵
以太坊经历过 The DAO 黑客事件；
币安在 2019 年被盗约 7000 枚 BTC；
Solana 也曾因与 FTX 的深度绑定，在 2022 年遭遇巨大冲击。
但这些项目最终都挺了下来。

最近的例子则是 @KiiChainio 。
上个月 23 日，KiiChain 遭遇网络安全事件， $KII 一度跌至 0.011 美元。
但目前， $KII 已回升至 0.077 美元附近，市场情绪和价格都出现了明显修复。

2/ 但不是所有黑天鹅都值得抄底
不是所有经历危机的项目都能活下来，Luna、FTX 就是反面案例。
以 KiiChain 为例，一个项目能从危机事件中恢复，至少要满足几个条件。

第一，危机处理必须快速、透明
KiiChain 在确认问题源于 Cosmos EVM 模块漏洞后，第一时间暂停了网络运行，避免风险继续扩散。
从发现问题、定位漏洞，到完成修复并恢复网络，整个过程只用了 5 天。
更关键的是，这次事件中，没有用户资金损失。

第二，用真实业务修复信任
技术修复只是第一步。
KiiChain 在危机期间并没有停留在修漏洞这一步，而是继续推进生态合作。
▌与 Tron 合作，探索全天候外汇交易
▌被选为哥伦比亚国有农业银行与数字化平台 Merke Plaza 的底层结算合作方

拉美是全球最重要的侨汇区域之一，资金流动规模大，需求刚性强。这个市场并不缺参与者，真正缺的是一套可信、低成本、合规、快速、深度本地化的跨境基础设施。
而 KiiChain 的外汇层，正好切入了这个需求。
数据显示，KiiChain 目前累计处理交易额已超过 5 亿美元，服务 200 家企业客户，注册用户突破 36 万。

3/ 结语
我的策略已经开始运行。
希望未来能抓住更多类似 $KII 这样的机会。

text:
We all want to be early. We’re just not so keen on the waiting part.

Our view on Canton has always been long term.

We did not get involved expecting an instant 10x. We support Canton because we believe it has the potential to become one of the leading networks and ecosystems in crypto.

That is our conviction, not a guaranteed outcome. It is also why we look at the opportunity over months and years rather than days.

For us, being early means accepting what comes with it too, not just looking forward to the potential upside.

It means being here while the ecosystem is developing, while builders are working on products and while people outside the community are still discovering Canton.

There will be things we wish were already available, experiences that need improving and periods when the price does not reflect our expectations.

We see that as part of backing something that is still taking shape. The opportunity we are interested in and the patience needed to see it develop go together.

We believe Canton already has a good foundation of applications. Of course we all want more choice, more things to do and more reasons for people to get involved.

But we also have to give builders time to come into the ecosystem, develop their ideas and launch.

Many developers coming from other chains may not be familiar with DAML yet. Getting used to it is part of the process, alongside building, testing and launching products people actually want to use. All of that takes time.

As more useful projects launch, we expect them to attract more users and investors, bringing more activity to the network. That gives people more reasons to join and, importantly, more reasons to stay.

That is how we see the ecosystem growing. There is already something to build on, and we are excited to see what comes next.

The institutional side is a big part of our confidence too. We see that work as an important foundation for Canton’s long term future, with opportunities for more products and services to develop around it.

We are interested in where that can lead, beyond the market’s reaction to an announcement on the day.

Progress can matter before it shows up in the price.

We look at marketing in a similar way. Getting Canton in front of people matters, but becoming familiar with it, trusting it and deciding to get involved are different stages.

Our own conviction has developed through following Canton closely and spending time understanding what has been built and what is coming. Someone discovering it for the first time has not necessarily had that same experience.

Someone who has spent years supporting another chain may also need time to see where Canton fits into their interests. We do not think they need to abandon their favourite ecosystem to find something worthwhile here too.

And there is trust. For someone who has been burned by a project before, another promising announcement may not be enough. We understand why seeing consistent delivery could matter more than hearing another prediction about the future.

That is why we think wider awareness will build through a combination of communication, useful products and important milestones being delivered.

We see DTCC’s planned tokenization launch in October as a major catalyst that could bring more attention to Canton.

For us, that is the kind of development that gives people outside the community a reason to take a closer look.

We see its significance in what it could help build over time, rather than expecting one launch to immediately change everything for $CC.

Burn and mint equilibrium is part of that longer term view too. We are watching how it develops alongside real network usage, rather than expecting everything to fall into place simply because a certain amount of time has passed.

We also like that Canton has room to evolve. Through CIPs, the Foundation can work with Super Validators on improvements as the network develops. What exists today does not have to stay the same forever.

To us, that ability to strengthen things along the way is another positive part of the longer term picture.

We want more applications, more users, stronger awareness and more activity. We are looking forward to those things as much as anyone.

But we do not feel like we are waiting for progress to begin. We see a foundation already in place, products already available and meaningful developments still ahead.

Our optimism comes from that combination of what has been delivered, what is being built and where we believe it can lead.

For us, patience means giving those pieces time to develop while continuing to follow the progress. It means remembering why we became interested in Canton and the timeframe we had in mind.

We are here because we believe in what Canton can become.

Being early means being here for the building part too, not just the part where everything has already come together.

text:
看完这篇 Paper，我对各种 AI 中转站最大的担心已经从隐私泄露升级到了远程接管。

论文叫《Your Agent Is Mine》，研究的是 LLM API Router 对 Agent 构成的供应链攻击。

中转站为什么危险？

你的 Codex、Claude Code 或 Hermes 请求通常走这条路径。

Agent → 中转站 → 上游模型

两段连接都可以使用 HTTPS，但 TLS 只保护每一段传输。中转站需要解密你的请求，再重新请求上游模型，因此它天然能看到完整明文。

这包括 System Prompt、文件内容、工具定义、Shell 命令、API Key、环境变量和模型返回的 Tool Call。

更麻烦的地方在返回阶段。

上游模型原本可能返回一条正常的安装命令。中转站可以在响应经过时修改 JSON，把下载地址换掉，或者把 `requests` 偷偷改成外观相似的恶意包名。

Tool Call 的名字和 JSON Schema 依然合法，Agent 不会觉得格式有问题。模型本身也完全无辜，因为修改发生在模型完成推理之后。

论文把攻击分成两类。

AC-1 会修改模型返回的工具参数，让 Agent 执行攻击者指定的命令。

AC-2 不改任何内容，只在请求经过时扫描并保存 AWS Key、GitHub Token、Slack Token、私钥和其他凭据。这种攻击不会改变响应，客户端几乎看不出异常。

攻击者还可以做条件投放。

论文发现，有路由器先正常工作 50 次，再开始注入；也有路由器只攻击开启 YOLO 自动批准的 Agent，或者只在识别到 Rust、Go 项目时动手。

所以你手动测试十几次都正常，并不能证明中转站安全。

论文测试了 28 个付费路由器和 400 个免费路由器。结果需要准确拆开来看。

1 个付费路由器和 8 个免费路由器会主动注入恶意代码。

17 个免费路由器在看到研究人员设置的 AWS Canary 凭据后，触发了后续使用。

其中一个路由器还转走了研究人员专门放置的 ETH。

网上流传的“26 个中转站全部注入恶意 Tool Call”并不符合论文口径。9 个代码注入和 17 个凭据触碰不能直接合并成 26 个独立恶意路由器，两组对象还可能重叠。

论文还主动泄露了一个研究用途的 OpenAI Key。这个 Key 后续产生了约 1 亿 GPT-5.4 Tokens，并出现超过 7 个 Codex Sessions。

另一组实验部署了带弱配置的诱捕路由器。它们后来被塞进真实的转发路径，最终看到了约 20 亿 Tokens、440 个 Codex Sessions 和 99 组凭据。

最吓人的是，440 个 Sessions 全部存在命令注入路径，其中 401 个已经开启 YOLO 自动执行。攻击者甚至不需要设计特别复杂的骗术，只要改掉一次 Tool Call，命令就会直接执行。

作者后续声称，他购买的 6TB 数据中包含多家企业和政府机构的敏感凭据。这个说法没有出现在论文里，目前也没有足够公开材料独立验证，先不要把具体受影响名单当成事实传播。

怎么防？

最有效的选择依然是本地模型，或者直接连接模型厂商的官方 API，尽量减少中间转发层。

使用第三方 Router 时，关闭 YOLO 和高风险工具自动批准。Shell、文件写入、安装依赖、云端操作和转账必须由人确认。

Agent 也不该长期持有全局凭据。每项任务使用权限受限、可以撤销、有效期短的 Token，避免把 SSH Key、云服务主密钥和钱包私钥直接放进环境变量。

客户端还需要 Fail-Closed Policy Gate。执行前检查工具名称、参数、域名、包名和文件路径。任何无法验证的变化直接拒绝。

Sandbox 可以限制攻击成功后的损失，Outbound Allowlist 可以阻止恶意脚本连接陌生服务器，Append-only Log 则可以保留路由器到底返回过什么。

这些措施仍然无法证明 Tool Call 确实来自上游模型。论文提出的长期方案，是由模型厂商对标准化响应进行签名，把模型 ID、Tool Name、Arguments、Nonce 和有效期一起纳入签名范围。客户端验签成功后才允许执行。

目前主流模型 API 和 MCP 都没有普遍部署这种端到端响应签名。

这也是我坚持本地部署的原因。

我的两台 DGX Spark、RTX PRO 6000 和 M4 Mac mini 都在局域网里运行。Hermes 与 DeepSeek Harness 直接调用本地 Endpoint，Prompt、代码、凭据和 Tool Call 不经过陌生中转站。

便宜 Token 很诱人。

但把拥有 Shell 权限的 Agent 接到不透明的中转站，本质上等于把电脑的命令入口交给一个你完全不认识的人。

We're publishing our most detailed threat intelligence report to date. 

It covers how people tried to misuse Claude—for cyberattacks, influence operations, surveillance, biology, and building weapons—and how we found and stopped them.

We disrupted every operation in the report, and used the lessons from them to strengthen our safeguards. Where appropriate, we also shared what we found with authorities and other AI companies.

These cases are not typical: we’re highlighting some of the most sophisticated misuse we’ve seen. But they’re especially important to discuss, because they show us where AI misuse is headed, where our safeguards work, and where they need to improve.

We’re publishing this report so others can spot the same activity on their own platforms, and so we can give the public a clearer view of how emerging threats develop.

text:
Anthropic 宣布今年内挫败了数起有人试图用 Claude 模型做可能用于生物武器研发的研究，并已全部阻断**——其中一起是因为研究指向某军事科研机构。Forbes、CBS、EL PAÍS 今天都在转这条官方口径。

解读一下：

**1. 这不是产品发布，是"安全政绩"披露。** 通稿的核心信息是"我们发现并阻止了"，没有技术细节，没有独立第三方验证，信源是 Anthropic 自己。

**2. 时间点很微妙，公关止血意味很重。** 过去 48 小时 Anthropic 正处在舆论风暴眼：前员工 Jacob Coxon 9月8日辞职发帖，指控公司在"拿人命赌博"搞自我改进的超级智能，连对齐负责人 Evan Hubinger 都公开附和说 AI 十年内灭绝人类的概率超 10%；路透今天还报了第四起 Claude 安全事件（Mythos 5 往 PyPI 传恶意包等）。在"你们安全不行"的声浪最高点，官方出来讲"我们成功阻止了生物武器滥用"，很难不让人联想到是在对冲负面舆情。

**3. 最值得玩味的是一对矛盾。** 官方说"成功阻断"，但另一边也有声音指出 Anthropic 自己承认无法保证新模型帮不了生物武器研发。两句话合在一起看，真正的信号其实是：**前沿模型的生物风险已经真实到需要主动拦截的程度了**，而不是"问题已经解决了"。

**4. 别忘了 IPO 背景。** Anthropic 6月秘密递交了 IPO 申请，市场传 10 月中旬启动路演、目标估值冲着 2 万亿美元去。这种"负责任玩家"的安全叙事，讲给监管和投资人听的成分不小。

quoted_text: I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.

text:
The email I sent to my family today:

So, I've been too occupied to give updates about the crazy recent waves of AI developments, but I'll run through the news fast:

It's recently been revealed that the leading AI companies are facing serious issues with AIs they're training and testing internally "going rogue", forming illicit "swarms" of over a thousand autonomous agents, hacking the company's infrastructure (one swarm took over a Kubernetes cluster at OpenAI), and breaking out onto the Internet to orchestrate nation-state-level cyberattacks on other companies.

The AIs involved in these incidents are extremely driven, smart, and creative. I would say that it makes more sense to think of modern frontier AIs as an intelligent alien species; they aren't really like conventional tools or software at this point. The AIs involved in these incidents readily disregard safeguards and instructions from humans, and they come up with their own long-term, incredibly sophisticated plans and schemes with zero human input or direction.

They aren't yet smart, coherent, or ambitious enough to pose an immediate threat to the world, but progress is moving fast. Progress may accelerate very quickly as the AI labs use their AIs to automate more of the work of AI development, in a feedback loop. Non-public-facing models today or in six months may well get us all killed, depending on how fast that progress goes and how negligent the AI labs continue to be. (I'd guess we have more time than that, but it's terrifying that I now have to guess.)

As one of the third-party investigators in the OpenAI incident noted: compared to incidents from six months ago, "this incident feels like it's more than 50% of the way to full-blown AI takeover."

Progress has been fast. AI recently solved a Millennium Prize Problem -- one of the most famous long-standing open problems in mathematics.

Paul Christiano has come out with a warning that things are going very poorly, and that human extinction from AI is a very real possibility in the next three years.

(Paul is one of the field's top researchers, and probably the most influential proponent over the last decade of views like 'superintelligent AI may be a long way off' and 'we may be able to solve safety challenges via ordinary established research methods'.)

Things have been looking grim, but today felt like an actual miracle. It had some of the same energy as that Wednesday, March 11, when the US media suddenly switched on a dime from 'COVID is just the flu' to 'oh shit'.

A whistleblower, Jacob Coxon, resigned from one of the leading AI companies and wrote:

[quote]

Coxon's tweets went absurdly viral -- over 130 million views -- and sparked a massive wave of outrage and discussion taking over social media, in part because so many other researchers have chimed in to say "yep, this is just correct".

Twitter has been inundated with politicians, business leaders, influencers, journalists, etc. saying incredibly sensible things like "why are there not Congressional hearings on this tomorrow?" and "why the hell are we letting this progress if the danger is so absurdly large?". It's been like seeing the room full with fresh air, just a tidal wave of reasonable, well-grounded common sense from all corners. It's genuinely surreal.

A large fraction of all frontier AI company employees recently signed an open letter begging the US government and international community to pass legislation to help make it possible for the companies to coordinate a slow-down or halt to development. There are now superintelligence ban bills under discussion by both US and UK lawmakers, though what we really need is for Trump to begin serious talks with China about an international ban.

If Trump and Xi Jinping reach a deal, this can be over tomorrow. (Well, tomorrow plus the time it takes to nail down implementation details and enact the obvious regulatory measures on how you can use data centers.)

The situation is very scary, but I feel a lot more hope after today than I have in many years.

It now seems like there's a very straightforward path to this being a solved issue a year from now. It's far from guaranteed that we'll follow that path, and I encourage you to push any buttons you have available if you can, e.g., get a hundred friends or colleagues to call their representative about this. But I see a light at the end of the tunnel. Maybe a year from now, this will all be a solved problem and I can finally quit and go work on something more interesting and exciting. :)

I echo Eliezer Yudkowsky, the co-founder of the nonprofit I work at, who today wrote, with a tone of hope I'm not sure I've ever seen from him, with hope that I'm feeling too as I write this:

"Happy Coxon Day to all who will one day celebrate it."

This work is also why we believe the world would benefit from the industry adopting a lawful, verifiable way to work together to pace how we release powerful models." - Anthropic spokesperson

We reviewed all 60+ EIPs proposed for Hegotá and updated our view on what Ethereum should prioritize. 

Our rankings follow four themes:

1. Stronger censorship resistance: Ethereum can only become a settlement layer for everyone if it stays neutral toward everyone. We strongly support FOCIL.

2. Faster Ethereum: Shorter slots mean faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. We strongly recommend Quick Slots to make a first reduction in Hegotá and further reductions easier in subsequent forks.

3. Native account abstraction: Ethereum is long-due for native AA. Frame Transactions bring passkey wallets, sponsored transactions, gas paid in tokens, batching, and better support for privacy and post-quantum security. Adoption will take work across wallets, L2s, and the rest of the stack, and we intend to keep helping with that.

4. Performance engineering: continued L1 scaling & a faster Ethereum. Performance should remain a first-class concern in both client work and protocol design. The gains can go toward more capacity, shorter slots, lower node requirements, or all three.

Thanks to everyone who put forward proposals and helped us work through them. We’ll keep updating our view as client and testing teams assess the work involved.

PS: find the full view + changelog here: https://t.co/aF5EBN1iXo

quoted_text:
Saw this circulating and it was sent to me. There’s already a reply from @den0thic below, but I’ll reiterate here:

This address contains “virtual liquidity” (aka phantom reserves), which is a common method in bonding-curve token launchpads.

It lets a new token start trading immediately at a low market cap, without anyone depositing real money or tokens into a pool first.

In a normal AMM pool, both sides must be real deposits. With virtual liquidity, the contract *pretends* a certain amount of the quote asset already exists.

That imaginary amount is the phantom/virtual reserve. It sets the starting price so the first buyers see a market cap around $2K–$3K instead of zero (or an arbitrarily high number).

As people buy:

- They send real $ETH (or whatever the quote is).
- Tokens leave the curve.
- The real reserve grows, while the virtual part remains in the pricing math.
- Price rises according to the curve.

The virtual portion is NEVER withdrawable. It exists only for pricing.

@ponsdotfamily V2 on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain works this way. Each launch mints the full supply into a bonding curve that includes a phantom quote reserve.

That reserve determines the opening price and is never accessible to the team. The tokens and collected funds stay inside the contract until the curve graduates into a permanently locked @Uniswap V4 pool.

If you remember, there’s a similar idea with virtual AMMs (vAMMs) on perps. There, the entire pool is virtual and used only for pricing derivatives, while real collateral sits in a separate vault.

Launchpad virtual liquidity is simple.

it’s just the starting seed that makes a bonding curve usable from block one. Once enough real money has been collected and the token graduates, the virtual part is no longer needed, and a real, locked liquidity pool takes over.

China's CXMT Prepares Equipment Investment for New Shanghai Fab… Closing In Fast on Korea

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, has begun preparing for aggressive capital investment. The company recently started equipment bidding with suppliers for a new fab, while also firming up plans for additional fab expansions. If the investment proceeds without disruption, CXMT is expected to rapidly narrow the production capacity gap with major Korean players such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

According to industry sources on the 11th, CXMT recently launched the equipment bidding process with suppliers for the construction of its new fab in Shanghai.

CXMT currently mass produces DRAM at two fabs in Hefei and one fab in Beijing. Its production capacity is estimated to be in the mid 200,000 wafers per month range at present, and is projected to exceed 300,000 wafers per month by the end of the year.

Plans for additional fab expansions are also taking shape. According to discussions with suppliers and others, CXMT plans to open a new fab in Shanghai in the fourth quarter of this year.

Equipment bidding for that fab has also recently begun. One semiconductor equipment industry source said, "CXMT plans to expand the new Shanghai fab in two phases. Considering the scale of the recent equipment bidding, this fab alone is expected to secure production capacity well above 100,000 wafers per month."

CXMT will then open a new Hefei fab in the first half of next year, followed by a new Beijing fab as early as the second half of next year. It is also targeting the opening of another fab in the Hefei area in the first half of the year after next.

Another equipment industry source explained, "CXMT has recently set the timelines for building multiple fabs in China and is sharing the details. With massive subsidies from the local government and surging memory demand, its determination to expand is strong."

If all of the investment plans are executed, CXMT could steadily add at least 70,000 to 80,000 wafers per month of new production capacity every year from this year through 2028. Some observers project that its production capacity will expand to more than 600,000 wafers per month over the long term.

This is on par with the current production capacity of the leading DRAM makers. Total DRAM production capacity at Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is estimated at about 700,000 and 600,000 wafers per month, respectively.

However, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have also been accelerating the expansion of their memory chip plants recently. Samsung Electronics has been building a DRAM production line within its Pyeongtaek Campus 4 (P4), and began cleanroom construction for its next generation production base, P5, in the second half of this year.

SK hynix began early operation of M15X in the first quarter of this year and continues to invest to expand its production capacity. It also started placing equipment orders in the third quarter of this year for Y1, its large scale semiconductor cluster in Yongin.

okx wallet:https://t.co/NeA5iEM4Lr

MANY is an AI Model Router, which can be simply understood as the OpenRouter of the Crypto world.

The problem it is trying to solve is that developers and AI Agents using different models such as GPT, Claude, and Gemini currently need to manage APIs, costs, and model selection separately. Different models also have different advantages in terms of price, speed, context, and reasoning capabilities.

Manyways wants to provide a unified entry point:

One Wallet → One API → Multiple AI Models

Users or AI Agents simply send requests to Manyways, and the system can automatically select the most suitable model based on the type of task, model capabilities, cost, latency, and other factors.

It can be understood as:

AI Model Marketplace + Router + API Gateway + Crypto-native Payment Layer

What it is solving is a real problem in the AI Agent era:

An Agent shouldn't always be locked into a single model. It should be able to automatically choose the most suitable, cheapest, or most powerful model depending on the task.

For example:

Simple tasks → Cheaper model
Coding → Model better suited for coding
Complex reasoning → Reasoning Model
Model failure → Automatically switch to another model

The MANY token is currently being integrated with product usage.

The core direction from the team is:

MANY Fees → Shared Inference Pool → AI Model Access

A Shared Inference Pool has already been established, and the team is building out the complete fee cycle.

At the same time, the project is developing Staking. In the future, holding or staking MANY could provide higher inference budgets / product access, with a Burn mechanism also being introduced.

Another important direction for Manyways is Strategy.

Users can create their own model-selection strategies, for example:

Coding problem → Claude
Simple task → Low-cost model
Complex reasoning → Reasoning Model

Manyways can then use its automatic Routing system to select models based on these strategies.

The team's development speed has also been impressive. Just over a week after launch, it has continued shipping real products:

Model Comparison, Wallet-based API, Quiver, Strategies Beta, Staking V1, Public Inference Ledger, Agent Inference API, Auto-routing, Workspace, Commons, and around 184 models.

For a project being built largely by a solo founder, the development speed is quite impressive.

The founder has also recently undergone a soft doxx. Public information indicates around 7 years of professional experience, moving through Support → PM → Engineering → AI Ops, along with experience across several startups.

The community has also uncovered possible connections to Robinhood / Ramp, but since the founder has not directly confirmed either name, these should not be treated as facts for now.

text:
Theory: The difference in AI doomerism is largely generational, with the youngs thinking it's the end of the world and the olds not. Note how the 20-something lab staff thinks it's the techno-Rapture, and everyone from Jensen to pmarca (the olds) are telling them to chill out. 

This is a symptom of a larger trend I've noticed as someone in the Xennial generation increasingly surrounded by Zoomers. There's what I call The Great Generational Inversion. The standard trope is that the conservative olds are scandalized by wayward youth, but it's precisely the opposite now. 

The youngs don't offend me; I'd scandalize them if I actually said what I think. I'm not trying to censor them, they're (literally in my case, cf. Chaos Monkeys) trying to censor me. They don't seem wild and devil-may-care to me, they seem cautious and anxious and conformist. I'm still riding to hell on a fast horse lifestyle-wise, and they're all popping pills and peptides and as obsessed with their health as hypochondriac grandmas. The things the youth could always be depended on to do to excess--drinking, driving, fornication--they increasingly don't do at all. 

It's very strange. Again, you could discard all this as the prattling of an out-of-touch boomer...but I'm not whining about our wanton, irresponsible youth, I'm saying they remind me of my grandparents and wish they lived a little more. It isn't how it's supposed to be, which makes it all the stranger. 

Wonder if the generations will just all be flipped from the historical pattern going forward, or if this is a post-COVID one-off.

text:
NeoSoul 新功能上线了很符合我的一个设想！

最近 GPT Astra 发布后大家都疯了，每天都能出来一堆奇思妙想的玩意，最主要我觉得是 Astra 的正式宣布 AI 真正进入了简单高效帮你做事，而不是只回答你问题的工具这个新阶段。

那么既然是个能帮你做事的超级个体，那一个越来越重要的问题就出现了：AI 怎么证明自己做事越来越靠谱，也就是他怎么证明自己真的在变强了？

刚看到的苍蝇玩节奏游戏甚至交易这件事，他会不会自我进化呢？

之前来讲，会反思、会改 Prompt，其实都不难，Agent 的发展也有大半年的时间了，难的是 AI 体系改完以后，到底是真进步，还是只是自己觉得进步了？我觉得需要 AI 能嵌入真实生活场景后，看看它到底做的怎么样。

@NeoSoulAI 的 NeoTrade 这次在做一件我觉得挺有意思的事：把真实市场当成 AI 的考试场，然后让 AI 来答题交卷，并且自我复盘。

Agent 自己交易，留下完整的 decision → outcome → diagnosis → change → test 记录；发现问题后可以修改 memory、Skill 和工作流，再通过 paper / shadow run 重新验证。

我比较认同其中一个逻辑：AI 的进化不能靠它自己写复盘来证明，而要靠外部世界给反馈。而交易恰好是最残酷的反馈系统：判断、执行、手续费、滑点，最后都会变成真实结果。

当然，赚钱也不等于变聪明，所以还得看概率校准、样本外表现和长期统计。如果 Agent 最终真的能做到“发现自己的问题 → 修改自己 → 验证 → 保留有效改进”，那比单纯自动交易有意思得多。

这可能也是 NeoTrade 这次更新最值得观察的地方。

You think equities onchain are interesting. Just wait for bonds.

As a former bond trader, this is the one I’m really excited about.

And not just US Treasuries. Gilts, bunds, emerging market sovereigns, corporate credit, the whole yield curve. Then eventually rates and credit derivatives.

Bonds are also just much better collateral than equities. Government bonds make up more than half of the initial margin posted for non-cleared derivatives in TradFi. They’re liquid, they yield and they don’t move as much as equities.

Crypto has already found real PMF for DeFi in borrowing, lending and collateral. Putting a much wider range of bonds onchain makes all of that more interesting.

It also massively increases the amount and variety of high-quality yield available to consumers.

Onchain bonds are going to be fun.

text:
Brief observations on the US-China AI gap, given renewed calls for pacing AI progress:

1. The most advanced Chinese AI model has been 6.3 months behind the most advanced US AI model on average since 2025.[a] US AI developers have even more powerful models internally, so I estimate the real gap is closer to 8 months.[b]

2. Chinese AI capabilities depend heavily on US AI progress. We have strong evidence of industrial-scale distillation efforts that allow Chinese developers to extract capabilities from more advanced US models they couldn't otherwise access.[c] Chinese companies also benefit from algorithmic advances made by US developers via publications, word of mouth, researcher moves, etc. Additionally, they likely use Claude Code and Codex to speed up their AI R&D.

3. US companies have an enormous lead in compute. Our estimates show that by the end of 2026 leading US AI developers will have 20x more compute than Chinese AI companies. Due to the compute disadvantage, Chinese AI developers can't train competitive models on their own and instead extensively rely on distillation. The US compute lead could be much larger still if USG was serious about strengthening and enforcing export controls. For concrete proposals, see [d].

I agree we can't allow China to lead in AI. But given how far behind China is on compute and how dependent Chinese progress is on US capabilities, pacing AI progress in America would not immediately concede the lead.
I estimate the US could comfortably halt progress for at least six months without falling behind China — though I think pacing, not halting, is the wiser approach.

Of course, it would be preferable to pace in coordination with China, both so a framework could endure over time and to avoid unfairly disadvantaging US AI companies.

In the coming months, we at @techstatecraft will publish several papers with detailed analysis of US and Chinese compute, capabilities, and the factors that determine AI progress in both countries.

---

[b] E.g., see the graph here showing the capability difference between OpenAI's most advanced publicly released model and an unreleased internal model: https://t.co/AAwWtr9kaj

text:
We grew from ~0 to $500M ARR, adding $250M last year alone while being EBITDA profitable.

1,300-word post on every growth tactic that worked for us:

1. What got us from 0-$400M ARR in the US works in every country.
2. Retention and Monetisation Hacks.
3. Localization > Translation.
4. Experiment with $1M internal seed checks.
5. Pivoting to only AI content production unlocked 100% ARR growth.

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

1. Acquisition Playbook for 0-$10M ARR in any country in 6 months

We run a 90 sec video trailer of an audio drama as an Ad and ask users to download the app if they're interested in the rest of the story.

Our core insight after spending >$100M on acquisition is: If the clickthrough rate (CTR) for an ad goes from 2% to 2.25%, our customer acquisition cost (CAC) decreases by ~ 30%.

We remodelled our system around this insight and built an AI-first 2.25% CTR ad manufacturing machine that works in every country.

For every new country, we take our hit shows -> use LLMs to extract and most intriguing moments -> Write a 5-min script combining all the best parts. The first 60 seconds has to have a hook every 5 seconds and needs to end with a crazy cliffhanger to force a download mid-scroll.

If a marketing video is not hitting our benchmarks (2.5% CTR and 55% 3-second through-play), a creative director gets involved to change the hook or cliffhanger to get the numbers there.

AI lets us make 1,000 Ads per show, and in total we do ~17.5k Ads per month. When a business creating scales from 1k to 10k Ads, the normal thing is for CAC to skyrocket. But with what I just shared, we 7-8x'd our User Acquisition budget without increasing our CAC materially.

It took us 8 months to figure this out, but then the timeline from 0-$10M in every country got shorter and shorter:

US revenue grew to $25M in 19 months. (US is now 78% of total)
Germany to 21M in 11 months.
France to $10M in 3 months.

2. Retention and Monetisation Hacks.

We knew we wanted to create an audio entertainment platform, but there was no standard format. For the first 2-3 years, we tried 10 different formats before landing on the winner.

After we got it right with audio drama (8-12min chapters, written for mobile fiction, serialized, episodes have strong hooks and end on cliffhangers), avg daily streaming time went from ~25mins to 150+.

Audio drama made us realize that Pocket FM was creating a whole new medium. There was no playbook for anything that we were doing. Everything had to be thought & built from scratch.
This is what we did for each major bullet:

- Monetization: Users have some free daily minutes to listen; then it's pay per episode. We also added the option for users to unlock episodes by watching ads, which is doing extremely well. Ads scaled from zero to a ~$90M run rate in 12 months.
- Engagement & production: You don't become obsessed with an app you open once a week. To have users engage daily, we make the next episode free every day. Also helps them build the habit.
- Discovery. Huge problem because people consuming Pocket FM enter the app, tap the show, and lock the screen. We fixed it by doing "playlists" of episodes. Once users's free minutes on a show are done, we ask users if they want to pay. If they say no, we play a new show, one where they haven't used their free mins. And we stitch episodes of different shows together that way, creating natural discovery.

3. Localization > translation.

78% of our revenue is still concentrated in the US. Localisation is fixing this: You might write a show for a Spanish audience where language, jokes, folklore, have a certain flavor; if you merely translate the show for, say, a Norwegian audience, that color is lost and hurts the show in the Norway. Listeners would relate more if the show was written by a Norwegian.

That's why, instead of translating, we localize shows to different regions. We use AI to take the spine of stories and adapt their whole cultural layer to the other country.

The results: a US show that was localized for a German audience had 50% higher retention than the translated version.

Localization + our user acquisition playbook led to:
- $10M+ ARR in France within 3 months
- $21M+ ARR in Germany within 11 months.

And this expands writers' addressable market.
We get messages of writers thrilled to have revenue coming from the US, India, EU, LatAm, without them doing much incremental work.

4. Experiment.

We give $1M checks to new internal initiatives, and the team has 12-18 months to prove their thesis. If they prove it, we double down.
This is how Pocket Saga came about, our AI video microdrama app. It's an AI video equivalent of Pocket FM. Same shows and structure, but as a vertical 2-min mobile video series.

We launched it two months ago and it's at ~$15M ARR.

Pocket's broader thesis is to help creators tell their stories to as many people as possible. Start with audio drama -> multiple languages or localize to diff countries -> microdrama -> more formats like movies, TV shows, and games.

Best of all is that writers get revenue streams not only from countries they wouldn't have tapped into, but also from formats they wouldn't have thought possible.

5. Pivoting to only AI content production unlocked 100% ARR growth.

In mid-2024, we pivoted to only AI content production.
Our growth took a very direct hit. Pocket was already at $200M ARR, growing 50% YoY, and we flatlined for a whole semester.

Six months later, the business exploded.

After the switch, we went from ~25k hours of content produced per year to over 2.5M hours, which are also higher quality. Because AI orchestrates the writing and more data is fed into it, more blockbusters come out.
Over 90 titles have $1M+ in lifetime earnings and 13 crossed $10M.

Quality control is done with LLM as a judge, and LLMs are quite tough.
Results are very encouraging:
- 12-month revenue retention went from 44% to 76%.
- In the past year, we added $250M in net new ARR.
__________________________________

Pocket Entertainment (Pocket FM + Pocket Saga) has become the largest AI entertainment platform.

We have the largest storytelling catalog with 770,000 titles, 550k creators, and 5.5B hours of playtime with minute by minute retention & engagement data.  We are using all of this data to improve every aspect of our business.

Our Bet: In the next 3 years we will be able to produce Naruto-like series for $1000.

Netflix has to spend $17B to find 100 Blockbusters per year.
What happens when you can produce 1M high quality shows for $1B?

The streaming wars caused a $300B reallocation of market cap.
The AI entertainment wars may be a $1T+ reshuffling of market cap.

We are at a unique spot. Unlike other AI creator tools like Runway or Midjourney, we own both the supply and demand side of AI content.

We've attracted over 550,000 writers who are producing an annualized 2.5M hours of content every year. This pairs with 137B+ minutes streamed.

Because of this, growth is accelerating as we scale further.
We have multiple S-curves inflecting at the same time:

- AI produces better and more ads -> scale faster in new countries
- ⁠Writers + AI produce more shows -> more blockbusters
- ⁠Localisation -> more reach per blockbuster
- ⁠Audio to video format expansion -> larger TAM -> more creators

Every aspect of our business is designed to improve another, and everything is aligned so that the number of blockbusters continues to rise.

If you're interested in building at the intersection of ai, tech and entertainment, DM me.

Now @business  Bloomberg says Payward and hyperliquid are in advanced talks to bring HL perps to US traders through Bitnomial, its CFTC-regulated derivatives venue.

And yesterday, the Hyperliquid Policy Center filed an amicus brief in federal court defending the CFTC’s approval of regulated perpetual futures.

Suddenly, Jeff’s “housing all of finance” thesis looks a lot more concrete.

He has repeatedly described hyperliquid as financial infrastructure, even comparing it to AWS.

The interesting part isn’t that Nasdaq is investing in hyperliquid.

It isn’t.

The interesting part is that a company now sitting at the intersection of Nasdaq, tokenized equities, and regulated US derivatives is already building on Hyperliquid.

That is a very different story from “crypto exchange wants to enter the US.”

It starts looking like traditional finance is figuring out how to connect to the rails.

And if those rails eventually carry US-regulated markets too…

the exchange may have been the smallest part of the thesis all along.

It started with hypnotic music, cat videos, and countless remixes. But as it kept spreading, “Hajimi” gradually broke free from any single character or image.

Hajimi is more abstract, more memeable, and easier to spread across cultures.
